text:
Nativity of the Virgin Mary: from The Golden Legend by Jacobus da Voragine, 1527.
.
HERE FOLLOWETH THE NATIVITY OF OUR BLESSED LADY
.
THE GENEALOGY OF MARY
.
The nativity of the blessed and glorious Virgin Mary, of the lineage of Judah and of the royal kindred of David took her original beginning. Matthew and Luke describe not the generation of Mary but of Joseph, which was far from the conception of Christ.[1] But the custom of writing was of such ordinance that the generation of women is not showed but of the men. And verily the blessed Virgin descended of the lineage of David, and it is certain that Jesu Christ was born of this only Virgin.
It is certain that he came of the lineage of David and of Nathan, for David had two sons, Nathan and Solomon among all his other sons. And as John Damascene witnesseth that of Nathan descended Levy, and Levy engendered Melchion and Panthar, Panthar engendered Barpanthar, Barpanthar engendered Joachim, Joachim engendered the Virgin Mary, which was of the lineage of Solomon. For Nathan had a wife, of whom he engendered Jacob, and when Nathan was dead Melchion, which was son of Levy and brother of Panthar, wedded the wife of Nathan, mother of Jacob, and on her he engendered Eli, and so Jacob and Eli were brethren of one mother but not of one father. For Jacob was of the line of Solomon and Eli of the line of Nathan, and then Eli of the line of Nathan died without children, and Jacob his brother, which was of the line of Solomon, took a wife and engendered and raised the seed of his brother and engendered Joseph.
Joseph then by nature is son of Jacob by descent of Solomon. That is to wit, Joseph is the son of Jacob, and after the law he is son of Eli which descended of Nathan. For the son that was born, was by nature his that engendered him, and by the law he was son of him that was dead, like as it is said in the History Scholastic.
And Bede witnesseth in his chronicle that, when all the generations of the Hebrews and other strangers were kept in the most secret chests of the temple, Herod commanded them to be burnt, weening [hoping] thereby to make himself noble among the others. If the proofs of the lineages were failed [missing], he should make them believe that his lineage appertained [belonged] to them of Israel. And there were some that were called dominics, for because they were so nigh to Jesu Christ and were of Nazareth, and they had learned the order of generation of our Lord, a part of their grandsires' fathers, and a part by some books that they had in their houses and taught them forth as much as they might.
.
THE CHILDREN AND GRANDCHILDREN OF ST. ANNE
.
Joachim spoused Anne, which had a sister named Hismeria, and Hismeria had two daughters, named Elizabeth, and Elind. Elizabeth was mother to John Baptist, and Eliud engendered Eminen. And of Eminen came St. Servatius, whose body lieth in Maestricht, upon the river of the Meuse, in the bishopric of Liège. And Anne had three husbands, Joachim, Cleophas, and Salome; and of the first she had a daughter named Mary, the Mother of God, the which was given to Joseph in marriage, and she childed our Lord Jesu Christ.
And when Joachim was dead, she took Cleophas, the brother of Joseph, and had by him another daughter named Mary also, and she was married to Alpheus.
And Alpheus her husband had by her four sons, that was James the Less, Joseph the Just, otherwise named Barsabee, Simon, and Jude.
Then the second husband being dead, Anne married the third named Salome, and had by him another daughter which yet also was called Mary, and she was married to Zebedee. And this Mary had of Zebedee two sons, that is to wit, James the More [Greater], and John the Evangelist. And hereof be made these verses:
.
Anna solet dici tres concepisse Marias,
Quas genuere viri Joachim, Cleophas, Salomeque.
Has duxere viri Joseph, Alpheus, Zebedeus.
Prima parit Christum, Jacobum secunda minorem,
Et Joseph justum peperit cum Simone Judam,
Tertia majorem Jacobum volucremque Johannem.
.
[Anna is commonly said to have conceived three Marys,
Whom she conceived by the men Joachim, Cleophas, and Salome.
These three had for husbands Joseph, Alpheus, and Zebedee.
The first gave birth to Christ. The second gave birth to James the Less, And Joseph the Just, and Simon and Jude. The third gave birth to James the Greater and the winged John.]
.
But it is marvellous for to see how the blessed Virgin Mary might be cousin of Elizabeth as it is tofore said. It is certain that Elizabeth was Zachary's wife, which was of the lineage of Levi, and after the law each ought to wed a wife of his own lineage. And she was of the daughters of Aaron, as St. Luke witnesseth, and Anne was of Bethlehem, as St. Jerome saith, and was of the tribe of Judah. And then they of the line of Levi wedded wives of the line of Judah, so that the line royal and the line of the priests were always joined together by cousinage. So that as Bede saith: This cousinage might be made sith [after] the first time, and thus to be nourished from lineage to lineage, and thus should it be certain that the blessed Virgin Mary descended of the royal line, and had cousinage of the priests. And our blessed Lady was of both lineages, and so our Lord would that these two lineages should entresemble together for great mystery. For it appertaineth [is appropriate] that he should be born and offered for us, very God, and very king, and very priest, and should govern his true Christian men fighting in chivalry of this life, and to crown them after their victory, the which thing appeareth of the name of Christ, for Christ is as much to say as anointed. For in the old law there was none anointed but priests and kings, and we be said Christian men of Christ, and be called the lineage chosen of kings and priests.
But because it is said that the men took wives of their lineage only, that was because the distribution of the sorts [i.e., the distribution of land by lot] should not be confounded. For the tribe of Levy had not his sort with the other, and therefore might they well marry them with the women of that tribe or where they would, like as St. Jerome rehearseth in his prologue.
.
HOW ANNE AND JOACHIM BECAME MARY’S PARENTS
.
When he was a child he had a little book of the history of the nativity of the Virgin Mary, but as he remembered a long time after, he translated it by the prayer [request] of some persons, and found that Joachim, which was of Galilee of the city of Nazareth, espoused St. Anne of Bethlehem, and they were both just and without reproach or reprehension in the commandments of our Lord, and divided all their substance in three parts: that one part was for the temple, that other they gave to the poor and pilgrims, and the third was for themselves and their meiny [household] to live with.
.
Joachim is Expelled from the Temple
.
And thus lived twenty years in marriage without having any lineage. And then they avowed to our Lord that if he sent to them any lineage they should give it to him, for to serve him. For which thing they went every year into Jerusalem in three principal feasts, so that in the feast of Encenia, that was the dedication of the temple, then Joachim went unto Jerusalem with his kindred, and came to the altar with the others and would have offered his offering. And when the priest saw him, he put him apart by great despite, and reproved him because he came to the altar of God, and said to him that it was convenable that a man cursed in the faith should not offer to our Lord, ne he that was barren should be among them that had fruit, as he that had none to the increase of the people of God.
.
He Stays with his Shepherds
.
And then Joachim, all confused for this thing, durst not go home for shame, because they of his lineage and his neighbours which had heard it should not reprove him. And then he went to his herdmen, and was there long.
.
The Annunciation to Joachim
.
And then the angel appeared to him only, and comforted him with great clearness, and said to him that he should not doubt [fear] ne be afraid of his vision, and said:
“I am the angel of our Lord sent to thee for to denounce [announce] to thee that thy prayers have availed thee and been heard, and thy alms be mounted tofore our Lord. I have seen thy shame and heard the reproach. That thou art barren is to thee no reproach by right, and God is venger of sin and not of nature. And when he closeth the belly or womb, he worketh so that he openeth it after, more marvellously. And the fruit that shall be born shall not be seen to come forth by lechery, but that it be known that it is of the gift of God.
“The first mother of your people was Sara, and she was barren unto the ninetieth year, and had only Isaac, to whom the benediction of all people was promised. And was not Rachel long barren? And yet had she not after [afterwards] Joseph, that held all the seigniory [lordship] of Egypt? Which was more strong than Samson, and more holy than Samuel? And yet were their mothers barren. Thus mayst thou believe by reason and by ensample that the childings long abiden [births long awaited] be wont to be more marvellous.
“And therefore Anne thy wife shall have a daughter, and thou shalt call her Mary, and she, as ye have avowed [promised], shall be from her infancy sacred unto our Lord, and shall be full of the Holy Ghost sith [after] the time that she shall depart from the womb of her mother, and she shall dwell in the temple of our Lord, and not without, among the other people, because that none evil thing shall be had in suspicion of her, and right as she shall be born of a barren mother, so shall be born of her marvellously the son of a right high Lord. Of whom the name shall be Jesus, and by him shall health be given to all the people.
“And I give to thee the sign, that when thou shalt come to the golden gate at Jerusalem, thou shalt meet there Anne thy wife, which is much amoved of thy long tarrying, and shall have joy of thy coming.”
.
The Annunciation to Anne
.
And then the angel, when he had said this, he departed from him. And as when Anne wept bitterly and wist not whither her husband was gone, the same angel appeared to her, and said all that he had said to her husband, and gave to her for a sign that she should go into Jerusalem, to the golden gate, and there she should meet with her husband which was returned. And thus by the commandment of the angel they met, and were firm of the lineage promised, and glad for to see each other, and honoured our Lord and returned home, abiding joyously the promise divine.
.
MARY’S BIRTH AND CHILDHOOD
.
And Anne conceived and brought forth a daughter, and named her Mary.
And then when she had accomplished the time of three years, and had left sucking, they brought her to the temple with offerings. And there was about the temple, after the fifteen psalms of degrees, fifteen steps or grees [steps] to ascend up to the temple, because the temple was high set. And no body might go to the altar of sacrifices that was without, but by the degrees. And then our Lady was set on the lowest step, and mounted up without any help as she had been of perfect age, and when they had performed their offering, they left their daughter in the temple with the other virgins, and they returned into their place.
And the Virgin Mary profited every day in all holiness, and was visited daily of angels, and had every day divine visions.
Jerome saith in an epistle to Chromatius and to Heliodorus that the blessed Virgin Mary had ordained this custom to herself that, from the morning unto the hour of tierce [from 9 a.m. till noon], she was in orison and prayer, and from tierce unto nones [noon to 3 p.m.] she entended to her work, and from nones she ceased not to pray, till that the angel came and gave to her meat [food].
.
THE MIRACLE OF JOSEPH’S ROD
.
And in the fourteenth year of her age, the bishop commanded in common that the virgins that were instituted in the temple, and had accomplished the time of age, should return to their houses and should after the law be married. All the others obeyed his commandment, but Mary answered that she might not do so because her father and mother had given her all to the service of our Lord. And then the bishop was much angry because he durst not make her to break her avow against the scripture, that saith: Avow ye vows and yield them to God.[2] And he durst not break the custom of the people.
And then came a feast of the Jews, and he called all the ancient Jews to council, and showed to them this thing. And this was all their sentence: That in a thing so doubtable, that counsel shall be asked of our Lord. And then went they all to prayer, and the bishop, that was gone to ask counsel of our Lord.
Anon came a voice out of the oracle and said that, all they that were of the house of David that were convenable [eligible] to be married and had no wife, that each of them should bring a rod to the altar, and his rod that flourished, and, after the saying of Isaiah,[3] the Holy Ghost sit in the form of a dove on it, he should be the man that should be desponsate [espoused] and married to the Virgin Mary.
And Joseph, of the house of David, was there among the others, and him seemed to be a thing unconvenable [inappropriate], a man of so old age as he was to have so tender a maid, and whereas others brought forth their rods he hid his. And when nothing appeared according to the voice of God, the bishop ordained for to ask counsel again of our Lord. And he answered that, he only that should espouse the virgin had not brought forth his rod.
And then Joseph by the commandment of the bishop brought forth his rod, and anon it flowered, and a dove descended from heaven thereupon, so that it was clearly the advice of every man that he should have the virgin. And then he espoused the Virgin Mary, and returned into his city of Bethlehem for to ordain his meiny and his house, and for to fetch such things as were necessary. And the Virgin Mary returned unto the house of her father with seven virgins, her fellows of her age, which had seen the demonstrance of the miracle.
And in those days the angel of our Lord appeared to the Virgin praying, and showed to her how the Son of God should be born of her.
.
THE DATE OF MARY’S NATIVITY
.
And the day of the nativity was not known in long time of good Christian men, and as master John Beleth saith that, it happed that a man of good contemplation every year in the sixth ides of September [September 8] was in prayer, and he heard a company of angels that made great solemnity. And then he required [asked] devoutly that he might have knowledge wherefore every year only on that day he heard such solemnity and not on other days. And then he had a divine answer that, on that day the blessed Virgin Mary was born into this world, and that he should do it to be known to the men of holy church, so that they should be concordable to the heavenly court in hallowing this solemnity. And when he had told this to the sovereign bishop the pope, and to the others, and had been in fastings, in prayers, and sought in scriptures and witnesses of old writings, they established this day of the nativity of the glorious Virgin to be hallowed generally of all Christian men.
.
THE OCTAVE OF MARY’S NATIVITY
.
But the utas [the octave][4] sometime was not hallowed ne kept. But Innocent the fourth, of the nation of Genoa, ordained and instituted the said utas to be observed. And the cause was this:
After the death of Pope Gregory, anon the citizens of Rome enclosed all the cardinals in the conclave because they should purvey lightly for the church, but they might not accord in many days, but suffered of the Romans much sorrow. Then avowed they to the Queen of Heaven that if they might go quiet from thence they should establish to hallow the octaves of the nativity which they had long negligently left. And they then by one accord chose Celestin, and were delivered, and accomplished then their avow by Innocent, for Celestin lived but a little time, and therefore it might not be accomplished by him.
.
THE THREE NATIVITY FEASTS
.
And it is to wit that the church halloweth three nativities, the nativity of our Lord, the nativity of the blessed Virgin Mary, and the nativity of St. John Baptist. And these three signify three nativities spiritual, for we be born again with St. John Baptist in the water of baptism, and with Mary in penance, and with our Lord Jesu Christ in glory. And it behoveth that nativity of baptism go tofore contrition, and that of joy also. For the two by reason have vigils,[5] but because that penance is accounted for vigil, therefore that of our Lady behoveth no vigil, but they have all utas, for all haste them unto the eighth resurrection.
.
MIRACLES OF THE VIRGIN
.
Our Lady’s Knight
.
There was a knight much noble and devout unto our Lady which went to a tourneying, and he found a monastery in his way which was of the Virgin Mary, and entered into it for to hear mass, and there were masses one after another, and for the honour of our Lady he would leave none but that he heard them all. And when he issued out of the monastery he hasted him appertly [out in public]. And they that returned from the tourney met him, and said to him that he had ridden right nobly. And they that hated him affirmed the same, and all they together cried that he had right nobly tourneyed, and some went to him and said that he had taken them [captured them in the course of the tournament]. Then he, that was wise, avised him [Then he, being wise, realized] that the courteous Virgin and Queen had so courteously honoured him, and recounted all that was happened, and then returned he to the monastery, and ever after abode in the service of our Lord, the son of the blessed Virgin.
The Devout Bishop
.
There was a bishop which had [held] the blessed Virgin Mary in sovereign honour and devotion, and there he saw the virgin of all virgins, which came to meet him, and began to lead him by sovereign honour to the church that he went to, and two maidens of the company went tofore singing and saying these verses:
Cantemus domino, sociæ, cantemus honorem,
Dulcis amor Christi resonet ore pio.
That is to say, “Sing we fellows to our Lord, sing we honour. Sing we with a voice debonair [mild] that sweet love which ought to please him.” And that other company of virgins sang and rehearsed again the same. Then the two first singers began to sing this that followeth:
Primus ad ima ruit magna de luce superbus,
Sic homo cum tumult, primus ad ima ruit.
That is to say, “The first pride fell low from great light. So the first man, for his eating of the apple, fell low also.” And so brought they to the church with procession the said bishop, and the two tofore began alway, and the others followed.
.
The Widow Who Took Jesus Hostage
.
There was a widow whose husband was dead, and had a son whom she loved tenderly, and that son was taken with [by] enemies and put in prison fast bound. And when she heard thereof, she wept without comfort, and prayed unto our blessed Lady with right devout prayers that she would deliver her son, and at the last she saw that her prayers availed her not, and entered then into the church whereas the image of our Lady was carved, and stood tofore the image and areasoned it in this manner, saying: O blessed Virgin, I have prayed oft thee for my son that thou shouldst deliver him, and thou hast not helped me, his wretched mother; and I pray also thy son to help me and yet I feel no fruit. And therefore like as my son is taken from me so shall I take away thine, and set him in prison in hostage for mine.
And in this saying she approached near and took away from the image the child that she held in her lap, and wrapped it in clean clothes and shut it in her chest, and locked it fast right diligently, and was right joyful that she had so good hostage for her son, and kept it much diligently.
And the night following, the blessed Virgin Mary came to the son of the same widow, and opened to him the door of the prison, and commanded him to go thence, and said to him: Son, say to thy mother that she yield to me again my son sith [since] I have delivered her son.
And he issued [went out] and came to his mother, and told to her how our blessed Lady had delivered him, and she was joyful, and took the child and came to the church and delivered him to our Lady, saying: Lady I thank you, for ye have delivered to me my son, and here I deliver to you yours again, for I confess that I have mine.
.
The Virgin Mary Saves a Thief
.
There was a thief that often stole, but he had always great devotion to the Virgin Mary, and saluted her oft. It was so that on a time he was taken and judged to be hanged. And when he was hanged the blessed Virgin sustained and hanged him up with her hands three days that he died not ne had no hurt, and they that hanged him passed by adventure thereby, and found him living and of glad cheer. And then they supposed that the cord had not been well strained, and would have slain him with a sword, and have cut his throat, but our blessed Lady set on her hand tofore the strokes so that they might not slay him ne grieve him.
And then knew they, by that he told to them, that the blessed Mother of God helped him, and then they marvelled, and took him off and let him go, in the honour of the Virgin Mary, and then he went and entered into a monastery, and was in the service of the Mother of God as long as he lived.
.
A Marriage is Prevented
.
There was a clerk that loved much the blessed Nativity Virgin, and said his hours [prayers] every day ententively. And when his father and mother were dead, they had none other heir so that he had all the heritage, and then he was constrained of his friends that he should take a wife and govern his own heritage.
And on a day it happed that they entended to hold the feast of his marriage, and as he was going to the wedding he came to a church, and he remembered of the service of our blessed Lady, and entered in and began to say his hours. And the blessed Virgin Mary appeared to him and spake to him a little cruelly: O fool and unhappy [unfortunate], why hast thou left me that am thy spouse and thy friend, and lovest another woman tofore me?
Then he, being moved, returned to his fellows and feigned all, and left to accomplish the sacrament of marriage. And when midnight came he left all and fled out of the house, and entered into a monastery and there served the Mother of God.
.
The Priest Who Said Mary’s Mass Only
.
There was a priest of a parish, which was of honest and good life, and could say no mass but mass of our Lady, the which he sang devoutly in the honour of her, wherefore he was accused tofore the bishop, and was anon called tofore him. And the priest confessed that he could say none other mass, wherefore the bishop reproved him sore as unconning [ignorant] and an idiot, and suspended him of his mass, that he should no more sing none from then forthon.
And then our blessed Lady appeared to the bishop and blamed him much because he had so entreated her chaplain, and said to him that he should die within thirty days if he re-established him not again to his office accustomed. Then the bishop was afeard, and sent for the priest and prayed him of forgiveness, and bade him that he should not sing but of our Lady.
.
The Vain and Riotous Student
.
There was a clerk which was vain and riotous, but always he loved much our Lady, the Mother of God, and said every day his hours. And he saw on a night a vision that, he was in judgment tofore our Lord, and our Lord said to them that were there: What judgment shall we do of this clerk? devise ye it for I have long suffered him, and see no sign yet of amendment. Then our Lord gave upon him sentence of damnation, and all they approved it.
Then arose the blessed Virgin and said to her son: I pray thee, debonair son, of thy mercy for this man, so that thou assuage [soften] upon him the sentence of damnation, and that he may live yet, by the grace of me, which is condemned to death by his merits.
And our Lord said to her: I deliver him at thy request for to know if I shall see his correction.
Then our Lady turned her toward him and said: Go, and sin no more lest it happen worse to thee. Then he awoke, and changed his life, and entered into religion, and finished his life in good works...

text:
Ibn Khaldun interrogates the fiscal collapse of resource dependent states as Saudi Arabia faces a severe economic crisis:

The red lines on the tactical display traced the maritime blockades from the southern straits straight up to the Persian Gulf, but Tariq was looking at a ledger that showed zero litres leaving the export terminals for the third consecutive week. He rubbed his eyes, staring at the projected fiscal deficit that swallowed three quarters of the sovereign reserves in a single quarter of 2026.

The old man sitting across the glass table, dressed in the dark wool garments of a fourteenth century jurist, didn't look at the glowing screens at all. He watched the subtle tremor in the hands of Tariq.

You look at the closed shipping lanes as if they're the disease, Ibn Khaldun said, his voice carrying the dry cadence of energy born of reflection. They're merely the fever breaking.

Tariq set his pen down, the plastic clattering against the glass. 47,000,000 litres a day are shut in at the eastern fields alone, and the tankers are turning back under missile fire. The state can't survive six months without petroleum revenue. You talk of fevers, but the patient is bleeding out.

A patient who lives entirely on foreign blood does not bleed when a vein is cut, Ibn Khaldun replied softly. He simply ceases to exist because he never learned to manufacture his own vitality. You call this a supply crisis. It's a structural failure of extraction.

Tariq shook his head, leaning forward. You don't understand modern statecraft. We've built desalination plants, motorways, and universities on the back of oil rents. We bypassed the need for internal taxation because the earth provided a surplus that allowed the government to nourish the populace without demanding tribute. That's not a failure. That's efficiency.

It's not efficiency, the old man said, tracing a finger along the polished edge of the table. It's an artificial slumber. When a state derives its wealth from beneath the ground rather than from the labour and enterprise of its people, the bond between ruler and subject changes its nature. In the days of the caliphates, when we collected the land tax and the tithe, the treasury grew in proportion to the cultivator's prosperity. If the harvest failed, the ruler felt the pinch immediately, and so he invested in irrigation, security, and justice. But when the wealth flows from an external pipe that requires no human toil to fill, the ruler no longer depends on the population. And when the ruler does not depend on the population, he owes them nothing.

And they owe us nothing, Tariq muttered. That was the social contract. We provide housing, electricity, and fuel subsidies. In exchange, the political order remains stable.

A contract written in sand and crude oil, Ibn Khaldun observed, leaning back. Stability purchased through distribution isn't stability at all. It's a rentier bargain that rots the social cohesion of the nation. When people contribute nothing to the treasury through their own productive enterprise, they possess no stake in the preservation of the state beyond the daily stipend. When the stipend stops because a missile strikes a pipeline, what remains of their loyalty? Nothing. A loyalty bought with oil is rented, not owned.

Tariq stared at the map where red warning icons blinked across every export terminal. We can institute emergency taxes. We can levy value added tax across the board and introduce corporate income levies to replace the oil revenue.

You can decree it on paper, Ibn Khaldun said, smiling faintly. But you can't collect it. Taxation requires an institutional apparatus rooted in mutual trust and a populace accustomed to productive trade. For decades, your government taught your citizens that money falls from the sky like rain. Why should a merchant pay a tax to a state that he views merely as a failing dispenser of charity? To extract revenue from a population, the state must offer protection, justice, and economic freedom in return. If you have spent generations treating your people as dependents rather than taxpayers, you will find they view your tax collectors not as partners in governance, but as extortionists.

The reserves will sustain us while we build new pipelines through the empty quarters to the southern coast, Tariq argued, though his voice lacked conviction. We can divert the flow past the blockades.

You're still looking for a plumbing solution to a political decay, Ibn Khaldun said, shaking his head. You believe that if you fix the pipe, the life returns. But the life was never in the pipe. A state that rests entirely on a single rentier resource passes through cycles just like a dynasty of old. It rises on the strength of initial cohesion, reaches its zenith of luxurious expansion when the rents flow without limit, and then decays into extravagance and dependence. When the external rent is severed, the decay is exposed all at once. You can't rebuild a productive economy in the middle of a fiscal winter when no one knows how to produce anything except the extraction of a liquid that no longer moves.

Tariq looked down at the financial projections for the coming year, where the numbers plunged toward an absolute floor. What would you do if you sat in my chair today?

I would stop trying to revive the old extraction, Ibn Khaldun said quietly. I would look at the ruins of the rentier model and recognize that the collapse of the oil export is the only shock severe enough to force your society to rediscover the value of human labour, domestic enterprise, and genuine taxation. A state only becomes real when its rulers realize they can't survive without the productive energy of their own people. Until then, you are merely a pipeline manager waiting for the pressure to return.

---

Ibn Khaldun (1332-1406) was an Arab historian and sociologist whose masterpiece, the Muqaddimah, pioneered historiography, economics, and social science. He's best known for introducing the concept of social cohesion to explain the rise and fall of civilisations.

My article on AI
AI: A Step in Evolutionary Development or Merely a AI: A Step in Evolutionary Development or Merely a New Technology?

Today’s (10 Sept 2026) Mumbai edition of the Times of India featured two intriguing items concerning Artificial Intelligence. The first involved an AI safety researcher warning that developers in leading labs fear advanced systems could pose an existential threat before the end of the decade. The second reported ambitious claims that AI systems could tackle major mathematical milestones, such as the Millennium Prize Problems.

These two narratives illustrate diametrically opposed visions for humanity’s future. Before addressing them, one must keep in mind that roughly 99.9% of all species that have ever lived on Earth are now extinct. There is no biological reason to assume that humanity is exempt from this rule. Charles Darwin never suggested that evolution culminates with human beings; he viewed humanity not as nature's ultimate product, but merely as one branch among countless others.
The formal discipline of Artificial Intelligence emerged after British mathematician Alan Turing published his seminal paper, "Computing Machinery and Intelligence," in 1950. In 1955, John McCarthy coined the term "Artificial Intelligence" in his proposal for the 1956 Dartmouth Summer Research Project. McCarthy also created the Lisp programming language in 1958. Practical robotics followed swiftly: General Motors introduced the first industrial robot, Unimate, to its assembly line in 1961 to handle hazardous die-castings and spot welding. In 1979, the American Association for Artificial Intelligence was founded; it has since been renamed the Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AAAI).
Data aggregated by Our World in Data tracks how modern AI benchmarks against human performance across several domains. Between 2010 and 2024, AI systems reached or exceeded human parity in six key capabilities: handwriting recognition, speech recognition, image recognition, reading comprehension, language understanding, and predictive reasoning.
AI has steadily automated routine decision-making across numerous sectors. Algorithms now routinely manage passenger airline ticketing, loan eligibility evaluations, and initial resume screenings. Recommendation engines, such as YouTube's, dictate viewer feeds based on behavioral history. In healthcare, computer vision aids diagnostic imaging, while robotic platforms assist surgeons with high-precision procedures.
Beyond data processing, machine learning has begun to assist pure mathematics. Rather than merely calculating known values, systems are beginning to assist in formulating novel conjectures. Projects like the Ramanujan Machine uncover algorithmic patterns and propose continued-fraction conjectures for fundamental constants, which human mathematicians subsequently formalize and prove. When AI systems map complex logical spaces, they inevitably highlight unproven edge cases and structural anomalies, generating new avenues for mathematical research.
Monopolies and the Enclosure of AI Research
A major barrier to realizing AI's potential is the paywall infrastructure maintained by commercial academic publishers. Media theorist Howard Besser observed that just as economic forces drive the gentrification of cities and erode physical public spaces, commercial interests have enclosed digital information spaces. Economists Michele Boldrin and David K. Levine examined this phenomenon in Against Intellectual Monopoly, arguing that broad IP protections frequently hinder innovation rather than foster it.
This issue was central to Google LLC v. Oracle America, Inc., regarding copyright enforcement on Application Programming Interfaces (APIs). In an amici curiae brief, prominent computer scientists emphasized that open interfaces are fundamental to computational progress:

"Excluding APIs from copyright protection has been essential to the development of modern computers and the Internet. For example, the widespread availability of diverse, cheap, and customizable personal computers owes its existence to the lack of copyright on the specification for IBM’s Basic Input/Output System (BIOS) for the PC."
If knowledge silos and aggressive IP claims restrict access to training architectures, development will consolidate within a handful of corporate monopolies.
Evolution on Earth began approximately 3.8 billion years ago, progressing across biological substrates and now extending into technological ones. While alarms over imminent extinction may often carry rhetorical hyperbole, ungoverned deployment of autonomous systems remains a genuine risk. Isaac Asimov’s classic "Three Laws of Robotics" offer a foundational philosophical reference for safety and human alignment:

The  First Law: A robot may not injure a human being or, through inaction, allow a human being to come to harm.
The  Second Law: A robot must obey the orders given it by human beings,  except where such orders would conflict with the First Law.
The  Third Law: A robot must protect its own existence, as long as such protection does not conflict with the First or Second Law.

To reflect on the twilight of our biological primacy, Arthur C. Clarke’s Childhood’s End provides a haunting portrait of species-level transition:
"There was nothing left of Earth. They had gone over it like a light that illuminates and consumes. They had left nothing behind them, and they were gone.
...
Jan Rodricks stood alone upon the dying planet... Earth was no longer his home, nor the home of man. It was only the launching pad from which humanity had leapt into the stars."

text:
Tariffs May Raise US Drug Prices; Manufacturing Shift Not Easy: Lupin Global CFO Ramesh Swaminathan

The Tariff Threat
Proposed 100–200% US tariffs on generic drugs could push up medicine prices for US patients or lead to shortages if drugmakers cannot absorb higher costs

In August, US President Donald Trump announced phased tariff plan on generic drugs — imports facing no tariff for two years from August 1, 2026

Duty will rise to 100% in August 2028 and 200% in August 2029 — seeking to push drugmakers to shift production to US

Lupin Executive Director, Global CFO & Head of API Plus SBU Ramesh Swaminathan: "The day President Trump actually comes out with tariffs on generics in US, the cost of medicine will go up"

Why US Manufacturing Shift is Hard
Shifting generic drug production to US would not be commercially viable without firm commitments on volumes and prices and possible government subsidies

"Unless there are guarantees in place, nobody will actually do this"

Drugmakers would initially seek to pass on additional costs but intense competition in commoditised generics could limit their pricing power

Some manufacturers could be forced to stop production leading to shortages — "Either way, the consumer will be hurt"

Lupin's Positioning
Lupin not currently affected by latest Section 232 tariffs — up to 100% on imported patented pharma and APIs — since its products sold in US are manufactured locally

Has limited exposure to brande drugs in the US

Company would continue to invest in Somerset and Coral Springs manufacturing units to manufacture products feasible from an economic point of view

GLP-1 Opportunity
Lupin sees significant long-term potential in GLP-1 segment despite signs of softer demand following semaglutide's patent expiry

Strong presence in diabetes and cardiovascular therapies makes it a key focus category

Partnered with Zydus Lifesciences to market generic semaglutide in domestic market

Also bringing Bofanglutide — a fortnightly GLP-1 injection — through a partnership with a Chinese company

Moving Up the Value Chain
Company simultaneously seeking to move up value chain through complex generics, specialty medicines and biosimilars

"Our focus area is really more complex stuff, a bit of biosimilars, and then looking at specialty the way we are doing"

Moving up the value chain requires overcoming cost and scale disadvantage against China — domestic manufacturers face logistics costs 14–15% higher and electricity more expensive than in China

China's Competitive Edge & India's Gap
China has already moved beyond APIs and generics into innovative drugs and biotechnology

Around 50% of Investigational New Drug (IND) filings are coming from China

For domestic industry, transition into biologics, biosimilars, antibody-drug conjugates, gene therapy and CAR-T remains a "long way off"

"India is nowhere in the picture. Our continued focus on re-engineering existing small-molecule drugs will not move the needle and will leave companies with wafer-thin margins"

China-plus-one strategy could offer opportunity but industry needs to move quickly to capitalise

Russians are not perfect. But they are one of the bravest people on the planet. They are proud of their national-cultural identity. Russia boasts of not only huge territory but also the biggest reserve of natural resources.

Despite all his flaws, Prez Putin has provided stability/continuity in Russia & most of former Soviet territories at a critical time. There is need for transformation in not only Russia but entire world.

Western democracies, despite their exceptional strengths, are grappling with their own share of weaknesses. They derive their strengths from their unique journey as a civilisation. It is grossly unfair/naive to expect entire world to be their replica.

Responsible statecraft, in a globalised world, must acknowledge unique identity of each state/civilisation to harness their role in shaping collective destiny of human race. 

From New Delhi, Russia has always appeared benign &friendly. It never came to colonise India on line of Portuguese, Dutch, French, English & other Westerners. It never indulged in divide & rule to fracture this subcontinent to pit Islamists/Pakistan against India through a variety of covert strategies.

While there is no emotion or sentiment in geopolitics, Russia always stood by India as a friend. There is huge goodwill for Indian culture/people in Russia & even China.

Yet realism in statecraft requires both India& Russia to be careful towards their more formidable neighbour China. Convergence of strategic interests between India & Russia appears unparalleled.

Throughout 20th Century, Western military-security establishments kept backing Pakistan with sole agenda of keeping one fourth of human race on this subcontinent in perpetual state of turmoil, conflict& underdevelopment. This appeared part of their strategy of global domination. Military-Mullah nexus of Pakistan & their ideological-crime partners in India appeared a dependable proxy to bleed this region.

Today world is different. Innate goodness of Western cultural, societal humanist values or freedom, innovation or higher, but not optimal, access to equality of opportunity offered by their systems are genuinely admirable. But they are neither perfect nor worthy of total emulation.

Despite shift in larger approach of the West, section of racist/piratic elements amidst them are suspected to be persisting with their agenda to subvert our democracy, governance& overall all stability/security of this region. We have our own 

We have not been able to harness such convergence for mutual gains & a better world, largely due to lack of adequate innovation in governance, education system & high end research not only in realms of technology but also human behaviour, governance, statecraft & different shades of warfare.

Whole world needs transition for a better shared future of human race. A degree of strategic equilibrium among nations, people & cultures is critical. An element of competition & even conflict shall be part of the process.

What we need is a far more responsible statecraft & a globalised world. Western democratic model or Chinese or Russian model and Indian ones, on their own,  appear fairly deficient in this direction. Statesmanship requires highest degree of sagely attributes.

Statecraft requires unique resilience. Once a large sections of Indians, esp US based/educated, were calling for total allegiance to USA. In discussions/conference I often used to be in singular minority under pain to insist upon our continued goodwill towards Russia for sake of our credibility as a state as well as convergence of strategic interests.

India as a civilisation has suffered enormously due to strategic myopia. We have not been & cannot afford to be parochial/hateful. But need exceptional pragmatism & all shades of raw national power to sustain, protect, uphold & promote our humanist civilisational ethos.

India needs integrity, courage, patriotism & humanism in its political- intellectual space. Rest will follow. @narendramodi

Gen. Kahinda Otafiire: A life shaped by the liberation struggle 

RO/00014 Gen. Kahinda Otafiire is among the living veterans whose service remains part of Uganda’s liberation history.

He joined the National Resistance Army during the 1981–1986 bush war and rose to important political responsibilities, serving as Chief Political Commissar and later National Political Commissar. His work involved political education, mobilisation and strengthening discipline within the movement.

His contribution was not confined to the battlefield. He was also involved in the administration of areas under NRA control as the struggle progressed towards Kampala in 1986.

As Uganda honours the men and women who gave their lives during the liberation struggle, the story of Gen. Otafiire offers a reminder of the living veterans who witnessed and helped shape that defining chapter of the country’s history.

text:
Sport

Inside the NFL’s big money plan to conquer Australia

This week’s NFL extravaganza in Melbourne was 16 years in the making, and is all about establishing the next big audience for the US football code.

Sep 11, 2026

By Patrick Durkin

More than 20 million Americans are expected to watch Friday’s historic National Football League clash in Melbourne between the Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers.

For many Americans, it will be their first time properly laying eyes on Australian soil, the NFL says.

More than 2 million Australians are also expected to be watching, as well as the almost 100,000 fans inside the Melbourne Cricket Ground.

“There’s already a massive fan base here which grows every year, and there’s a lot of similarities between the AFL and NRL with the NFL, so I think this is just the tipping point to NFL becoming insanely more popular,” says Isabelle Van Coevorden, head of global markets for the Seattle Seahawks.

But this game was no one-off accident. Visit Victoria chief executive Brendan McClements says conversations began back in 2011, and Sydney was the front-runner when former NSW premier Mike Baird reportedly offered $20 million in 2015 to host the 49ers at Accor Stadium. Victoria has not disclosed what it paid but reports suggest it is up to $45 million for the three-game deal.

When the NFL set up an office is Sydney that city became the short-priced favourite to host a game. But Melbourne, Perth, Tokyo and Seoul were also in the running. The interested parties made final presentations just before Christmas in 2023 and came together at the NFL’s games at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London in 2024, before the final announcement at the New Orleans Super Bowl in February 2025.

McClements says the mood really changed in 2024, as NFL research showed strong growth in the game’s popularity in Australia, but NFL commissioner Roger Goodell had one final reservation.

“He was really testing us on the idea that 100,000 people could possibly turn up for a sports game on a Friday morning, we had to convince him of how sports mad Victorians really are,” he tells The Australian Financial Review.

“It’s just a juggernaut. Once they announced the game, we started to really understand the size, scale and power of the NFL.”

The NFL, which generates $US23 billion ($31.8 billion) in revenue each year compared with the AFL’s $1.2 billion a year, have a multi-year plan to take the Australian sporting market by storm, backed by research shared exclusively with the Financial Review.

“We measure fandom across the world in our 12 priority markets of which Australia is one,” says Brett Gosper, the NFL’s head of Europe and Asia-Pacific. Gosper, originally from Melbourne, was previously the chief executive of World Rugby and is son of the late International Olympic Committee vice president Kevan Gosper.

“This market has a high percentage of sports fans per population compared to other markets. We’ve seen a massive uptick in this country that would probably blow away any market, anywhere. We’ve got 8.8 million fans here, self-declared, from our annual surveys. (AFR)

We would be fine if we stopped buying Canadian Natural Gas or Crude however Canada would go bankrupt in a few months. We might have short term higher prices but it wouldn’t affect the U.S. like it would Canada. We export more than we import. 

“If the U.S. completely halted energy trade with Canada, the missing 5% of natural gas would be handled entirely by expanding domestic U.S. production and capping exports, while the missing 20–25% of crude oil would be sourced from a mix of domestic drilling and maritime imports from Latin America and the Middle East.
Because Canada sends its energy directly via cross-border pipelines, replacing it would trigger immediate logistical friction, higher transportation costs, and a massive re-routing of global shipping lanes. [1]

Here is exactly how the U.S. would obtain the missing resources:

1. Replacing the Missing Natural Gas (5% of Total Use)
Because Canada supplies nearly 100% of U.S. natural gas imports, losing this supply means losing roughly 8 to 9 billion cubic feet per day (Bcf/d). However, the U.S. is already the world's largest natural gas producer and a massive EXPORTER. The shortage would be solved domestically: [1, 2, 3, 4]
•Redirecting U.S. LNG Exports: The U.S. currently exports a staggering 17+ Bcf/d of Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) to Europe and Asia. If a crisis hit, the U.S. government could restrict or redirect a portion of these ocean-bound exports to stay within domestic markets. [1]
•Surging Domestic Production: U.S. marketed natural gas production is on track to hit a record-breaking 122.5 Bcf/d. The Permian Basin in Texas and New Mexico is generating massive amounts of "associated gas" alongside oil extraction. With modest infrastructure adjustments, domestic shale could easily bridge the 5% gap. [1]

2. Replacing the Missing Crude Oil (20–25% of Refinery Supply)
Replacing Canada's 4 million barrels per day (bpd) of crude oil is a much steeper mountain to climb. U.S. refineries specifically need heavy, sour crude, which domestic fracking fields do not yield in large quantities. The U.S. would have to pivot to a combination of international waterborne suppliers and increased domestic drilling: [1, 2]
•Latin American Imports (Brazil, Guyana, Colombia): According to energy analysts tracking recent tariff shocks, U.S. Gulf Coast refineries are already looking to aggressively scale up heavy and medium crude imports from Anas Alhajji / Energy Outlook Advisors:
◦Guyana: One of the fastest-growing oil producers in the world.
◦Brazil: Offers vast offshore reserves of medium-to-heavy crude grades.
•The Venezuelan Long-Game: The U.S. recently brokered major energy agreements granting long-term field concessions to North American companies. While Venezuela currently only produces around 1.25 million bpd, intense investment is geared toward aggressively ramping this up over the next few years to absorb Canadian market share. [1]
•The Middle East (Saudi Arabia & Iraq): The U.S. would likely be forced to buy more heavy crude from Iraq and Saudi Arabia via oil tankers. Saudi Arabia maintains the world's largest "spare capacity" (the ability to turn on millions of barrels of production almost overnight).  [1, 2]
•Unlocking More Domestic Crude: U.S. crude production is already at an all-time historic high of 13.8 million bpd. Higher oil prices (which currently average over $84/b for West Texas Intermediate) naturally incentivize American drilling companies to ramp up production even further

text:
Where were you on 9/11?

At the time, I was sleeping on a mattress in my 350 dollar a month studio apartment on Sycamore Avenue, just off Hollywood Boulevard. I was so broke back then that I couldn't even afford to pay attention.

I was sleeping late, as the night before I had worked my usual shift as a doorman at a bar/nightclub down in Brentwood.

The phone ringing wrenched me awake. It was my Swedish friend Fredrik.

'What's happening?' I asked him on the back of a yawn.

'Are you watching this?'

'Watching what? I was sleeping.'

'Turn on the TV! We're under attack!'

Will never forget him saying 'We're', despite being from Sweden.  

Fredrik, to let you understand, was a 6'6" former professional kickboxer who had moved to Hollywood from Japan to carve out a career in movies. In the meantime, he made his way working as a bodyguard for various celebrities. 

I had missed the first tower in NYC being struck, but I watched the second being hit live on the news. Awful.

Hollywood in the hours and days afterwards was a ghost town. People were scared, I mean really scared, and also confused.

But not all.

I remember the older Mexican guy who manned the parking garage down the street, where I parked my chevy at the time. We use to talk politics whenever we passed.

The following day he was at the entrance of the parking garage as usual, as I headed for my car. As I approached he said in a low voice: 'You see what happens, señor? You see what happens when you go around the world killing people?'

Make no mistake about it, across America post-9/11, for every blue-eyed patriot screeching for revenge, there was a poor migrant worker in brown skin -- parking the cars, cleaning the homes, and working three jobs for minimum wage -- who felt that America had just got what it deserved.

These people were and still are the unseen and the unheard in the 'land of opportunity'. Polite and servile on the surface, in their hearts resides the residual anger of the oppressed of all lands. 

Most businesses -- shops, bars, restaurants, etc. -- in and around Hollywood closed over the following few days. The bar/nightclub where I worked four nights a week at the time decided to remain open. Brentwood is located a half hour drive away, close to the main UCLA campus, and the bar down there where I worked -- El Dorado -- was popular with the legion of the predominately white children of the rich who studied there.

Two nights later there I am, standing in the middle of a deserted nightclub. The decision to remain open on the part of the owners was the wrong one. 

At one point, looking out at an empty dance floor, the DJ put on Frank Sinatra's classic tune, 'New York-New York'. It was intended as a gesture of solidarity with the victims of 9/11. It went down like a lead balloon, to the point where the few people who were there started booing him.

It was crude and it was crass under the circumstances, and he quickly and advisedly changed the music.

The last thing I remember from that time is the old homeless lady shuffling in my direction on Hollywood Boulevard a few days later. I felt sorry for her and offered her a five dollar bill.

She stopped, looked at me and said with surprising lucidity: 'No, thank you, I have my own money.' She then said, before shuffling off again: 'The world will never be the same.'

Moments later, this young white guy came striding along the street with his chest puffed out. 'Hey man,' he boomed in my direction. 'We're gonna kick their fucking asses.'

text:
🇺🇸 Prediction markets could start deciding elections instead of just predicting them.

The danger is the feedback loop: a political narrative moves the betting markets → the movement becomes news → perceived momentum brings attention, credibility and potentially funding → that momentum can begin influencing the race the market supposedly exists merely to predict.

California recently offered a striking example of the mechanism: a purported poll showing Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass comfortably ahead was amplified by her campaign, and within minutes election-market prices moved in her favor. 

The poll was later retracted as fabricated. A false political signal had already become a financial signal before the truth caught up.

And that creates potentially explosive incentives for propaganda, lies, corruption and cover-ups. 

If suppressing a damaging story for 48 hours, or successfully flooding the information environment with a misleading one, can move the market, political actors gain another reason to manipulate not just what voters know, but when they know it.

With prediction markets operating continuously and attaching prices to an expanding universe of political events, winning the market narrative could become half the political battle.

According to Stanford University economics professor Nick Bloom, up to 8% of the UK’s GDP has been lost due to leaving the EU – about £3,000 per adult.

Keith Brown, SNP deputy leader, said the figures showed how leaving the UK would benefit Scotland’s economy.

He made the claim days after Prime Minister Andy Burnham suggested that an independence vote could be held if public opinion showed demand for one.

Brown said: “Andy Burnham has stated the conditions for an independence referendum and now we know one of the prizes on offer – an independence dividend worth up to £3,000 for every person.

“Brexit has been an utter disaster for Scotland’s economy and public services – Westminster will never take us back into the EU, independence is the only way to make it happen."

Leaving the EU has damaged growth and investment, costing the public finances £250 million every day – so much of the cost-of-living crisis that is hurting people across Scotland today can be traced back to the decision to drag us out of the EU against our will.

“Andy Burnham is wedded to Brexit, so it is encouraging that he has set out the process and recognised the need for allowing the people of Scotland a choice over our own future.

“Only by taking our place as an independent nation in the EU can Scotland turn the page on our chapter in broken Brexit Britain. Scotland needs a fresh start with independence.”

Scottish Labour said the claims were “utter mince from a deluded and desperate SNP”.

text:
Alex Ivanov Demos Personal AI OS

Let’s dive into something that’s been making waves in the tech world: becoming an “AI Native.” It sounds like a fancy term, but it's really about making artificial intelligence work smoothly for you without all the chaos and confusion.

On September 15th at 6 PM Moscow time, Alex Ivanov will host a live stream titled "AI Native: три демо — как построить свою PersonalOS." This event promises to show how to turn your basic or intermediate use of AI into a reliable system that understands your context and tasks. So, what’s the big deal? Why should you care about becoming an “AI Native”? And how can this live stream help?
What’s Changing for You

Most people use AI like a smart search engine—they open it up, ask something, get an answer, and then close it. This approach often leaves them with results that need tweaking and makes AI seem unreliable. Plus, there's always the nagging feeling of FOMO (Fear Of Missing Out) as new AI tools pop up every day.

But what if you could create a Personal AI OS—a system where the AI knows who you are, understands your context, and works directly with your data? That’s exactly what Alex Ivanov will be showing during his live stream. He’ll cover three main demos:
• Building Knowledge in Obsidian: How to structure files and contexts so that AI can work with them efficiently without needing extra explanations.
• Note-taking and Task Management: Transforming meeting transcripts into tasks, ideas for content, calendar events, offers, and more.
• Automation of Routine Tasks: Setting up processes that run on their own using skills and AI agents. For example, creating content automatically or managing a personal dashboard.

So what changes for you? Instead of feeling overwhelmed by the constant influx of new AI tools, you’ll learn how to set up a system that works reliably with your existing data and tasks. This means less time spent on repetitive work and more time focusing on meaningful projects.
How It Works

The Personal AI OS concept is about creating a system where the AI understands who you are, your context, and works directly with your data without requiring constant tweaking. This means less time spent on repetitive work and more time focusing on meaningful projects.

During the live stream, Alex Ivanov will demonstrate how to build knowledge in Obsidian by structuring files and contexts so that AI agents like Claude or Codex can understand them efficiently. This is crucial because it means your AI system will be able to access and process information more effectively, reducing the need for manual intervention.

Another demo covers transforming meeting transcripts into actionable tasks and ideas. Imagine having a transcript of a business meeting automatically converted into tasks in your task management app or calendar events. This can save you hours of manual data entry and ensure nothing falls through the cracks.

The final demo showcases how to set up automated processes using AI agents. For example, setting up an agent to create content based on predefined templates or managing a personal dashboard that updates in real-time with your latest projects and tasks.
What Is Stored

When you build a Personal AI OS, what is stored includes structured data from Obsidian notes, meeting transcripts, task lists, and calendar events. The system also stores configurations for automated processes and settings related to AI agents like Claude or Codex. This ensures that the AI can work seamlessly with your existing workflows without requiring constant manual intervention.
What Is Excluded

The Personal AI OS does not store personal identifiable information (PII) unless explicitly provided by you, nor does it retain sensitive data such as financial records or health information. The system focuses on integrating and automating general tasks and knowledge management to enhance productivity.
User Controls

Users have control over what data is shared with the AI system through Obsidian settings and configurations. You can choose which files and contexts are accessible by AI agents, ensuring that sensitive or private information remains secure. Additionally, users can customize automated processes according to their specific needs and preferences.
Availability

The live stream on September 15th at 6 PM Moscow time is free and open to anyone who wants to attend. You can register via the link provided by Luma, which hosts tech-focused events regularly. Whether you’re a casual user or deeply involved with AI, there’s something here for everyone.
What This Does Not Prove

While Alex Ivanov’s approach offers valuable insights, it might not be the only way to achieve an "AI Native" status. Different people have different needs and preferences when it comes to technology integration. So while this event can offer valuable insights, it’s important to keep an open mind about other methods and tools that might work better for you.
Practical Takeaway

If you’re already using AI tools but feel like they’re not living up to their potential, becoming an "AI Native" could be a game-changer. It’s about understanding how to integrate these tools into your daily workflow in a way that makes sense for you and enhances productivity without the need for constant attention.

If APPLE still needs visibility, who exactly do you think you are? 😂

Apple launched the new iPhone 18 series and the iPhone Duo two days ago, and as expected, the internet went crazy

But what caught my attention wasn’t even the phones

It was what happened AFTER the launch

Samsung  started throwing shade at Apple 😂

Then Duolingo joined the conversation because Apple named its new foldable phone “Duo” 😂

And just like that, you had Apple trending, Samsung talking, Duolingo talking, tech creators talking, customers arguing and different communities joining the conversation

Most people look at this and see BANTER

I look at it from a marketing perspective and see something completely different

VISIBILITY

Think about what Samsung did

Millions of people were already paying attention to Apple

Instead of sitting somewhere and allowing Apple to have all that attention, Samsung inserted itself into the conversation

Now Team Apple responds

Team Samsung responds

People quote the posts

People argue about which foldable is better

Tech creators make comparison videos

And Samsung gets even MORE visibility from a product launch that wasn’t even theirs 😂

Duolingo did the same thing

The conversation had absolutely nothing to do with language learning

But there was an opportunity around the word “Duo,” and they took it

That is how brands think

Where is the ATTENTION?

How can we enter the conversation naturally?

How do we get people talking about us?

And there’s another interesting layer to the Apple and Samsung relationship

They are fierce competitors in the smartphone market, but Samsung has also supplied components for Apple products over the years

Business is interesting like that 😂

But don’t misunderstand it

That doesn’t mean the social media shade is secretly planned between them

It simply shows that brands can compete aggressively for customers while still doing business together elsewhere

And the bigger lesson for me is this👇

NO BRAND OUTGROWS THE NEED FOR VISIBILITY

Apple is already one of the biggest companies in the world

Everybody knows Apple

Yet when they launch a new product, they don’t quietly put it on their website and wait for people to discover it

They create an EVENT, they build anticipation, they get the media involved, they get creators talking

Samsung is already one of the biggest smartphone brands in the world

Yet they still jump into a competitor’s trending conversation to make sure people are talking about Samsung too

Duolingo already has a massive online presence

Yet they saw an opportunity to join the conversation and took it

Why?

Because being KNOWN doesn’t mean you stop trying to be SEEN

And somehow, you have a business with 300 followers and you’ve decided you don’t like posting 😂

You have a skill nobody knows about

You have an offer you barely talk about

You have a business and you’re waiting for customers to magically discover you

My dear, COME OUTSIDE 😂

Talk about what you do

Show your work

Join relevant conversations

Share your results

Talk about your offer

Make some noise around what you’re building

Because no matter how good you are, people need to KNOW YOU EXIST before they can buy from you

If Apple, Samsung and Duolingo are still fighting for attention, you definitely haven’t reached the stage where you can afford to be invisible

BE SEEN

text:
Apple releases iOS 27 with enhanced Siri

It’s that time again when the tech world gets all excited about new gadgets and software updates. Today, Apple dropped some big news with their latest iOS 27 release, which includes a significant overhaul of Siri. But is it really as groundbreaking as they’re making it out to be?
Apple releases iOS 27 with enhanced Siri

Apple’s announcement centers around the new dedicated app for Siri, which will sync your conversation history to iCloud. This means that Siri can now understand personal context like emails, messages, and photos, and even interact within third-party apps if developers support it through App Intents. But wait a minute—wasn’t this kind of functionality already available in some form? 

The new app aims to make Siri more conversational by storing your interaction history and using it to provide better context-aware responses. However, the actual implementation details are quite nuanced. For instance, while Siri can now understand personal context, it doesn't mean that every detail from your emails or messages is stored indefinitely. Apple’s privacy policies still apply, meaning only relevant data is retained for a short period.
Under the Hood: AFM 3 AI Core

The real tech wizardry behind Siri’s new capabilities lies in Apple’s third-generation AI Core (AFM 1). This core runs on devices with a capacity of 3 billion parameters, while the more advanced version has 20 billion parameters but only activates between 1 to 4 billion at any given time due to its sparse architecture. For cloud-based processing, Apple is using AFM 1 Cloud and ADM 1 Cloud models for image recognition, and AFM 1 Cloud Pro runs on NVIDIA GPUs in Google’s cloud infrastructure.

This new AI core significantly boosts Siri's performance by enabling more efficient use of computational resources. The sparse architecture ensures that only necessary parameters are activated at any given time, reducing power consumption while maintaining high accuracy. This is particularly important for devices like the iPhone and Apple Watch, where battery life is a critical factor.
What Is Stored?

When it comes to what Siri stores, it’s essential to understand that not everything you say or do with the app gets saved indefinitely. For example, your conversation history is stored temporarily in iCloud to provide context-aware responses but is deleted after a short period unless explicitly saved by you. Additionally, Apple’s privacy policies dictate that only relevant data is retained for improving Siri's performance and understanding user preferences.
What Is Excluded?

On the flip side, there are several things that Siri does not store or process. For instance, it doesn’t save your personal health data from apps like HealthKit unless you explicitly grant permission. Similarly, sensitive information such as financial details or passwords is never stored by Siri to protect user privacy.
User Controls

Apple has always been keen on giving users control over their data and how it’s used. With the new iOS 27 update, you can manage your Siri settings more granularly. For example, you can choose which apps Siri interacts with, set up voice commands for specific tasks, and even disable certain features if they make you uncomfortable.
Availability

The new iOS 27 is rolling out now, so you should see it on your device soon if you haven’t already. The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are scheduled to hit stores on September 18th, while the foldable iPhone Duo will be available for pre-order starting October 16th.
What This Does Not Prove

While Apple’s new features might seem impressive, it's important not to overstate their significance. The reality is that many of these capabilities have been in development or even partially implemented by other tech companies for years. For instance, Google Assistant and Amazon Alexa already offer similar context-aware interactions within third-party apps.
What This Does Prove

What this does prove is the ongoing evolution of AI-driven personal assistants and how they integrate with our daily lives. Apple’s approach highlights a shift towards more collaborative development, where external hardware like NVIDIA GPUs in Google's cloud infrastructure are leveraged to enhance performance. This move underscores the complexity and resource requirements involved in pushing the boundaries of AI technology.
The Awkward Bit: Renting Hardware from Google

The real awkward bit is why Apple is renting hardware from Google to run their models. It’s like they’re admitting that even with all their resources, they can’t quite keep up without some help. That’s a big deal for a company known for its proprietary tech stack.
Developer Considerations: Supporting App Intents

If you’re developing apps, supporting App Intents becomes crucial since Siri won’t know anything about your app otherwise. This means developers need to integrate these new features into their applications to stay relevant and ensure compatibility with the latest iOS updates.

So what do you think about this shift in strategy and reliance on external AI solutions? Let us know in the comments below!

text:
Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong told us that U.S. crypto will get regulatory definition whether or not the Senate advances the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act on September 15. Passage would lock the rules into statute. 

Failure would still matter, he argued, because the SEC and CFTC have said they are ready to publish rulemaking around the same date. The industry, in his telling, is no longer waiting on a single bill so much as on an end to legal fog.

The Clarity Act would split oversight that has been fought over for a decade: tokens whose value comes from a functioning blockchain network would generally sit with the CFTC as digital commodities, while tokens sold with an expectation of profit from others’ efforts would remain securities under the SEC. It would also set registration paths for exchanges and brokers and sit beside the already enacted GENIUS Act for payment stablecoins. 

The House passed it with a large bipartisan margin. The Senate still needs sixty votes for cloture. Republicans do not have them alone, and the last fights are political as much as legal: ethics limits on officials who hold or launch tokens, how far DeFi developer protections should go, and whether stablecoin arrangements can pay yield without becoming uninsured bank deposits in all but name.

That last point is the macroeconomic fault line. Banks, led publicly by Jamie Dimon, say yield on dollar tokens would pull deposits off balance sheets, weaken bank lending, and let crypto firms run a payments-and-savings product without the full stack of capital, AML and consumer rules that apply to insured institutions. 

Armstrong calls that self-interest from firms that dominate dollar payments. The real question is who intermediates the dollar once settlement can be programmed. Congress can assign that franchise by statute. If it cannot, the agencies will still have to decide how far existing securities and commodities law stretches, including for tokenized equities that Coinbase wants to offer onshore as real securities rather than offshore synthetics.

Coinbase is already hedging. Spot trading has been weak, quarterly revenue and earnings have missed, and the stock has been under pressure. The firm has expanded into stocks, commodities and FX, leaned on stablecoins and custody, and built hubs in Singapore and the UAE. 

That is the behavior of an intermediary that treats Washington as one jurisdiction, not the only one. It also fits the macro backdrop: the Fed has held rates in a 3.50–3.75 percent range while inflation has stayed above target, and the mid-September FOMC meeting lands in the same week as the Senate vote. In a higher-for-longer world, institutions do not need a perfect law. 

They need to know which statute applies, who supervises the venue, and whether a product can be sold to U.S. clients. Clarity of either kind lowers the legal discount on crypto cash flows and on the listed firms that stand between those flows and traditional capital. What remains is whether the settlement this month is durable enough to bring that capital in, or only clear enough to keep the same activity migrating to places that already licensed it.
