𝐕𝐀𝐍𝐂𝐄 𝐃𝐄𝐌𝐎𝐋𝐈𝐒𝐇𝐄𝐒 𝐌𝐄𝐗𝐈𝐂𝐀𝐍-𝐀𝐍𝐃-𝐏𝐀𝐋𝐄𝐒𝐓𝐈𝐍𝐈𝐀𝐍-𝐅𝐋𝐀𝐆 𝐇𝐄𝐂𝐊𝐋𝐄𝐑 𝐀𝐓 𝐃𝐀𝐋𝐋𝐀𝐒 𝐆𝐎𝐏 𝐂𝐎𝐍𝐕𝐄𝐍𝐓𝐈𝐎𝐍 — 𝐂𝐑𝐎𝐖𝐃 𝐃𝐄𝐋𝐈𝐕𝐄𝐑𝐒 𝐍𝐈𝐆𝐇𝐓’𝐒 𝐋𝐎𝐔𝐃𝐄𝐒𝐓 𝐑𝐎𝐀𝐑

A protester waving a Mexican flag and a Palestinian flag together tried to hijack Vice President JD Vance (@JDVance)’s closing keynote at the GOP’s midterm convention in Dallas Thursday night. “𝘞𝘦𝘭𝘭, 𝘮𝘺 𝘧𝘳𝘪𝘦𝘯𝘥, 𝘪𝘧 𝘺𝘰𝘶 𝘭𝘰𝘷𝘦 𝘔𝘦𝘹𝘪𝘤𝘰 𝘴𝘰 𝘮𝘶𝘤𝘩, 𝘨𝘦𝘵 𝘺𝘰𝘶𝘳 𝘢–– 𝘰𝘷𝘦𝘳 𝘵𝘩𝘦𝘳𝘦,” Vance sh∗t back once security hauled the demonstrator out. “𝘐’𝘭𝘭 𝘣𝘶𝘺 𝘺𝘰𝘶 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘱𝘭𝘢𝘯𝘦 𝘵𝘪𝘤𝘬𝘦𝘵.”

Vance told the arena the TV cameras at home had missed the moment, so he narrated it himself: a demonstrator had broken from the stands mid-speech, one flag in each hand, interrupting his remarks on ending birthright citizenship. 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐜𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐝’𝐬 𝐫𝐞𝐬𝐩𝐨𝐧𝐬𝐞 𝐰𝐚𝐬 𝐢𝐧𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐞𝐨𝐮𝐬 — a wall of “USA! USA!” chants that multiple outlets, including Fox News and Breitbart, called the loudest eruption of the entire convention.

Vance didn’t let the moment pass as a footnote — he built it into the thesis of his closing pitch. He told the arena the heckler had just handed Republicans “𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘴𝘺𝘮𝘣𝘰𝘭 𝘰𝘧 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘧𝘢𝘳 𝘭𝘦𝘧𝘵,” someone who’d rather wave two foreign flags than the one flying over the arena he was standing in. Vance said Republicans would keep doing the opposite: “𝘸𝘢𝘷𝘦 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘈𝘮𝘦𝘳𝘪𝘤𝘢𝘯 𝘧𝘭𝘢𝘨 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘧𝘪𝘨𝘩𝘵 𝘧𝘰𝘳 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘈𝘮𝘦𝘳𝘪𝘤𝘢𝘯 𝘥𝘳𝘦𝘢𝘮.” 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐜𝐨𝐧𝐭𝐫𝐚𝐬𝐭 𝐰𝐚𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐰𝐡𝐨𝐥𝐞 𝐩𝐨𝐢𝐧𝐭 — a party defending the flag, against a fringe that won’t even hold it.

It wasn’t Vance’s only moment stealing the spotlight in Dallas. With Secretary of State Marco Rubio absent from the final night and President Trump delivering a shorter-than-usual 25-minute closer, Vance had the runway to himself — and attendees walked away convinced he’d claimed it. “𝘏𝘦 𝘭𝘰𝘰𝘬𝘦𝘥 𝘵𝘰𝘯𝘪𝘨𝘩𝘵 𝘭𝘪𝘬𝘦 𝘩𝘦 𝘩𝘢𝘥 𝘣𝘦𝘤𝘰𝘮𝘦 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘨𝘶𝘺,” Texas attendee Frank McCaffrey told the New York Post, predicting the party will “𝘩𝘢𝘷𝘦 𝘵𝘰 𝘱𝘢𝘴𝘴 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘵𝘰𝘳𝘤𝘩 𝘵𝘰 𝘩𝘪𝘮” after the midterms.

For a base that’s watched Democrat-run cities defend illegal immigration and wave foreign flags at their own protests, the scene in Dallas landed as proof of exactly who’s fighting for the flag and who isn’t. text:
He did everything he promised for Americans. Here are just 25 things he did. That's one a month. He did more, much more. 
Trump Restored American Safety and Sovereignty

1. He made the border a real border again.
In a matter of months, Trump reduced illegal border crossings to their lowest level in half a century. Catch-and-release is finished. The wall is going up and even being expanded, “Remain in Mexico” is back, and the Administration reduced releases into the country by an incredible 99.9 percent.

2. He reversed mass migration.
America recorded negative net migration in 2025 for the first time in at least half a century. So far, nearly 3 million illegal aliens have left the country, whether voluntarily or involuntarily: more than 675,000 forcibly deported and the rest “self-deported.” 

Many of those self-deportations were facilitated by the President’s innovative program to offer plane tickets and cash bonuses for illegals to leave, not only incentivizing good behavior but significantly reducing the cost of deportations. Citizenship and the law actually mean something again.

3. He signed the Laken Riley Act — and required detention of criminal illegal aliens.
Named for an innocent girl murdered by an illegal alien, the Laken Riley Act requires federal authorities to detain illegals arrested for theft, burglary, shoplifting, assaulting police, or any crime causing death or serious injury. It also lets states sue officials who refuse to enforce it.

Laken Riley should still be alive. This law will prevent tragedies like hers.

4. History’s biggest drop in violent crime, and the lowest violent crime rate in 126 years.
According to FBI data, violent crime in America dropped an incredible 9.7 percent in 2025 — the largest one-year decline in history. Murder fell 18.1 percent, robbery fell 18.5 percent. And America’s violent crime rate is its lowest since 1900.

This is what happens when you put the National Guard on the streets in crime-ridden blue cities: fewer victims, safer streets, and better futures for America’s poorest.

Trump Launched an American Industrial Supercycle

5. He made the 2017 tax cuts permanent…and better.
The One Big Beautiful Bill locked in the largest tax cut in modern history, including the doubled standard deduction, the expanded Child Tax Credit, and 100 percent expensing for factories and equipment. It also delivered No Tax on Tips, No Tax on Overtime, an abolition of most taxes on Social Security benefits, and major relief for seniors.

Every Democrat voted no. With the 2017 act set to expire in December 2025, that would have resulted in the largest tax hike in American history.

6. He repealed 129 regulations for every new one.
In fiscal 2025, federal agencies finalized 646 deregulatory actions and just five regulatory actions: 129-to-1, and in nearly every case, the “one” was to repeal the others! OIRA says the savings exceeded those of Trump’s entire first term. That is more freedom, lower costs, and less bureaucratic sabotage.

Of these, the crown jewel was the repeal of Obama’s 2009 “Endangerment Finding”, the legal foundation for the Green New Scam’s vehicle mandates. EPA calls it the largest deregulatory action in American history and estimates that by itself, it will save Americans more than $1.3 trillion. Trump also killed the federal EV mandate, restored Americans’ freedom to buy the cars and trucks they actually want, and even eliminated the incentives behind the almost universally hated start-stop button.

7. He secured $18 trillion in announced investment commitments.
That’s nearly two-thirds the size of the entire American economy, building American factories, chip plants, data centers, energy projects, steel mills, shipyards, and supply chains employing American workers. Apple, Meta, NVIDIA, Micron, Hyundai, U.S. Steel, Ford, Taiwan Semiconductor, and many corporations and sovereign wealth funds are betting big on Trump’s America. 

No President has ever done anything remotely like it. And it’s just getting started.

8. He made “reshoring” and “reindustrialization” real, not a slogan.
Ford is moving Lincoln production out of China. Toyota is shifting Tacoma production from Mexico to Texas. GM, Honda, Mercedes-Benz, Stellantis, and others are expanding U.S. production. The capital equipment pouring into the country is the machinery that’s building the growing boom.

9. He replaced lopsided trade deals with balanced, reciprocal trade.
Trump used tariffs as leverage to reverse 80 years of lopsided trade deals that favored everyone but America, and to win new or improved agreements with trading partners accounting for more than half of global GDP. Those agreements open foreign markets, attack non-tariff barriers, defend strategic industries, and make it more profitable to build in America than to export American jobs.

10. He shifted global energy dominance from the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of America.
Once the world’s largest energy importer — “exporting” $700 billion a year to our enemies — America now outproduces Saudi Arabia and Russia combined. The U.S. is also setting new records in oil, natural gas, and LNG exports, becoming the first country ever to export more than 100 million metric tons of LNG in a year.

Trump also opened land, accelerated permits, expanded pipelines and export terminals, and made American energy a tool for prosperity and peace.

11. After four decades of nuclear paralysis, Trump brought five new reactors online in a single year.
For more than 40 years, not one new privately developed non-light-water reactor reached criticality in America. Trump ordered at least three by July 4, 2026. DOE delivered four by the deadline, then a fifth just one month later.

Decades of zero. One Trump summer: five. That is a genuine nuclear renaissance.

Trump Made Elections Matter Again

12. He broke the Deep State’s power to defy the elected branches.
In Trump v. Slaughter, the Supreme Court ruled for the first time in 90 years that Article 2, Section 1 is still part of the Constitution: the President may fire subordinate officials in the executive branch, overturning the 1935 precedent that insulated “independent” agencies from voters’ control.

Ever wonder why elections often seem to change nothing? How about one President and 5,000 political appointees vs. 2.8 million unfireable, unaccountable bureaucrats? THAT is the “Deep State”.

Trump then made that victory real. For the first time in a century, all policy-making bureaucrats can now be fired for misconduct, incompetence, or defying lawful directives. The permanent bureaucracy no longer gets to veto the voters.

13. He ended nationwide injunction abuse.
In Trump v. CASA, the Supreme Court sharply limited nationwide injunctions. A single, local, district judge should not be able to block a national policy for everyone, everywhere; and yet that’s exactly what they’ve done, nonstop, ever since Trump (and only Trump) took office in 2017. 

In restricting that unconstitutional power, the Court kneecapped the Black Robe Bureaucracy’s favorite tool of unlawful judicial supremacy.

14. He shut down USAID as a left-wing slush fund and shadow government.
USAID had become a taxpayer-funded machine for exporting abortion, gender ideology, censorship, and left-wing politics. It had a bigger budget than the CIA and the State Department combined, absolutely no accountability whatsoever, and a penchant for overthrowing governments.

Trump terminated it — completely — and moved real humanitarian aid under the State Department. Immediately, seven socialist Latin American governments lost re-election. Coincidence?

15. He shrank Federal employment to its lowest level in 60 years.
From a high under Biden, the federal workforce is now its smallest since 1966. Workforce reductions, agency closures, and spending cancellations mean fewer bureaucrats paid to resist the voters.

What’s more, when Biden left office, 94 percent of federal employees “worked” from home. The Trump administration cracked down: as Elon Musk put it, “you can work from the office or you can pretend to work somewhere else.”

16. He expelled DEI from the federal government.
Trump eliminated federal DEI offices and barred race- and sex-based preferences across the executive branch. Government hiring and contracting are returning to merit and equality under the law, ending the grotesque Democrat idea that “fighting discrimination” requires the federal government to discriminate.

He Defended Faith and Family

17. He delivered sweeping pro-life reform.
In his first term, Trump delivered the judges that overturned the abominable Roe v. Wade. Hardly anyone believed it could be done, or that Trump would do it. But he did, and a half-century nightmare finally ended.

Since returning to office, Trump has enforced the Hyde Amendment prohibiting the use of federal funds to pay for abortions, reinstated and expanded the Mexico City Policy prohibiting federal funding of foreign abortions, ended federal fetal-tissue research, strengthened conscience protections, protected Medicaid from funding large abortion providers, and pardoned 23 pro-life activists prosecuted by Biden’s weaponized Justice Department.

He’s also done everything within the Executive Branch’s power to defund Planned Parenthood. It would be nice if Congress did likewise.

No President has ever done more to protect life. No one.

18. He got men out of women’s sports, and restored biological reality to federal policy.
The United States government once again officially recognizes two sexes: male and female. Trump ended federal support for the chemical and surgical gender mutilation of children, stopped taxpayer funding of such irreversible abominations, and forced more than three dozen health systems to end or suspend their programs as well.

Trump also enforced Title IX as written: women and girls deserve their own teams, trophies, scholarships, and locker rooms. The NCAA and other athletic organizations changed their rules in response. After years of Democrats doing everything they could to destroy women’s sports and ruin girls’ lives, Trump’s administration protects women and girls again.

19. He enacted America’s first nationwide school-choice program — and launched Trump Accounts.
As part of the President’s One Big Beautiful Bill, Trump enacted America’s first-ever nationwide school choice program. The new Education Freedom Tax Credit helps fund scholarships for tuition, books, and other educational costs.

That’s on top of the new Trump Accounts, which give every child a tax-advantaged stake in America’s future, including a $1,000 federal seed for eligible newborns. Parents gain power. Bureaucracies lose it. And children learn first-hand about free markets and future orientation.

20. He targeted anti-Christian bias and discrimination.
Trump created the White House Faith Office, Religious Liberty Commission, and Task Force to Eradicate Anti-Christian Bias. He restored conscience protections and made clear that Christians do not surrender their First Amendment rights merely by entering public life.

He Restored Peace Through Strength and Put America First

21. He forced NATO to stop freeloading and increase defense spending by 250 percent.
For decades, wealthy European governments underfunded their militaries, effectively sending America the bill and using American taxpayers to subsidize their bloated welfare states. Trump forced NATO to replace its old two-percent-of-GDP spending target with an enormous five percent by 2035.

Allied spending is rising, American defense orders are soaring, and Europe is becoming a partner instead of a dependent.

22. He drove China out of the Caribbean.
China spent years building strategic beachheads at both ends of the Panama Canal, in Cuba, and in Maduro’s Venezuela. Trump forced Panama out of Belt and Road, expanded American security access around the Canal, and captured Maduro, who now sits in a New York jail cell awaiting trial.

Beijing’s planned encirclement of the United States collapsed. The Monroe Doctrine is back. Call it the Donroe Doctrine.

23. He brokered eight peace deals in just eight months.
In eight months, Trump brokered peace in eight conflicts spanning four continents, including wars that had gone on for as much as 40 years. It’s a record unmatched by any other President.

24. He launched and funded Golden Dome, the first-ever true missile defense for the U.S. population.
Ronald Reagan dreamed of making nuclear missiles obsolete through his Strategic Defense Initiative. Today, Trump is actually building it: a layered homeland shield with space-based sensors and interceptors, conventional defenses, and new technologies including microwave systems to destroy drone swarms and directed-energy weapons (yes, lasers) that can replace an $11 million missile with $2 of electricity.

Congress has funded the initial $25 billion, with far more on the way once it passes the NDAA this fall. Better a shield than a sword.

25. He restored the warrior ethos — and reversed the recruiting crisis.
After years of missed targets under Biden, every active military component met or exceeded its 2025 recruiting goal. Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth refocused the newly renamed Department of War on actually winning wars, while pouring resources into shipbuilding, munitions, drones, missile defense, and America’s atrophied industrial base.

Austin, TX — Democratic U.S. Senate nominee James Talarico is, according to a review of photographs, school records and multiple eyewitness accounts, an eighth grader.

Reporters observed the candidate Thursday morning stepping off a school bus outside Westview Middle School in gym shorts, sneakers and a multicolored propeller cap, backpack over both shoulders, walking in with everyone else.

The campaign says Talarico is 37, has served in the Texas House since 2019, and is a student at Austin Presbyterian Theological Seminary. It did not address the bus.

The finding may explain a persistent oddity in the polling. Ken Paxton leads voters over 50 by thirteen points, 53 to 40, a gap analysts had credited to Social Security and the cost of living. One strategist offered a simpler theory: older Texans have met eighth graders before and were the first to notice.

Talarico still leads the race overall, by four in the AARP survey, by five in Univision/YouGov and by one in InsiderAdvantage. Texas has not sent a Democrat to the Senate since 1988, and would now be doing it with someone who has a locker.

He has raised $68.6 million to Paxton's $9.25 million, a figure the campaign touts as evidence of grassroots strength and which would also make him, comfortably, the wealthiest eighth grader in the state.

Records do confirm Talarico spent several years at a middle school in San Antonio. The campaign notes this was in the capacity of a teacher. Reporters were unable to determine which account is correct.

At press time, the candidate was up four points statewide and had been asked to produce a hall pass.

https://t.co/3vwon84vZM

These 14 stories offer essential media monitoring and press review on film, streaming and entertainment, from IFFJK's record-breaking festival to PVR INOX's VPF drop and Salman Khan's legal battle. According to Press Monitor's tracking of Indian publications, this week's developments span festivals, legal battles, streaming shifts, and box office triumphs — a must-read briefing for entertainment professionals.

1. IFFJK 2026 Sets New Attendance Record
A front-page report in The Hindu says the International Film Festival of Jammu and Kashmir 2026 concluded as an unforgettable journey. Over 1,84,000 films were submitted and screened across the festival, featuring masterclasses and discussions from 6,600+ visitors. Directorate of Information and Public Relations, J&K acknowledged sponsors and associates for supporting the celebration of cinema and culture.

Why it matters: The International Film Festival of Jammu and Kashmir drew unprecedented participation, signaling the region's growing ambition as a cinema hub.

Key detail: Over 1,84,000 films were submitted and screened, with 6,600+ visitors attending masterclasses and discussions.

Source: Cross-referenced across 8 publications including The Hindu, Times of India, State Times, and Tribune.

Next step: Watch for year-round programming commitments from the J&K government.

Closing: Can Jammu and Kashmir become India's next major film destination?

2. PVR INOX Proposes to Drop Virtual Print Fee
A front-page report in Business Standard says that the Competition Commission of India has invited public comments on PVR INOX Limited’s proposal to drop the Virtual Print Fee for film producers. The proposal offers a choice between a per‐show exhibitor charge or a revised revenue‑share that caps the producer’s share drop at seven point five percent, with implementation within twelve days of approval. Comments are due by October first, 2026.

Why it matters: The Competition Commission of India is reviewing a landmark proposal that could reshape the economics of film exhibition across India.

Key detail: PVR INOX's commitment offers exhibitors a choice between a per-show charge or a revised revenue-share capping producer share drop at 7.5%, with implementation within 12 days of approval.

Source: Business Standard, Financial Express.

Next step: Public comments are due by October 1, 2026.

Closing: Will the end of VPF accelerate film distribution for smaller producers?

3. TIFF Festival Opens Sixth Decade
A front-page report in Business Standard says The Toronto International Film Festival embarks on its sixth decade with the launch of TIFF: The Market, a new commercial platform for industry professionals. The festival also opens a direct pathway to the Academy Awards for non-English-language films through its Platform competitive section. Indian films Angh, Half, and Dorothy are among the notable entries in this year's lineup.

Why it matters: The Toronto International Film Festival launches a new commercial platform and opens an Oscar pathway for non-English-language films, with Indian entries in the spotlight.

Key detail: Indian films Angh, Half, and Dorothy are among notable entries in the Platform competitive section.

Source: Business Standard, reported from Toronto on 10 September.

Next step: Track which Indian films gain traction at TIFF: The Market.

Closing: Could an Indian film finally secure an Oscar nomination through this new route?

4. Hanuman Ansh Becomes a Devotional Box Office Hit
A front-page report in Times of India says Hanuman Ansh, a biographical film depicting the life of Neem Karoli Baba, has emerged as a major box office success, grossing approximately rupees one hundred fifty-one crore on a rupees seventy-two crore budget. The sleeper hit is sparking renewed interest in the devotional genre, which historically dominated early Indian cinema before being largely displaced by television and modern mainstream productions. Filmmaker Vishal Chaturvedi’s spiritually grounded narrative connects deeply with audiences while highlighting themes of humility and social equality.

Why it matters: The biographical film on Neem Karoli Baba has grossed over ₹151 crore, reviving interest in the devotional genre that once dominated early Indian cinema.

Key detail: Made on a ₹72 crore budget, the sleeper hit is sparking renewed interest in spiritually grounded storytelling.

Source: Times of India, reported from Noida.

Next step: Watch for more devotional biopics entering production.

Closing: Is the devotional genre poised for a mainstream comeback?

5. Government's Move to Shift National Film Awards Draws Criticism
A front-page report in The Asian Age says a government decision to move the 72nd National Film Awards ceremony from Delhi to Kevadia in Gujarat has drawn criticism. Raj questioned why Gujarat was chosen over Mumbai or major film-producing states like Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, alleging an attempt to reduce the cultural and economic importance of both Mumbai and New Delhi to favour Gujarat. The report notes this is the first time in the 72-year history of the National Film Awards that the ceremony is being moved away from the country's capital Delhi.

Why it matters: The decision to move the 72nd National Film Awards from Delhi to Kevadia, Gujarat has sparked debate about cultural politics and regional favoritism.

Key detail: This is the first time in the awards' 72-year history that the ceremony is being moved away from the capital Delhi.

Source: Asian Age.

Next step: Monitor reactions from film bodies and state governments.

Closing: Should national cultural events remain in the capital?

6. NAZA Documentary Exposes AI-Enabled Warfare at Venice
A front-page report in Deccan Chronicle says a new documentary from two Oscar-winning Israeli filmmakers provides damning new testimony about AI-enabled mass killings in Gaza from 24 Israeli military or intelligence figures who agreed to testify on camera in Tel Aviv with protected identities. The film NAZA, named after a euphemism used by Israeli intelligence for expected civilian casualties in airstrikes, is the only documentary in competition at this year's Venice Film Festival and describes how mass surveillance combined with AI technology identified people for assassination. Israel's bombardment of Gaza has left around 73,500 Palestinians dead and 174,500 wounded since October 2023 according to Gaza's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures the United Nations deems reliable.

Why it matters: A new documentary featuring testimony from 24 Israeli military figures on AI-enabled mass killings is the only film in competition at this year's Venice Film Festival.

Key detail: The film NAZA describes how mass surveillance combined with AI technology identified people for assassination.

Source: Deccan Chronicle, reported from Venice.

Next step: Follow the festival's reception and potential awards impact.

Closing: Can documentary filmmaking drive accountability in conflict zones?

7. Salman Khan Blocks Kala Hiran Release at Delhi High Court
A front-page report in Tribune says that actor Salman Khan approached the Delhi High Court on Thursday to block the release of the film Kala Hiran: The Battle for Legacy. Khan sought an injunction against the film's release and over Rs 2 crore in damages for alleged defamation and violation of his personality rights. Producer Amit Jani argued the film was not yet in a releasable form and had not received Central Board of Film Certification.

Why it matters: Salman Khan's legal move to block the release of Kala Hiran: The Battle for Legacy highlights the growing intersection of celebrity rights and film certification in India.

Key detail: Khan sought an injunction and over ₹2 crore in damages for alleged defamation and violation of personality rights.

Source: Tribune, reported from New Delhi on 10 September.

Next step: Watch for the court's ruling on the injunction.

Closing: Where should the line be drawn between personality rights and creative expression?

8. Zee 5 Transforms Platform for Family Streaming
A front-page report in Economic Times says Zee 5 has reimagined its platform across mobile and connected TVs with sharper personalisation and AI-led discovery. The service targets the entire Indian household with five entertainment universes covering premium content, free programming, kids, TV, and sports including FIFA World Cup 2O26 rights. Ormax OTT Audience Report 2O26 data cited by the paper shows India's active connected TV audience grew sixty per cent in a year to 206.9 million viewers.

Why it matters: Zee 5's AI-led personalization and five entertainment universes target the entire Indian household, backed by data showing a 60% surge in connected TV audiences.

Key detail: India's active connected TV audience grew to 206.9 million viewers, with Zee 5 securing FIFA World Cup 2026 rights.

Source: Economic Times.

Next step: Monitor subscriber growth following the platform overhaul.

Closing: Will family-centric streaming outpace niche content in India?

9. Samantha Ruth Prabhu Makes Triumphant Acting Comeback
A front-page report in Millennium Post says that actress Samantha Ruth Prabhu, diagnosed with myositis in twenty twenty-two, has returned to acting after overcoming a difficult period and an unsuccessful shoot for Citadel Honey Bunny. With encouragement from her husband Raj Nidimoru, she starred in Maa Inti Bangaram, which became the highest-grossing female-led Telugu film and earned one hundred crore rupees at the box office. Despite initially considering a full exit from screen acting to pursue entrepreneurship, Samantha credits Raj’s unwavering faith in her talent for her successful comeback.

Why it matters: After a health challenge and a failed project, Samantha Ruth Prabhu's return with Maa Inti Bangaram became the highest-grossing female-led Telugu film.

Key detail: The film earned ₹100 crore at the box office, proving the power of resilience in an actor's career.

Source: Millennium Post.

Next step: Track her upcoming projects and the broader trend of actress-led blockbusters.

Closing: What does her comeback mean for women in South Indian cinema?

10. Bollywood Continues Betting on Biopic Productions
A front-page report in Mint says filmmakers continue backing biopic and sports drama projects despite recent box office misses. Experts advise producers to focus on stronger emotional narratives and immersive theatre experiences rather than strict documentary styles. This shift targets audiences who value engaging stories over specific genres, while maintaining long-term streaming value, following a Michael Jackson biopic earning rupees sixty crore in India.

Why it matters: Despite recent box office misses, filmmakers are doubling down on biopics and sports dramas, shifting toward emotional narratives and immersive theatre experiences.

Key detail: A Michael Jackson biopic earned ₹60 crore in India, signaling audience appetite for real-life stories.

Source: Mint, reported from New Delhi.

Next step: Watch which biopic projects secure greenlights in the next quarter.

Closing: Are biopics the safest bet in an uncertain box office landscape?

11. Manisha Koirala Set for Hollywood Debut in Cowgirls and Indians
A front-page report in Morning Standard says Manisha Koirala will next be seen in a Hollywood independent production titled Cowgirls and Indians, written and directed by Tejal Desai. The coming-of-age film is set in the American southwest and follows a middle-aged Indian woman navigating unlikely friendships against a Texas backdrop. Koirala recently starred in Sanjay Leela Bhansali's series Heeramandi on Netflix and was moved to tears when veteran Bollywood actress Rekha praised her performance.

Why it matters: Manisha Koirala's next role in a Hollywood independent production signals growing cross-border opportunities for Indian talent.

Key detail: The coming-of-age film set in the American southwest is written and directed by Tejal Desai, following Koirala's acclaimed Netflix series Heeramandi.

Source: Morning Standard.

Next step: Follow casting announcements and production timelines.

Closing: Will this be the breakthrough role that redefines Koirala's international career?

12. Karnataka High Court Quashes 2% Cinema Cess
A front-page report in Deccan Herald says the High Court of Karnataka quashed various orders and circulars issued by the state government that prescribed levying a 2 percent cess on cinema ticket revenues under the Karnataka Cine and Cultural Activists Welfare Act, 2024. Justice H T Narendra Prasad passed this order while allowing a petition filed by the Multiplex Association of India, PVR INOX Ltd, and others, who challenged the government directives issued in 2026. The court also noted that the Labour Department withdrew the office circulars that directed the collection of the cess on ticket sales and related establishments.

Why it matters: The Karnataka High Court struck down the state's 2% cinema cess, a ruling that could influence entertainment taxation policy across India.

Key detail: The court allowed a petition by the Multiplex Association of India and PVR INOX Ltd, noting the Labour Department had withdrawn related office circulars.

Source: Deccan Herald, reported from Bengaluru.

Next step: Watch for state government responses and potential appeals.

@RobPowellWFC  

Robin ,

I asked you some very straightforward questions about the extraordinary claims you’ve publicly made about your athletic, coaching and professional career.

You didn’t answer a single one.

So I’ll ask again. All I’m requesting is independent, verifiable evidence for your own public claims. 🧵

1/ You’ve described yourself as an “Olympic hopeful.”

What sport and event? What Olympic cycle? Can you provide official qualifying results, rankings, trials results or contemporary reporting showing you were actually an Olympic hopeful?

2/ You’ve claimed involvement with the AFL and CFL and an invitation from the Miami Dolphins.

Which teams and what years? What exactly was the Dolphins invitation—tryout, camp, workout or contract? Can you provide team records or contemporary documentation?

3/ You’ve claimed 150+ records and 1,000+ victories.

In what sports? Which governing bodies recognized them? Where are the official record books, meet results, rankings or databases documenting these extraordinary numbers?

4/ You’ve described yourself as a four-time “world champion” and promoted your World Fitness Challenge accomplishments.

Which recognized organizations awarded those world titles? How many competitors were in each event you won? Where are the complete official results and standings?

5/ You’ve made extensive claims about fighting/martial arts and training military and law-enforcement personnel.

What sanctioned fights or competitions? Which organizations kept the records? Which military or law-enforcement agencies hired you, when, and can they verify it?

6/ You’ve described yourself as a professional bodyguard.

Who employed you, during what years and through what company or agency? Can you provide independent documentation—licenses, employment records, contemporary reporting or verifiable clients?

7/ You’ve claimed to be a five-time Teacher of the Year.

Five is an impressive number. Which schools, districts or organizations presented each award, and in what years? Can you provide district announcements, board records, yearbooks or contemporary coverage?

8/ You’ve claimed an extraordinary number of championships as a coach, with different versions of your biography apparently giving different totals—including 16 and 20.

Which championships, schools, sports and years? Why the different totals? Where are the official records?

9/ You’ve claimed two bowl victories as part of your football coaching résumé.

Which bowl games? What years and teams? What was your official coaching position? Can you provide official staff rosters or contemporary coverage showing you were actually on those staffs?

10/ Your biography describes an extensive coaching career.

How about a simple year-by-year résumé: school, sport and position? And for each stop, did you resign, complete your contract or get dismissed? Can those jobs be independently verified?

11/ You’ve also made claims about your college athletic career and scholarship opportunities.

Which colleges did you attend or compete for? Which sports and seasons? Which schools offered scholarships? Can you provide official rosters, statistics, letters or contemporary reporting?

12/ Rob, these are YOUR public claims. I’m not asking anyone to believe me.

I’m asking you to substantiate them with independent sources: official results, rosters, school records, governing-body records or contemporary reporting.

Yesterday you answered none of them.

text:
Reformed theology does not treat the “how” as a solved mechanism. It treats it as a tension Scripture itself forces on us and then draws a set of distinctions to keep two claims together: God ordains whatsoever comes to pass, and God is not the author of sin.

The distinctions they and we use:

They distinguish “first cause” from “second causes”. God is the ultimate, first cause of everything that exists and happens. Creatures (including human wills) are real second causes. The Confession’s language is that the decree does not take away “the liberty or contingency of second causes, but rather established” them. People really choose; their choices are not illusory. Those choices simply fall inside God’s prior plan.

They further distinguish an “efficacious” (or efficient) decree from a “permissive” decree.

- For holiness and good works, God works “in” the person (“it is God who works in you, both to will and to work,” Phil. 2:13). That is an efficient decree.
- For sin, they refuse to say God works the evil “in” the sinner the same way. Sin is treated as a defect or corruption (a lack of the good that ought to be there), not as a positive thing God produces. God decrees that the sinful act will certainly occur- by creating the agent, upholding the agent’s existence and power to act, placing the agent in particular circumstances, withholding restraining grace, and bounding the act so it serves His ends- but “the sinfulness thereof proceedeth only from the creature, and not from God.” That is the language of Westminster Confession 5.4.

So the Reformed answer to “Does God make it happen?” is: He makes the event certain; He does not produce the moral defect. The proximate, blameworthy cause is the creature acting according to its own will.

They also insist this is not “bare permission” (God standing back as a spectator). The permission is active: He bounds, orders, and governs the sin “to his own holy ends.”

 The “how” we do not claim to have

Calvin himself said the precise way God can ordain the fall and other sins “without God being implicated as associate in the fault” is “a secret so much excelling the insight of the human mind, that I am not ashamed to confess ignorance.” Later Reformed writers repeat the same limit. They do not offer a complete causal diagram that satisfies every “how.” They say both truths are taught in Scripture, therefore they are compatible, even if the inner relation is not fully transparent to us.

The texts they always cite are the ones that hold both sides in one sentence:

- Joseph’s brothers: “You meant evil against me, but God meant it for good” (Gen. 50:20).
- The crucifixion: Jesus was “delivered up according to the definite plan and foreknowledge of God,” and at the same time “you crucified and killed by the hands of lawless men” (Acts 2:23; 4:27–28).

Same event, two intentions, two agents. God is not doing the lawless act; the lawless men are. Yet the event is not outside His plan/decree

The “why”:  the manifestation of God’s glory- specifically His justice and His grace.

Arminianism and Molinism does not actually escape the original problem. God still freely chooses to create this world, knowing every rejection and every evil that will occur. He still permits what He could prevent. The “how is God not responsible?” question is only moved, not removed. If God decided to create with the knowledge of the fall, He still decreed the fall and every sin thereafter.

text:
Is it schismatic to leave a NAPARC church or denomination to form a church outside of NAPARC? No, it is not, certainly not inherently so.

Jeremiah Burroughs is helpful here. You do not have to agree with every point he makes or every detail to see that his framework is correct and beneficial. Many men remain in compromised Reformed and Presbyterian churches or denominations because their Elders heap false guilt upon them, groundlessly charging them with being schismatics, claiming that leaving a Reformed and Presbyterian Church that belongs to NAPARC (North American Presbyterian and Reformed Council, which includes many Reformed and Presbyterian denominations such as the PCA, OPC, ARP, RPCNA, URC, etc.) to join or find a new church or denomination that is not associated with NAPARC is tantamount to sinful division, fracturing the body of Christ, disturbing the peace and purity of the church, ipso facto declaring any and all in NAPARC to be a false or apostate church, etc. Yet, as Jeremiah Burroughs shows us, none of these things necessarily follow. If you refute them on these points, some of these NAPARC Elders will then resort to charging you with joining or forming a false or illegitimate church if you join or form one outside of NAPARC or a “NAPARC approved” denomination.

But, as Burroughs demonstrates, you can join a new church or denomination without damning or anathematizing the one you no longer belong to. You can still believe that your former church or denomination, along with its minister and Elders, are true Christians and a true congregation. In other words, you do not need to think that NAPARC or any particular denomination or particular church is apostate or false like the Roman Catholic Church or something similar, in order to join a Reformed and Presbyterian church that is not associated with NAPARC. You could even think that NAPARC is perfectly healthy and still join a Reformed and Presbyterian Church that is not NAPARC for a host of legitimate reasons.

Now, I do believe that NAPARC is quite compromised and that many of the denominations within NAPARC are compromised by the Egalitarian and Feminist spirit of our age and can rightly be said to be apostatizing. But you do not need to have that level of distress to join a church or denomination, or even to form one, that is outside of NAPARC or one of its member denominations (such as the PCA, OPC, ARP, RPCNA, URC, etc.). If they try to argue that you are joining a micro-presbytery or are (at least temporarily) becoming an independent church, that argument also holds no weight, and by making it they contradict themselves. NAPARC includes several micro-presbytery denominations, some of which number only single digits in terms of congregations, and total membership per Wikipedia of the Presbyterian Reformed Church denomination within NAPARC is said to be only 226 members: (https://t.co/Dm0KvQattk).

If the question is asked, COULD leaving a local church or denomination be schismatic, the answer of course is yes. But the reason for the schism is not because you are leaving any particular denomination or particular church or particular council and constellation of denominations, but because you are departing and joining or forming something new for unbiblical and illegitimate reasons.

But without further ado, here is Burroughs chapter on these matters, from his book Irenicum:

Chapter 23 --  The Fourth Dividing Practice: Gathering of Churches Disorderly

This is cried out as the greatest dividing practice of all. You may speak of this or that being dividing amongst us, say some, but above all things, this gathering of churches is the great divider amongst us. To this I shall speak in these six things.

First, it is not absolutely unlawful for a church to be gathered out of a church. Voetius, that learned professor of Utrecht, answering Jansenius pleading against us for separating from the Romish Church, which was the most ancient and famous Church: No, says he, it is not absolutely evil to separate from such a church; for then the Christians gathering themselves out of the Jewish Church were schismatics, which is false.

Doctor Jackson, a prelatical man, in the 14th chapter of his Treatise of the Church, gives two reasons which he says are just and necessary for which men (whether few or many) may and ought to separate themselves from any visible church. First, because they are urged or constrained to profess or believe some points of doctrine or to venture upon some practices which are contrary to the rule of faith or love of God. Second, in case they are utterly deprived of freedom of conscience in professing what they inwardly or are bereft of some other means either altogether necessary or most expedient to salvation. For which latter he quotes 1 Cor. 7:23: "Ye are bought with a price; be not ye servants of men." Although (says he) we were persuaded that we could communicate with such a church without evident danger of damnation, yet inasmuch as we cannot communicate with it upon any better terms than legal servants or bondslaves do with their masters, we are bound in conscience and religious discretion when lawful occasions and opportunities are offered to use our liberty and seek our freedom rather than live in bondage.

This doctrine was allowed in the bishops' times. Now suppose upon these two grounds there be a withdrawing from a church; Christ does not require his people to live without ordinances all their days rather than they should join themselves together into another body.

Secondly, yet where these causes are not but men may communicate without sin, professing the truth and enjoying all ordinances as freemen of Christ. Men must not separate from a church though there be corruption in it to gather into a new church which may be more pure and in some respects more comfortable. First, because we never find the saints in Scripture separating or raising churches in such a case; and secondly, there would be no continuance in church fellowship if this were admitted: for what church is so pure and has all things so comfortable but within a while another church will be more pure and some things will be more comfortable there? The general peace of the church should be more regarded by us than some comfortable accommodations for ourselves.

Thirdly, although you cannot for the present communicate with the church in which you are without sin or bondage, yet you are not presently to withdraw to gather into another or join with another. You are bound to give so much respect to the church as to continue with much long-suffering to seek the good of that church to remove the sin that is upon it with all good means you can. You must bear much with a brother; much more with a church.

Fourthly, if things were in that ordered and settled way as they ought, there ought to be no gathering of any new churches without consulting and advising with neighboring churches. Christ would have all churches unite themselves and have conjunction one with another being all of the same body of Christ. If then there is to be raised a new sister church that expects and desires the benefit of communion with the rest, there is all the reason in the world that the help, advice, and assistance of the other churches should be made use of in raising and ordering this church that they are thus to own in the way of communion with them to whom they are to give the right hand of fellowship.

Fifthly, all believers who live in a place together ought, as far as they can, to join into one Church, even if they have different judgments and temperaments. Whatever differences they have, if they can coexist with grace, they have no encouragement from the examples of any of the Churches we read about in Scripture to divide themselves into small groups. The way of Christ throughout Scripture is that all the Saints in such a place, who are not more than can join in one, should join together and form just one Church. Certainly, this is more for the honor of Christ's Body than the division of Saints in the same place into several small societies. Christ places great importance on the union of his Saints in one, in all ways, by all means possible.

Sixthly, as things currently stand with us, there is no substantial reason for the outcry against the gathering of Churches as a divisive practice, as many seem to make it. How can this practice be so offensive when almost all of you think it lawful for a man to move from one Church to another for convenience, provided he relocates his dwelling? But these do not establish new Churches.

Answer: If a group of men with estates is not satisfied with the Ministry they are currently joined with and decides to buy land close by, build on it, and receive permission from the State to create a new Parish from those dwellings, who would blame them for gathering a Church in this manner? Hence, it is apparent that withdrawing from our Churches and gathering others is not against any Church Principle according to our Brethren's judgments; the offense lies only against some Civil constitution.

Secondly, this practice has been commonly practiced before without any offense to the godly and is still practiced without complaint. Has it not been, and is it not still common for many not to communicate in the Parishes where they live? Nor commonly to hear there, but from all parts of the City to come to some Parishes where they perceive the best Ministers to be, and there to hear and communicate regularly, with allowance for the maintenance of such Ministers? Yes, and thus the husband goes one way and the wife another, yet none are offended; perhaps the gentleman is content with his Parish-Church, but his wife or lady is not satisfied and must go elsewhere.

If it is said that this was during a time of great confusion when things were not as reformed as they are now and may be further reformed:

Answer: 1. Then it is not inherently unlawful. 2. It continues so still in many places of this City. 3. When you have reformed further, perhaps men's consciences will be further satisfied; you may reform enough to prevent much of what you now complain about.

But though they came for their present relief, they did not bind themselves to one another by Covenant as men do now.

Answer: If those who came constantly to your Ministry and Sacraments had professed their willingness to join with you in all the Ordinances of Christ as far as they knew and to walk accordingly, you might have more comfortably administered ordinances to them; it could not have been offensive to you.

Objection: But their Covenant binds them so that they cannot return back again, regardless of any reformation.

Answer: Pray for and endeavor to advance Reformation to the utmost, and then see what they will do; they have not yet declared themselves as holding themselves so joined by any Covenant that they may not join with you. Whatever relief they have had for the present time or whatever agreement there has been among themselves should not hinder them from following that way consistently presented in Scripture; namely, for all the Saints that live together to join in one as far as possible.

But those who gather Churches in this way view all others who are not in that way as Heathens; what division must this cause?

Answer: If this were true, it would indeed be a sad dividing practice; wicked men cannot endure being judged this way or being cast out as unworthy of Church-fellowship. Much less can the Saints bear it; it must deeply affect their hearts. Aben Ezra says the Ammonites and Moabites burned the Books of the Law because of Deuteronomy 23:3: "An Ammonite or Moabite shall not enter into the Congregation of the Lord, even to their tenth Generation." If an Ammonite or Moabite cannot bear being shut out of the Congregation of the Lord,* how can the Saints bear it? But God knows, and our Brethren may know—I hope they shall know— that this is not the case: O no, they view you as precious Saints of God, their dear Brethren in Jesus Christ. They bless God for the graces they see in you and rejoice in the hope of living eternally in Heaven with you.

But why then will they not admit them to their communion?

Answer: In all worship that belongs to Saints as Saints, they joyfully join with them; but they believe there is some worship that belongs to Saints gathered in a Society under officers, which cannot be performed orderly except in that way. They think it unreasonable for anyone to have the benefits of Church privileges while being under no power or discipline of any Church; that they should pick and choose Ordinances yet live at liberty so that if they walk disorderly, no Church has any power to call them to account. Suppose this is a reason why they do not admit some; this is different from judging them as Heathens.

Let me say further: I know none of these congregated Churches, either here or elsewhere, that ever refused anyone who appeared godly from communicating with them if they acknowledged themselves as members of any Church elsewhere, even if that Church was in a different way regarding government.

You will ask, what need is there for that?

Answer: If it is to prevent looseness in men who will be under no government or because they judge Sacramental communion as a Church-Ordinance; or if it should be through a mistake—yet howsoever—this must not be judged as them considering all who do not join with them as Heathens; this is the most uncharitable interpretation possible.

"We both gave each other imposter syndrome for all of this time."

And before they even committed to building Wispr Flow, they spent 6 months talking through how they'd navigate hard situations. Especially one particular question:

"If we got X dollars of an acquisition offer, what matters to us really?"

text:
9 Pivotal Online Services & Digital Platforms Stories for Tech Leaders
https://t.co/czBVuA3tnj

According to Press Monitor's tracking of Indian publications, the digital services landscape is shifting rapidly. This media monitoring report delivers a focused press review of nine critical moves shaping how platforms operate, compete, and comply. Our media intelligence briefing highlights actionable insights. Read on for news on Online Services & Digital Platforms that every executive needs to know.

1. Government Tightens E-Commerce Rules from 2027
A front-page report in Deccan Herald says the government has tightened norms for online shopping platforms by amending the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, focusing on greater price transparency, clearer disclosures and curbs on manipulative practices. The Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) (Amendment) Rules, 2026, notified by the Department of Consumer Affairs, will take effect from January 1, 2027. Platforms must display both the discounted price and the prior price, defined as the lowest price offered in the thirty days preceding the discount, and they are barred from manipulating search results to mislead users.
Why it matters: Platforms face stricter transparency mandates, directly impacting consumer trust and operational compliance.
Key detail: The amended Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, effective January 1, 2027, require discounted and prior price disclosures, ban manipulative search results, and mandate yearly dark-pattern audits.
Source: Deccan Herald
Next step: Audit your pricing algorithms and disclosure frameworks ahead of the deadline.

2. Ride-Hailing Platforms Seek GST Exemption
A front-page report in Economic Times says the app-based mobility industry has urged the government to exempt ride-hailing platforms from the five percent goods and services tax, arguing the levy unfairly burdens platforms that do not collect fares directly. The Internet and Mobile Association of India submitted a representation to the Goods and Services Tax Council stating that drivers collect fares while apps simply connect passengers, yet platforms must account for the tax under Section 9(5) of the CGST Act. The association highlighted conflicting rulings by state tax authorities, creating prolonged uncertainty for the sector.
Why it matters: Tax clarity is crucial for gig economy scalability and driver-platform economics.
Key detail: IAMAI urges the GST Council to exempt app-based mobility operators from the 5% levy, arguing platforms merely connect passengers and drivers rather than collecting fares directly.
Source: Economic Times
Next step: Engage with state tax authorities to resolve conflicting rulings.

3. Online Bond Platforms Push Insurance-Like Structures
A front-page report in Financial Express says online bond platform providers suggested insurance-like investment structures for debt securities to enable non-institutional investors to participate in corporate bond repos on Thursday in Mumbai. Panelists including Aditi Mittal of India-Bonds and Nikhil Aggarwal of Grip Invest discussed how universal premiums could lower costs to as low as 20 to 50 basis points while improving risk diversification across 20 to 30 issuers.
Why it matters: Democratizing corporate debt markets could unlock significant retail capital.
Key detail: Industry leaders propose universal premium structures lowering costs to 20-50 basis points, enabling non-institutional investors to participate in corporate bond repos.
Source: Financial Express
Next step: Evaluate risk diversification models for retail debt portfolios.

4. Samarthanam Launches Connect Platform
A front-page report in Deccan Herald says a new platform called Connect helps visually challenged students find verified volunteer scribes to assist with writing exams. The free online tool matches students with Aadhaar-verified volunteers within a local radius and is fully accessible with screen readers. Founder Mahantesh G Kivadasannavar stated the initiative aims to make education truly accessible for every student.
Why it matters: Accessibility tech expands talent pools and fulfills CSR commitments.
Key detail: The free, screen-reader-compatible tool matches visually challenged students with Aadhaar-verified volunteer scribes within local radii.
Source: Deccan Herald
Next step: Integrate accessible tools into campus support systems.

5. India Launches US Trade Export Platform
A front-page report in Mint says India has launched an online platform to connect its exporters with US buyers, aiming to boost bilateral trade to five hundred billion rupees by the end of the decade. The initiative comes as India and the US continue talks on a trade deal whose broad contours were agreed earlier this year.
Why it matters: Direct B2B matchmaking accelerates bilateral trade targets.
Key detail: The new portal connects Indian exporters with US buyers, supporting the goal of reaching ₹500 billion in trade by decade-end amid ongoing trade deal negotiations.
Source: Mint
Next step: Register early to secure buyer-seller matching priority.

6. RBI Governor Urges Responsible Fintech Data Use
A front-page report in Statesman says Reserve Bank of India Governor Sanjay Malhotra urged fintech firms to treat customer data as a fiduciary responsibility rather than a commercial asset. Speaking at the Global Fintech Fest 2026 in New Delhi, Malhotra emphasised that trust remains vital for India’s digital financial ecosystem and highlighted India’s position as the third largest global fintech hub. He also announced that the central bank will launch corporate bond tokenisation alongside SEBI and approved United Fintech Forum as a new self-regulatory organisation.
Why it matters: Fiduciary data handling remains the bedrock of India’s digital finance reputation.
Key detail: Governor Sanjay Malhotra emphasized trust over commercialization at Global Fintech Fest 2026, announcing upcoming corporate bond tokenisation and a new self-regulatory organisation.
Source: Statesman
Next step: Align data governance frameworks with fiduciary standards.

7. Brics Launches CONNECT Network
A front-page report in Business Standard says Brics countries launched Brics CONNECT, a cooperation network to forecast future skills and share labour‑market intelligence. The network, unveiled in New Delhi on 10 September 2026, will cover capacity building on social security, women’s workforce participation, skills and employability, and digital public infrastructure. Meetings in Hyderabad and Thiruvananthapuram earlier in the year focused on AI, gig workers and traditional knowledge, underscoring the group’s commitment to a future‑ready workforce.
Why it matters: Cross-border skills forecasting prepares workforces for AI-driven transitions.
Key detail: The network focuses on social security, women’s workforce participation, gig worker protections, and digital public infrastructure across member states.
Source: Business Standard
Next step: Monitor policy alignments for cross-border talent mobility.

8. Jharkhand High Court Orders Internet Restoration
A front-page report in Statesman says the Jharkhand High Court has sought responses from all internet service providers regarding the disruption of internet services in several areas of Ranchi during a drive to remove web of internet and cable wires from electricity poles. A division bench of Chief Justice M S Sonak and Justice Rajesh Shankar directed immediate restoration of affected connections and asked the service providers to furnish details of the dates when connections were disconnected, areas affected, number of connections severed and number of services restored so far.
Why it matters: Judicial oversight ensures telecom infrastructure maintenance doesn’t compromise digital rights.
Key detail: The court directed ISPs to immediately restore connections severed during wire-removal drives and submit detailed disruption reports.
Source: Statesman
Next step: Review field operations to prevent future service interruptions.

9. Satellite Spectrum Pricing Approved at 5%
Why it matters: Affordable spectrum access accelerates rural broadband and health-tech expansion.
Key detail: The Digital Communications Commission set usage fees at 5% of adjusted gross revenue, pending cabinet approval for providers like Starlink and One Web.
Source: Business Standard
Next step: Track regulatory clearances for next-gen connectivity rollout.

These developments underscore why rigorous print media monitoring is vital for strategic planning. Which of these shifts will impact your sector first? Share your insights below.

#MediaMonitoring #ECommerceRules #FintechIndia

A moving woman has finally met her fully funded Master’s scholarship at the number one school in the world for Development Studies. 😎

After dedicating October/November 2025 to February 2026 to applying for opportunities, I tried to prepare my mind for anything. Then the rejections started coming in, and I think they got to me a bit.

I mean, I’m a Cannes Lions-winning copywriter. I contributed to Nigeria and West Africa’s first-ever win at the most prestigious international festival of creativity. I’ve executed award-winning marketing communications and advertising campaigns, won pitches for local and international brands, consulted for startups on brand and communications strategy, led creative teams at some of the leading advertising agencies in Africa, led the communications team at Africa’s leading civic tech organization, mentored over 50 copywriters through my creative agency, founded a disability-inclusive creative talent management and advocacy company, led the team that created Nigeria’s first Albinism Advocacy Pageant, published the first-ever dictionary of disability-inclusive language, co-founded an adaptive clothing line for people with disabilities, started a disability-focused media company, and built a gamified disability education tech product over the last ten years of my professional career. Surely I could pitch myself well enough to win a scholarship? 😭

I was the person people came to when they needed to sharpen a pitch or proposal, review an application, or prepare for an interview. Turns out, I was about to be humbled. 

I started wondering if it was my 4.45 GPA. Or the nine-year gap since my BSc. Maybe I had waited too long. Maybe I was no longer the kind of candidate these opportunities were looking for. Maybe I even needed to scale my work or publish more research.

When I made the post below, I had stopped expecting anything else. But God, and His perfect humbling twists, started sending the YES-es. Every time I thought I had received my best offer, another one would come. 

I’ve achieved a lot of things in my life, but you see this particular win? I still can’t find the words. Just pure gratitude in my heart. God really did His big one. He truly, truly crowned all my hard work and sleepless nights with Sussex. 😉
