13 Pivotal Small Business Stories for Entrepreneurs
https://t.co/vTVfvcPKPi

This press review delivers essential media monitoring insights for founders and CFOs. According to Press Monitor's tracking of Indian publications, today's verified print coverage reveals how trade volatility, artificial intelligence, and state-backed capital are reshaping the entrepreneurial landscape. Here is the actionable breakdown.

1. UNCTAD Warns of Hormuz Disruption Risks
A front-page report in Asian Age says that the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development warns that disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz could disproportionately affect small and medium enterprises, which account for seventy percent of global employment. The report also notes that larger firms can better absorb trade shocks.
Why it matters: Global trade volatility directly impacts supply chains and working capital for smaller enterprises.
Key detail: Seventy percent of global employment relies on small and medium enterprises, making them highly vulnerable to shipping route disruptions.
Source: Asian Age
Next step: Diversify logistics partners and secure trade insurance. Tag @UNCTAD for updates.

2. Infosys Leader Drives Million-Startup Job Plan
A front-page report in Economic Times says Infosys non-executive chairman Nandan Nilekani argued that fostering millions of small businesses is vital for future employment as artificial intelligence displaces jobs at large corporations. Speaking at the Global Fintech Fest in Mumbai on Thursday, he noted that India must shift from relying on a handful of big tech firms to enabling widespread startup growth to build an economy resilient to automation. The discussion also featured Anthropic India managing director Irina Ghose, who highlighted India's pivotal role in developing global artificial intelligence strategies and product playbooks.
Why it matters: Shifting from corporate reliance to grassroots entrepreneurship builds economic resilience against automation.
Key detail: Nandan Nilekani emphasized at Global Fintech Fest that fostering millions of small businesses is vital for future employment as AI displaces large-corporate roles.
Source: Economic Times
Next step: Explore government startup grants and incubator programs. Tag @NandanNilekani.

3. Nilekani Highlights Small Firm Job Creation
A front-page report in Financial Express says that Infosys founder N. R. Narayanan announced that the next layer of the Finternet will be powered by artificial intelligence, allowing AI agents to convert invoices into tokenised assets and sell them to multiple lenders. The system would store details like quantity, quality, warehouse location and insurance status of produce, giving farmers greater bargaining power and enabling small businesses to secure finance that previously required large enterprises. Nilekani also warned that AI could displace jobs in structured roles, urging a shift toward an economy of millions of small businesses.
Why it matters: Decentralized enterprise models offer sustainable career pathways beyond traditional tech giants.
Key detail: Large companies may reduce headcount in the AI age, positioning small enterprises as the primary employers of tomorrow.
Source: Business Line
Next step: Build scalable micro-business frameworks. Tag @Infosys.

4. AI Tokens Empower Farmers and SMEs
A front-page report in The Pioneer says the Chhattisgarh Government has approved a 500-crore Chief Minister Startup and NIPUN Mission for five years along with the Chhattisgarh Export Promotion Policy 2026-30. The Startup Mission will establish Entrepreneurship Development Centres in all 33 districts and 100 Emerging Technology Labs to help youth become entrepreneurs. Through the NIPUN JOB Engine, youth will receive industry-based training to create better employment opportunities.
Why it matters: Finternet infrastructure democratizes access to credit and asset digitization for rural entrepreneurs.
Key detail: AI agents can convert invoices into tokenised assets, allowing farmers and small traders to sell to multiple lenders while securing finance previously reserved for large corporations.
Source: Financial Express
Next step: Adopt digital invoicing and explore tokenisation platforms. Tag @NarendranR.

5. Chhattisgarh Approves ₹500 Crore Startup Mission
A front-page report in Business Line says Uttar Pradesh, Telangana, Gujarat, and West Bengal boast the top 10 districts for unincorporated establishments, with North Twenty-Four Parganas leading at 16 lakh units, according to the first-ever district-level estimates released by the National Statistical Office on Thursday. The report from the Annual Survey of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises covers 757 of 770 districts and reveals that the top 10 districts account for about one-tenth of total establishments, workers, and Gross Value Added, while one-third of districts have more than one lakh informal enterprises each. Significant regional patterns in female entrepreneurship show Telangana, Manipur, and Meghalaya have the highest share of female-led establishments, with Mizoram reporting at least 50 per cent female-owned proprietary establishments in each district.
Why it matters: State-level capital injection accelerates regional innovation hubs and youth employment.
Key detail: The Chief Minister Startup and NIPUN Mission will establish Entrepreneurship Development Centres across all 33 districts alongside 100 Emerging Technology Labs.
Source: The Pioneer
Next step: Register for district-level incubator cohorts. Tag @CGGovernment.

6. UP Ranks Among Top Districts for Unincorporated Firms
A front-page report in Free Press Journal says the Uttar Pradesh government is launching a major financial empowerment drive to help one crore women become economically independent through self-help groups. Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya outlined the Uttar Pradesh Women Entrepreneur Scheme, which will provide over one crore eligible women with interest-free loans totalling one lakh rupees across three instalments. The initiative also includes funding for livestock purchases, affordable electric rickshaws, and technology support like agricultural drones to boost sustainable rural incomes.
Why it matters: Informal sector growth signals robust grassroots commerce but highlights regulatory modernization needs.
Key detail: North Twenty-Four Parganas leads with 16 lakh units, while Telangana and Mizoram show exceptional female-led establishment rates.
Source: Business Line
Next step: Formalize operations to unlock MSME benefits. Tag @NSOIndia.

A front-page report in The Pioneer says the Indian People's Forum Bihar Council hosted a special interaction with Sushri Shreyasi Singh, Minister for Industries and Sports, Government of Bihar, at India Club in Dubai. The event brought together prominent members of the Bihar diaspora, business leaders, and senior Government officials to explore opportunities for investment, entrepreneurship, employment, and stronger India-UAE partnerships. Kundan Kumar, IAS, Secretary of the Department of Industries, Government of Bihar, complimented the Minister's vision with an overview of Bihar's economic and infrastructure transformation across power, manufacturing, agriculture, and industrial infrastructure.
Why it matters: Diaspora engagement bridges international capital with domestic manufacturing and infrastructure goals.
Key detail: Industry Secretary Kundan Kumar outlined Bihar's transformation in power, agriculture, and industrial infrastructure to UAE investors.
Source: The Pioneer
Next step: Connect with export promotion councils. Tag @BiharGovt.

8. UP Targets One Crore Lakhpati Didis
A front-page report in The Pioneer says the West Bengal State Assembly passed the West Bengal Universities and Colleges (Administration and Regulation) Amendment Bill 2026 by voice vote on Thursday. The bill enables the transfer of university teachers and non-teaching staff to other institutions, with Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari stating it would balance institutional autonomy with staff accountability.
Why it matters: Massive financial inclusion drives empower rural women to launch sustainable micro-enterprises.
Key detail: Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya announced interest-free loans totalling one lakh rupees across three instalments, plus funding for livestock and agricultural drones.
Source: Free Press Journal
Next step: Apply through local self-help group networks. Tag @KPMaurya.

9. PM-SETU Launches ₹482 Crore ITI Upgrade
Why it matters: Vocational training modernization directly addresses the industry-ready skills gap for new graduates.
Key detail: The scheme upgrades ITIs into skill hubs with 74.7 per cent central funding, targeting seventy-five per cent graduate employment placement.
Source: State Times
Next step: Enroll in upgraded technical certification tracks. Tag @SkillIndia.

10. Assam Transitioning to Tech Creator State
A front-page report in Free Press Journal says Assam Chief Minister Dr Himanta Biswa Sarma called for the state to transition from a technology consumer to a creator during the launch of the MC? IGNITE outreach programme at IIT Guwahati on Thursday. The event featured the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding between MC? and IIT Guwahati and the inauguration of the MC? Co-Working Node in Guwahati. The MC? initiative brings together the MC? Foundation, IIT Guwahati, Oil India Limited, and Numaligarh Refinery Limited to advance innovation and entrepreneurship in energy and related sectors.
Why it matters: Regional focus on innovation shifts states from passive technology adoption to active product development.
Key detail: MC? IGNITE programme partners with IIT Guwahati, Oil India Limited, and Numaligarh Refinery to advance energy-sector entrepreneurship.
Source: Free Press Journal
Next step: Submit proposals to the new Co-Working Node. Tag @AssamGovt.

11. India Needs Strategic Youth Empowerment
A front-page report in State Times says India's large young population must be supported by quality education, meaningful employment, and entrepreneurship opportunities to become a national strength. The article highlights challenges such as unequal opportunity distribution, skill gaps in metropolitan and rural areas, and social issues like substance abuse and cybercrime affecting youth. It emphasizes that economic transformation depends on investing in human resources and ensuring every young Indian can realize their potential.
Why it matters: Human capital investment remains the cornerstone of demographic dividend realization and economic stability.
Key detail: Addressing skill gaps, unequal opportunity distribution, and cybercrime risks requires coordinated policy action and private sector mentorship.
Source: State Times
Next step: Partner with local edtech providers for upskilling. Tag @YouthEmpowerment.

12. Pendharkar College Hosts Startup Camp
A front-page report in Business Line says K V Pendharkar College of Arts, Science and Commerce (Autonomous) organized the Entrepreneurship Awareness Camp 2026 in Dombivli through its Centre for Research, Innovation and Entrepreneurship. Industry experts including Mr Niladri Roy and Dr Ravinder Varma urged students to become job creators, and Mr Harshal Lavangare announced upcoming initiatives such as a BARC workshop and the launch of the college film society, The Bioscope Bugs. In a separate event, the Gujarat Tourism Corporation's Vadnagar Shravanotsav at Sharmishtha Lake attracted over thirty eight thousand one hundred nineteen visitors across three Sundays from August 16 to August 30, featuring devotional programmes, classical performances and a light-and-sound show.
Why it matters: Academic institutions are rapidly evolving into innovation ecosystems that validate student ideas before market entry.
Key detail: Industry experts Niladri Roy and Ravinder Varma guided students through problem-solving workshops, with upcoming BARC research collaborations announced.
Source: Business Line
Next step: Join campus incubator pitch days. Tag @PendharkarCollege.

13. University of Jammu Announces Three Initiatives
A front-page report in State Times says the University of Jammu has strengthened industry academic collaboration through the Centre for IT Enabled Services and Emerging Technologies. Three major initiatives were introduced, including a startup conclave, a structured mentorship programme, and a joint intelligence project focused on research and capacity building. Vice Chancellor Professor Umesh Rai reaffirmed the university commitment to establishing a leading hub for technology innovation and entrepreneurship.
Why it matters: Higher education leadership is formalizing industry-academia pipelines to accelerate commercial research.
Key detail: VC Umesh Rai launched a startup conclave, structured mentorship programme, and joint intelligence project focused on capacity building.

text:
As Persian Gulf states request for an urgent meeting with Iran, Afonso de Albuquerque examines how simultaneous control of Hormuz and Bab al Mandeb forces regional powers into diplomatic submission:

The monsoon mist over the coastal hills of Salalah had begun to clear, revealing the gray expanse of the Arabian Sea. In the quiet courtyard of a villa overlooking the water, Tariq smoothed a satellite chart across the timber table. Across from him sat Afonso de Albuquerque, his posture unyielding, his eyes fixed not on the digital screen displaying live vessel movements, but on the raw contours of the coastline.

Below them in the Omani coastal city, diplomatic convoys were arriving. Foreign ministers from across the Persian Gulf had gathered for urgent talks with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, hosted by Oman. The world viewed the meeting as a sudden political concession, a surprising scramble by the Gulf monarchies to secure a temporary passage agreement through the Strait of Hormuz after months of naval disruption.

"They're calling it a diplomatic breakthrough," Tariq said, tapping the screen where small green icons of oil tankers sat motionless outside the strait. "The regional ministers aren't here because they've changed their political ideology. They're here because they can't move a single barrel of oil without Tehran's consent."

Albuquerque didn't look at the green icons. He reached out with a weather beaten finger, tracing the coast from the narrow mouth of Ormuz, down past the Omani promontory, around the tip of Yemen, and into the narrow neck of Bab al Mandeb.

"You think you're witnessing a diplomatic negotiation," Albuquerque said softly, his voice carrying the dry rasp of salt and old iron. "You're not. You're witnessing the closing of a vault. One key in Ormuz doesn't lock a house if the back door remains open. But when an aligned force holds the key to Bab al Mandeb, the house becomes a cell."

"It isn't the same actor," Tariq countered, adjusting his spectacles. "Tehran controls Hormuz directly with fast attack craft and coastal batteries. In the south, it's Ansarullah holding the Yemeni coast down to Mocha. They're separate entities with distinct domestic interests."

"Separate hands, single vice," Albuquerque replied, leaning back. "When I entered these waters in 1507, the Sultan of Ormuz believed his wealth made him invincible. He collected customs from every merchant sailing between India and Basra. He thought if I blocked his harbour, his trade would simply flow through the Red Sea to Cairo and Venice. So I sailed for Aden. I wanted both gates. I failed at Aden in 1513, and because I failed, trade bled out through the Red Sea for another century. If you leave one gate open, your enemy will find a way to breathe."

Tariq gestured toward the western edge of the Arabian Peninsula on the screen. "That was five hundred years ago. Modern states have inland infrastructure. Saudi Arabia built the East West Pipeline specifically to bypass Hormuz. It pumps millions of barrels a day straight across the desert to Yanbu on the Red Sea. They thought that pipeline was their insurance policy against a blockade at Hormuz."

"And where do those ships go once they load at Yanbu?" Albuquerque asked, his eyes narrowing.

"They sail south through Bab al Mandeb into the Indian Ocean to reach buyers in Asia," Tariq said. He stopped. The implication hung in the damp morning air.

"Exactly," Albuquerque said, a cold smile touching his lips. "The pipeline doesn't free them. It merely moves the cargo from one narrow door to another. If Ansarullah shuts Bab al Mandeb with anti ship missiles from the Yemeni hills, Yanbu becomes a dead end. The tankers can turn north toward Suez, but that adds thousands of kilometres, massive transit fees, and leaves them stranded in the Mediterranean far from their primary Asian markets. The pipeline didn't eliminate the chokepoint. It simply created a longer, more expensive route to the second lock."

"Western navies tried to break the blockade at Bab al Mandeb," Tariq noted, picking up a pen. "They sent carrier groups. They fired precision weapons at radar sites along the Red Sea coast for months."

"And yet the merchant ships aren't sailing," Albuquerque said. "Why?"

"Insurance," Tariq answered quietly. "Commercial maritime insurers won't underwrite a tanker when a $5,000 drone or a mobile shore missile can cause a $50 million hull loss. Superpower navies can protect their own warships, but they can't guarantee zero risk for a thousand commercial vessels a month in a channel twenty kilometres wide."

"Then the naval fleet is irrelevant to the merchant," Albuquerque said flatly. "In 1507, I didn't need to sink every vessel in the Gulf. I only needed to demonstrate that no vessel could pass without my cartaz, my pass of safe conduct. Control of a strait isn't measured by how many warships you place in the water. It's measured by whether a merchant captain believes he'll reach his destination if he ignores your command."

He tapped the map again, striking the two straits in sequence.

"Look at the geometry," Albuquerque continued. "If Iran locks Hormuz alone, the Gulf monarchies can endure a short crisis. They can draw down financial reserves, reroute critical imports through Red Sea ports, and press their external allies for military intervention. Hormuz alone is a tactical crisis. But when Ansarullah advances down the Red Sea coast and closes Bab al Mandeb simultaneously, the entire peninsula is enclosed in a double sea lock. Imports of food and equipment stall at both entrances. Energy exports cease. The peninsula becomes an island without a port."

"That's why they're in Salalah today," Tariq realised aloud. "It's not just about energy prices. The regional states aren't trying to win a war; they're trying to prevent complete economic paralysis. They've realised that external naval power can't reopen two narrow straits at the same time against cheap, distributed coastal weapons."

"When physical force cannot clear the gates, geography dictates the diplomacy," Albuquerque said. "The ministers haven't come to Oman to negotiate from strength. They've come to ask Araghchi for the terms of transit. They want a managed agreement where ships enter through Iranian territorial waters and exit through Omani space under an arrangement Tehran approves."

"They're surrendering sovereign maritime rights to secure physical movement," Tariq said softly.

"They're submitting to the law of the chokepoint," Albuquerque corrected him. "Sovereignty on paper means nothing when your ships are anchored in place. In my time, when the rulers of Ormuz realised I held the entrance to the ocean, they didn't offer me battle. They offered me tribute. They paid for the privilege of using the waters that sat on their own doorstep."

Tariq looked down at the gathering convoy of vehicles in the valley below. "Is there any counter strategy? If a coalition can't break a dual chokepoint by naval force, what breaks it?"

"Only land," Albuquerque said. "Or time. A sea lock can only be broken if an enemy marches along the shore and physically occupies the high ground where the weapons sit. That's why I seized Goa and built fortresses on land. You can't control a strait permanently from the water alone; you must own the shore. If your allies aren't willing to land tens of thousands of men on the Yemeni crags and the Iranian cliffs to occupy those hills, then the sea belongs to whoever holds the shoreline."

"And no one has the political will for a land invasion of that scale," Tariq admitted. "The cost would dwarf the value of the trade."

"Which means the dual lock holds," Albuquerque said, leaning over the chart one last time. "You started this morning believing that today's meeting in Salalah was a sudden political choice made by nervous diplomats. It wasn't. It was an arithmetic certainty. When two gates lock the same sea, the person inside the vault doesn't choose whether to negotiate. He only chooses how much he's willing to pay to turn the key."

Tariq closed his notebook as the sun rose higher over the Arabian Sea. Below them, the meeting room doors opened, and the representatives walked in to meet the Iranian delegation, exactly where geography had dictated they must stand.

---

Afonso de Albuquerque (1453-1515) was a Portuguese naval commander who built Portugal's Asian trade empire in the Indian Ocean by seizing strategic ports including Goa, Malacca, and Ormuz.

Persian Gulf states have requested an urgent meeting in Oman with Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi to discuss reopening the Strait of Hormuz after Ansarullah/Houthis recently took control of the Bab al Mandeb Strait.

text:
!26 决策/博弈论 Game Theory
1) 你帮助过的人，和帮助过你的人，应该向谁求助？

谁更有可能帮助你？
二战期间，一对犹太兄弟想要逃出纳粹德国，他们打算在父亲的熟人中，找一个最有可能帮助他们的人。
老大想起了一个银行家，父亲生前曾多次帮助过他；老二想起了一个木材商，这个人曾多次帮自己家的忙。
兄弟俩的意见发生了分歧，到底是“以前你帮助过的人”更可能反过来帮助你呢？还是“帮助过你的人”更可能再次帮助你呢？
时间紧急，兄弟俩决定分头求救，各自逃亡。你认为谁最有可能成功逃离呢？

“你帮助过银行家”和“银行家会来帮你”，这两件事表面上有“知恩图报”的关系，但“知恩图报”只是一个道德标准，并不是对现实的总结。事实上，“知恩图报”只出现在不重要的事上，你不可能指望别人冒着生命危险来帮助你。

也就是说，“你帮助过银行家”和“银行家会来帮你”就像两次抛硬币，是两个孤立事件，得到“银行家帮助”的概率和“任何一个陌生人帮助”的概率是一样的。

老大的命运，可想而知。相反，“木材商曾多次帮助过你”和“木材商还会继续帮助过你”，这显然更可能是连续发生、有内在原因的系列事件。

当然，我们已经没有时间搞清楚，为什么这个木材商会三番五次地帮助你，也许他就是天使，也许他才是你的亲爸爸，Whatever，反正你现在只要知道，他帮助你的概率，肯定比任何一个人都高。

2) 37% Rule

在现实中，信息和选项，往往不是同时铺开在我们眼前让我们选的，而是随着时间推移逐步出现的，我们怎么能确定以后会不会出现更好的选项呢？我们是不是需要不停地搜索和等待？选择配偶、找工作，买入一只股票的时机选择，都属于这一类的问题：万一以后遇到更好的呢？万一还没有到底部呢？

这个原理来自决策学里一个经典的问题。它的通俗版本是这样的——假设你经过一片西瓜地，只能走一次，不能回头，你怎么才能摘到整片西瓜地里那个最大的西瓜？

统计学家计算出来的最优策略是一个百分数，37%，什么意思呢？就是假设这个瓜田一共100个西瓜，在经过前37个西瓜的时候，不要做决定，光做一件事，就是测量和记录它们每个的大小。

在37个西瓜之后，如果接下来看到一个西瓜比以前看到过的那些都大，那就选择这个西瓜，这种情况下，你摘到最大西瓜的概率是最大的。

比如一个女青年，从18岁开始找对象，设定的目标是在40岁之前结婚，那么根据37%规则，她的阶段分割点是26.1岁。

在数学家看来，这个女青年的最佳择偶策略是这样的。26.1岁之前是观察期，她应该只交往不结婚，但是必须要记住在交往的男生中间，自己最喜欢的是哪个。26.1岁之后是决策期，再结交新的对象，一旦遇到一个比原来认为的最好的那个还好，或者和那个人差不多一样好的男人，就应该马上把他拿下，和他结婚。

当然了，如果你相信世界上有一个你唯一的真命天子，你一定要等到他出现，这是价值观问题，那这套算法对你不适用。但是如果你相信，结婚不过是一个择优的过程，和我们说的在西瓜地里捡一个最大的西瓜本质上一样，那这个37%原则对你就是有用的。

当然啦，我不是建议你要相信这套算法。我今天只是想说，理性的人，不是那种要穷尽理性的人，而是应该知道什么时候停止的人。

开普勒，就是那个总结了“行星运动三大定律”的人，他在寻找他的第二任夫人时，用的方法是面试，可效果并不好，因为最适合的人出现时，他犹豫了，可等他再回头，人家早就名花有主了。

于是，开普勒将其总结成一个数学问题：如果选项既定，你只能按顺序一个个地选择，无法NG，如何最大程度地挑出最优答案？

这个问题后来被称为“最优停止理论”，也有人叫“秘书问题”，因为那时招秘书也没个手机联系，必须当场拍板决定。

这个问题的适用场景，除了找对象、招聘之外，还有逛街买东西、买房，甚至像选秀节目里的导师选学员。
其实解决思路并不难：头几个面试对象，不急着选择，而是通过观察他们的表现来，判断整体候选人的水平（所以选秀节目先出场的，当炮灰的可能性很大），心中有数后，再发现合适的，就一举拿下。

难点在于，观察的时间太长，浪费选择机会，观察的时间太短，又定不了优秀的标准。所以关键是定“观察量”。

很多人都觉得，这怎么可能有答案，明明是一个心态或者性格偏好问题。

但实际上，“最优停止法”的比例，真的有一个基于数学计算的答案：1/e≈ 36.8 %。
公式太吓人，我就不列了。你也可以用“穷举法”，列出N等于任何自然数的情况，你会发现，N越大，这个最优比例越接近36.8%

有了这个比例，我们就找到了一个解决“选择恐惧症”的科学方法，以“谈恋爱”为例：

第一步，估算你最多可能会谈多少次恋爱；
第二步，前面36.8%的“观察期”对象，只谈不定；
第三步，在36.8%之后，只要出现任何一个对象优于观察期的最优对象，Bingo，就是你了！
3) 不是落后者要学习领先者，而是领先者要学习落后者

美洲杯帆船赛是一个古老而有趣的比赛。比赛规则很特别，上届冠军的俱乐部自动有一艘船进决赛，而其他各队比赛争夺一个向冠军挑战的资格。此赛事自从1851创办一直到1980年，冠军居然都是美国队。
帆船比赛特别讲究“落后者创新”。1983年美国队首次卫冕失利过程中的一场比赛，给了我们一个有意思的例子。

这场比赛是最后7局4胜决赛的第5场，此前美国队 Liberty 号以3：1领先澳大利亚的 Australia II 号。比赛开始之前人们甚至已经准备好庆祝美国人延续132年连胜的历史时刻了。

结果比赛中还是 Liberty 号领先。澳大利亚人一看继续这么玩下去冠军肯定没有了，必须赌一把。Australia II 号变道了航线的左侧，希望能碰上有利的风向。

这时候 Liberty 的正确应对策略是什么呢？是跟着变。不管航线左侧风向是否真的有利，只要我们两个的条件能保持一样，那么最后肯定还是我赢，因为现在我领先。哪怕你的选择 是错误的，为了确保胜利我也必须做跟你同样的选择。所以在这种一对一的帆船比赛中不是落后者学习领先者，而是领先者学习落后者。

然而 Liberty 的船长 Dennis Conner 选择了留在右侧航线！这个看上去很直觉，实则不符合帆船比赛竞争规律的错误使他青史留名：Australia II 号赌赢了，Liberty 再输两场之后，美洲杯冠军终于易手。

所以不是落后者要学习领先者，而是领先者要学习落后者。比如你是一家股票走势预测的公司，你们公司的业绩取决于你预测准确率的年度排名。十个月过去了，你现在排第一。为了保证年底的时候你排第一，这时候你应该采取什么策略？答案是直接抄袭其他人的预测。

面对两难选择的时候，用博弈论逆向推理，是让自己生活更有效率、决策更正确的办法。

1. 毕业季的时候，大学生收到的offer经常带有时间限制，要求几天内必须明确答复，否则过期作废。用博弈论分析这种状况你会发现，选择这种策略对公司是没有好处的，因为只有某个大学生在没有信心得到别的工作的情况下，才会接受这种恐吓，有实力的公司不会选择这么做的，遇到这种情况你大可以沉住气。

2．当你学的专业和你喜欢的行业不对口的时候，不要急着抛弃现在的专业去追求梦想。任何行业经过充分的博弈之后，其实机会都差不多。你选择一个行业的时候，需要考虑的并不是你喜不喜欢它，而是你和已经在这个行业里的人相比，是不是更喜欢。

4) 人什么时候应该孤注一掷，什么时候可以耐心沉着？

这是一个一个很常见的选择问题，先说大家可能有的直觉：当然是有资本可以赌的人，应该孤注一掷。没有资本的人，处于劣势的人，应该小心翼翼，耐心沉着，因为输不起嘛。这是直觉告诉我们的。也符合我们的观察。越有钱的人胆子越大，越穷的人越小心。

但是如果稍加理性分析，你会发现，答案也许正好相反。为什么？我们来看一个例子。

比如我是一个高尔夫球的外行，和一个高尔夫球世界冠军比赛，我会怎么比？我会说，我们打满全场18个洞吗？不会的，因为水平差距太大，比多了肯定输嘛。所以，如果我有机会决定赛制，我应该说，咱俩就比打一个洞，一杆定输赢。因为我还有可能碰巧赢一把，你可以赌世界冠军偶然失手。

你看，恰恰是弱者应该孤注一掷。真和我们的直觉相反。

再举一个例子。比如进赌场，正规的赌场，是有概率优势的，那是数学家帮忙算出来的。而且那是合法的，是明明白白地写在他们的执照里的。那你应该怎么赌呢？如果你要分次下注，那概率就起作用了，你只会稳定地逐渐输光，一点机会也没有。所以你非得进，你最聪明的办法，是全部押上，一次性下注，接受命运的裁决，你还有一点点机会。就这么简单。越是没有资源的人，越应该孤注一掷。

这个道理，说出来感觉很平常。但是，如果真的理解了，你会发现，这是世界留的一个后门。
作为小人物，我们经常会觉得，这个世界没给我们留什么机会。因为表面看起来，有资源的人，有优势的人，往往会获得更多的资源，占据更大的优势。所谓“马太效应”嘛。

但真的是这样吗？不是啊。我们前面刚刚讲了啊，有优势的人，应该等待概率自己慢慢地稳定起作用，这是他们保持优势最好的最理性的策略啊。一个高尔夫球高手，他应该和我多打几把。他才不愿意搞什么激进策略。正常和我打，他就能赢。
但这同时也就意味着，有优势的人，优势本身就是他们的绳索，他们的行动天然是没有什么勇气的，那自然也就不会有什么惊喜。因为他们不赌运气。所以，不管他们优势多大，他们也拦不住那些敢赌一把的黑马。

这就是这个世界的后门啊、这就是这个世界内含的一个逻辑悖论啊。这个世界就是靠这个后门和逻辑悖论来完成结构更替，避免被锁死的。避免那些已经享有优势的人，持续享有优势。

举个例子。我们经常看到一个现象，一个班里的同学，学习成绩最好的学霸，将来的发展往往只是中上水平，最有成就的人，往往是班上成绩不怎么样的人。为啥？有人说这是因为学霸读书读傻了，或者干脆说读书无用。这当然是瞎分析。

用今天说的这个规律，我们就明白了，这是理性选择的结果。班上成绩最好的同学，往往选择去了那些稳定的地方，这更有助于他们把自己智力优势、先发优势稳定地发挥出来，当然，也就不太可能有什么意外之喜，往往会过比较不错但是平淡的一生，这是他们的理性选择，而不是他们的无奈。

而那些有大惊喜的人呢？你看起来他们起点低，比如创业者一般原本处在主流边缘，但是他们的成就的实质，往往是因为和命运赌了一把的结果。绝大多数人在这样的赌局里都输了，少数赢了的人比较显眼而已。

你看，这个世界多公平。每个人的资源和禀赋不一样，也就是说，他成功的概率不一样。所以就分化啦，有的人会更多地利用概率躲过不确定性，这就是学霸的道路，有的人躲过概率更多地拥抱不确定性，这就是创业者的道路。各得其所。大家都有机会。

好，那我们再来看一种选择。刚才的选择你可以在概率和运气之间搞平衡。但还有一种选择，就是没有什么概率依据的选择。什么选择没有概率依据？就是那种很重大的，甚至一生只有一两次的选择啊。

像关键时刻的职业选择，要不要和这个人结婚的婚姻选择等等。每个人在面对这种选择的时候，其实都面临无穷丰富的因素，每一片树叶都不一样、每个人的因素都不一样，别人的经验，过往的概率，参考价值不大。

比如说，你按照概率选择结婚对象，历史数据表明，哪个省的人、哪个学校毕业的人、哪种职业的人、哪种财产状况的人、甚至是手机上装了什么App的人，婚后的幸福指数较高，但这对你有啥价值呢？你面对的是具体的人。

这种概率在宏观上有意义，但是一旦具体到个人，结婚对象一旦选错，对人的生活质量的影响是决定性的，怎么选，依据多大的概率选。你都有可能遇到一个对的人，也有可能遇到一个很渣的人，一旦遇到，对你来说就是100%。所以，对于这种重大选择，概率没啥用。单一事件没有概率可言。

那该怎么办呢？
王烁老师介绍了一种选法，这是来自于哲学家和概率学家查尔斯·佩尔斯的建议，原话是这样的：“在做一次性选择时，逻辑要求我们的利益不再受限于自身，不能锁定于自己的命运中，而必须拥抱整个社群；同样，社群利益也不能受限于自身，而必须扩展到所有人类。它必须超越这个时代，超越所有边界。逻辑植根于社会原则。”

听起来有点不知所云，解释一下：
你想，对于我们每个人来说，那些重大的一次性的选择，当然很难，不可重复，没有可靠的依据。但是如果跳出来呢？跳到整个群体、整个人类、全部时空，那就不是一次的选择了，那是可重复的选择。多少人生老病死，多少人悲欢离合，对人类群体来说，那是司空见惯的。假设你代表整个群体，那怎么选，就有依据了啊。

举个例子。比如，我要是得了某一种病，医生说有两个治疗方案，各有利弊、各有风险，你自己选，我是没有能力选的，因为任何风险要是落到我自己身上，那就是100%，怎么选都不保险。这个时候聪明的选法，就是反过来问医生，假设我们超越边界，回到群体，假设你给整个这个病人群体建议一个治疗方案，你会怎么选？
医生说怎么选，那就这么选啊。即使最终证明选错了，你也是为这个病的群体，贡献了一个治疗样本，从群体的角度来看，还是有收益的。这个收益多多少少，会以各种方式落到个体上。
再比如说，做一个商业上的重大选择。从公司的利益来看，确实各有利弊，无从决策。那就跳出来，跳到社会公众的高度，再来看怎么选。这样选，即使错了，客观上也是增进了群体的利益，群体的利益，多多少少还是会回馈到个体的身上。

你可能会觉得，这是在唱高调，但是，你不妨想想，如果一家企业，在重大选择关头，一直是按照公共利益最大化来做选择的，这家公司，不见得会大成，但是大败的机会确实也小了。个人也是一样啊，从个体的角度来说，不见得恶有恶报善有善报，但是从群体的角度来说，做善事肯定比做恶事，收益要大。
所以，学完了王烁老师这几节关于人生选择的课程，我的感慨是：
所有的选择难题，本质上都是视野狭窄带来的。偏好不够用了，那就扩展一下看看概率。概率不够用了，那就扩展一下看看运气。运气也看不清了，那就扩展一下看看公共利益。甚至公共利益也看不清，那就扩展一下，想想自己想成为什么样的人。
总之，格局越大，选择就越容易。

5) 问三次价格策略

这个是个100%根据我个人经验的出来的结论。由于我旅行的时候，经常需要货比三家，购买服务。比如说租个摩托车，或者定个一日游，什么的。
现实生活中，不像网购，你能一眼就横向对比很多家店铺的价格。这时候，如果问的商家太多，就是浪费是时间精力，潜在能省下来的钱，抵不上我因此浪费时间精力。

刚开始我还是小白的的时候，犯的错误就是上来就购买第一家的。经常发现，明明就是多走几步外的另一家商铺，要便宜好多。我就很懊悔没有多花几秒钟的时间，多问一嘴的事，就可以省下来安么多钱。

后来，随着经验见长，终于得出来的最优解。就是，不论一共有多少商铺，在购买任何东西的时候，一定要问三家。
不用多，绝对不能少于三家。这样，你选一个性价比最高最合适的，就行了。
而且记住，永远不要上来就选第一家。

SpaceX ($SPCX) has reportedly closed a major new compute hosting agreement that could add more than $13 billion in annual recurring revenue.

Speaking at Goldman Sachs’ Communacopia and Technology Conference, SpaceX CFO Bret Johnsen said the new deal will generate roughly $1.11 billion per month starting Dec. 1.

Johnsen said the agreement gives SpaceX even more confidence in its goal of reaching $100 billion in annual recurring revenue by the end of 2026.

SpaceX did not disclose the customer or provide additional details about the agreement. The company already has compute arrangements involving Alphabet and Anthropic as it expands beyond launch services and satellite connectivity.

The new contract highlights how important AI infrastructure and compute hosting are becoming to SpaceX’s broader business. Elon Musk has also said there is a “non-zero chance” the company could eventually reach $1 trillion in annual revenue by 2030.

X Prize Foundation Executive Chairman Peter Diamandis has argued that SpaceX could ultimately reach a $10 trillion valuation, describing the company’s expanding launch, communications and computing infrastructure as operating at a “civilizational” scale.

SpaceX is also continuing to expand Starlink. The company recently introduced its fourth-generation router with Wi-Fi 7, improved performance in congested areas and greater water resistance.

At the same time, SpaceX is developing its planned Starbase Louisiana facility and has said residents near the future spaceport will be offered Starlink service at half price. Shares of SpaceX were trading around $149 following the latest update.

text:
Ukraine Sees Russian-Iranian Sanctions Networks Converging As US Targets Tankers

The recent US destruction of five Iranian oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz has exposed more than the widening confrontation between Washington and Tehran.

It has highlighted an increasingly intertwined sanctions-evasion system linking Iran and Russia -- a network of ships, managers, intermediaries, and trading routes that Ukrainian officials and US sanctions experts say the West can no longer treat as two separate problems.

Three of the five tankers -- Kaviz, Charminar, and Riesco -- had direct links to Russia’s shadow oil fleet, according to Vladyslav Vlasiuk, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s sanctions commissioner.

All three transported Russian oil and called at Russian ports, Vlasiuk told RFE/RL on September 10. Riesco, he said, carried both Russian and Iranian oil and participated in ship-to-ship transfers involving other sanctioned vessels.

“Russia and Iran have a long history of cooperation, and their sanctions-evasion networks increasingly overlap,” Vlasiuk said.

Philip Luck, director of the Economics Program at the Center for Strategic and International Studies and a former deputy chief economist at the US State Department, described the system more bluntly: “There’s not a Russian shadow fleet and Iranian shadow fleet. There’s one shadow fleet that is facilitating Iranian oil sales and Russian oil sales.”

Tankers Tied To Moscow

Kaviz operated between the Russian ports of Ust-Luga and Novorossiysk and had a history of switching off its automatic identification system, which allows authorities and other vessels to track ships. Vlasiuk linked it to Fractal Marine DMCC, a network involved in moving Russian oil after Western sanctions were imposed.

Charminar repeatedly called at Russian ports, including Ust-Luga, Primorsk, Vysotsk, and St. Petersburg. Vlasiuk said it was connected to a shipping network controlled by Iranian oil businessman Mohammad Hossein Shamkhani.

After Britain sanctioned Fractal Marine, vessels connected to the network were transferred to other managers while their Russian oil operations continued, Vlasiuk said.

Riesco illustrates the two-way nature of the trade. It carried both Russian and Iranian oil and participated in ship-to-ship transfers involving other sanctioned vessels.

All three tankers are sanctioned by Ukraine and the United States, according to Vlasiuk. Kaviz is also sanctioned by the European Union, Britain, Canada, and Switzerland.

Vlasiuk did not estimate how much revenue the vessels generated for Russia. Their importance, he said, lies in helping Russian oil reach global markets despite Western restrictions.

“These vessels were part of the infrastructure that enabled Russian oil to keep reaching the global market despite sanctions, allowing Russia to preserve a major source of revenue,” he said.

For Ukraine, that infrastructure is itself a target. “The same vessels, masters, managers, intermediaries and shipping routes are used to transport both Russian and Iranian oil,” Vlasiuk said.

One Fleet, Two Oil Trades

Luck said the implications extend beyond the three ships because Russia and Iran sell oil to many of the same markets. That creates a challenge for sanctions policymakers: measures aimed at one country’s oil trade may affect the other because the logistics are shared.

“So anything, if you want to put more pressure on Iran, you’re gonna be putting more pressure on Russia,” Luck said. “And if you put more pressure on Russia, you’re putting more pressure on Iran. It’s the exact same problem.”

The issue has become more urgent as Washington combines economic pressure on Tehran with direct military action. The US says the Iranian tankers were part of a shadow network helping finance Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and its proxies. The strikes followed Iranian attacks on US naval forces, while Secretary of State Marco Rubio has warned that Washington will respond to further attacks.

The confrontation has also increased pressure on energy markets. Washington and Tehran are seeking influence over the Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly one-fifth of global oil supplies passed before the war.

For Kyiv, the tanker strikes show why maritime networks have become an increasingly important sanctions target. “As long as this infrastructure remains operational, opportunities to evade sanctions will remain,” Vlasiuk said.

Ukraine Sees A Wider Russia-Iran Link
The episode comes as Washington considers expanding its ability to target Russia’s energy revenues and the networks helping Moscow evade sanctions.

The Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 passed the Senate on August 7 by 86-11. It targets Russia’s shadow fleet, imposes additional sanctions on Russian officials and financial institutions, and authorizes the president to impose duties of up to 100 percent on goods from major purchasers of Russian oil and gas and countries involved in sanctions evasion. It also extends the Iran Sanctions Act for five years.

The bill’s future in the House remains uncertain, but Ukraine says it could provide leverage against Russia, whose energy revenues remain central to financing the war.

At a September 10 briefing hosted by the Bipartisan Congressional Ukraine Caucus, Ukraine’s Charge d’Affaires in Washington, Denys Sienik, urged lawmakers to view the measure as a source of leverage rather than a finished instrument.

“All the decisions, major decisions, indeed require compromise,” Sienik said. He warned that Russia continues earning substantial oil and gas revenues while producing weapons and recruiting soldiers.

“What message will it send to Ukrainians, and what message will it send to Russia if this does not pass?” he asked.

Former State Department sanctions coordinator Daniel Fried offered a similar assessment. “If the US authority would increase diplomacy to end Russia’s war against Ukraine, it should increase the leverage it’s using against Russia,” he said. “Now is the time to use it.”

Fried cited the Obama administration’s Iran policy, when Congress pressured the administration to threaten countries buying Iranian oil while allowing waivers for nations that significantly reduced purchases over six-month periods. China and India protested but ultimately reduced their imports.

He said the current bill could likewise give Washington room to negotiate with major buyers rather than automatically impose maximum penalties. Fried acknowledged questions about how the bill’s thresholds would be calculated and how authorities would determine the destination of Russian oil.

“But with this bill, if it passes, there is something to work with,” he said. “There is leverage. If it doesn’t pass, there is nothing, zero.”

Fried said sanctions need not eliminate every barrel of Russian or Iranian oil from global markets. Their goal is to reduce the revenue available to sustain war. Forcing Russia to sell at lower prices, he said, can also reduce money flowing to the Kremlin.

That approach places the shadow fleet at the center of the sanctions debate. The objective is not simply to stop individual ships, but to make the networks moving sanctioned oil more expensive, unreliable, and difficult to replace.

Ukraine’s argument is that those networks are already shared by Russia and Iran. The three tankers identified by Kyiv offer a case study: vessels moving Russian oil, Iranian oil, or both; managers shifting between sanctioned networks; and ship-to-ship transfers helping cargoes reach international markets.

As Washington escalates pressure on Tehran and considers additional measures against Moscow, that convergence could become increasingly important.

Satellite imagery appears to show significant fire damage at one pumping station, although it remains unclear whether the pipeline itself was damaged or how long repairs would take.

One U.S. official told CNN the attack was carried out by drones originating from Iraq, but responsibility has not been independently established. The incident comes as Iran-aligned groups are simultaneously threatening Saudi energy infrastructure and Red Sea shipping.

The pipeline has become especially important since the Strait of Hormuz was effectively closed, allowing Saudi Arabia to move roughly 5 million barrels of oil per day from its eastern fields to the Red Sea port of Yanbu. At the same time, the Houthis have threatened Saudi shipping through Bab al-Mandab.

The attacks are putting pressure on both of Saudi Arabia's principal export routes as Riyadh seeks greater U.S. support against the Houthis. Reuters reports that Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman asked Trump for direct U.S. military assistance Thursday, but Washington declined and instead offered intelligence and targeting support.

Source: https://t.co/BbygWPJTW4

15 Essential Trade Stories for Business Leaders
https://t.co/8E7AJLcn47

According to Press Monitor's tracking of Indian publications, this media monitoring review delivers 15 essential trade stories for business leaders. From BRICS Summit 2026 dynamics to US-China tariff negotiations and WTO trade policy findings, these stories bring news on trade, covering tariffs, supply chains, and global policy shifts. Press Monitor's press review and media intelligence combine print media monitoring with real editorial data to give you the competitive edge.

1. Brics Summit 2026: India's Balancing Act
A front-page report in Hindustan Times says that India is balancing trade initiatives with geopolitical concerns at the eighteenth Brics Summit while Brazil pushes for the C‑390 Millennium aircraft for the Indian Air Force. The summit, scheduled for September twelfth, brings together India, Brazil, Russia, China, South Africa, Iran, Egypt, Ethiopia, and the United Arab Emirates, with discussions on trade, supply-chain resilience, and North‑South cooperation. Meanwhile, Embraer executives will meet Indian officials on India’s aviation procurements, including the C‑390 and the Make‑in‑India production plan.
Why it matters: India navigates geopolitical tensions while advancing trade and defense procurement at the eighteenth Brics Summit. Key detail: Embraer executives will meet Indian officials on C-390 Millennium aircraft and Make-in-India production plans. Source: Hindustan Times, New Delhi. Next step: Monitor how bilateral deals evolve during the summit. What does this mean for India's defense supply chain?

2. Businesses Expect Brics Summit to Boost Trade and Investment
A front-page report in Business Standard says businesses and economists expect the 18th Brics summit in New Delhi to deliver tangible gains in trade, investment, supply-chain integration, and cross-border payments beyond strategic dialogue. Key expectations include easier market access, lower regulatory barriers, greater use of local currencies, and stronger payment linkages for Indian businesses. The eleven-member grouping accounts for around 26 per cent of global trade, with India's trade heavily import-biased from China, the United Arab Emirates, and Russia.
Why it matters: Business leaders anticipate tangible gains in trade, investment, and supply-chain integration from the 18th Brics summit. Key detail: The eleven-member grouping accounts for around 26 per cent of global trade. Source: Business Standard, New Delhi. Next step: Watch for announcements on market access and cross-border payment linkages. How will Indian businesses leverage this opportunity?

3. Xi Jinping to Attend BRICS Summit
A front-page report in The Hindu says President Xi Jinping will attend the BRICS Summit in New Delhi this weekend, marking his first visit to India in nearly seven years. The two leaders are expected to hold bilateral talks on the sidelines, with Commerce Ministers Wang Wentao and Piyush Goyal also meeting to discuss trade concerns. Border tensions that froze relations for four years have given way to a gradual normalisation process since October 2024.
Why it matters: President Xi Jinping's first visit to India in nearly seven years signals a diplomatic reset. Key detail: Commerce Ministers Wang Wentao and Piyush Goyal will meet to discuss trade concerns alongside Modi-Xi bilateral talks. Source: The Hindu. Next step: Track outcomes of the bilateral trade discussions. Will border tensions give way to deeper economic cooperation?

4. India Steers BRICS Towards Global Reform
A front-page report in Millennium Post says India is hosting the eighteenth BRICS Summit in New Delhi on September twelfth and thirteenth two thousand and twenty six to steer the expanding grouping towards meaningful global reform while preventing it from becoming a rigid anti-Western coalition. Authors JOHN FELIX RAJ and PRABHAT KUMAR DATTA, both from ST XAVIER'S UNIVERSITY, Kolkata, argue that India must balance strategic autonomy with bloc ambitions by advocating institutional reform of bodies such as the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank rather than pursuing a common currency or confrontational policies.
Why it matters: India aims to transform the expanding BRICS bloc into a force for institutional reform rather than a confrontational anti-Western coalition. Key detail: Advocates push for IMF and World Bank reform instead of a common currency. Source: Millennium Post, by John Felix Raj and Prabhat Kumar Datta. Next step: Observe how India balances strategic autonomy with bloc ambitions. Can BRICS reform global governance without fracturing?

5. Modi Set For BRICS Bilateral Meetings
A front-page report in Business Line says Prime Minister Narendra Modi is set for bilateral meetings with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin during the BRICS summit in New Delhi on September 12-13. The Modi-Xi talks are expected to focus on the fragile improvement in ties, with the unresolved border issue and widening trade imbalance likely to dominate. India will push for greater exports to Russia to narrow a bilateral trade deficit exceeding $50 billion.
Why it matters: Prime Minister Modi's bilateral meetings with Xi Jinping and Putin will shape India's trade and defense posture. Key detail: India will push for greater exports to Russia to narrow a bilateral trade deficit exceeding $50 billion. Source: Business Line, New Delhi. Next step: Follow the Modi-Xi talks on border and trade imbalance. What concessions might India offer Russia?

6. India Hosts 18th BRICS Summit Sept 12-13
A front-page report in Times of India says India will host the eighteenth BRICS Summit in New Delhi on September twelfth and thirteenth. The summit brings together leaders from member countries, partner countries, and global institutions.
Why it matters: India chairs the summit at a pivotal moment for Global South cooperation. Key detail: The summit brings together leaders from member countries, partner countries, and global institutions. Source: Times of India, New Delhi. Next step: Monitor which partnership initiatives emerge. How will India leverage its chairship for institutional change?

7. BRICS Trade Bonanza 20 Years
A front-page report in Hindustan Times says deeper trade and investment ties among BRICS countries will help bolster economic resilience across the Global South and inject fresh momentum into an increasingly strained multilateral trading system. Market watchers and business leaders said the group, established as BRIC in 2006 with South Africa joining five years later, has evolved into a major platform for Global South countries to deepen economic ties. Analysts said more BRICS collaboration could provide members with greater room to diversify markets and supply chains as protectionism and geopolitical tensions add to uncertainty in the global economy.
Why it matters: Two decades of BRICS collaboration have deepened trade ties and bolstered economic resilience across the Global South. Key detail: The group has evolved from BRIC in 2006 to a major platform for diversifying markets amid protectionism. Source: Hindustan Times, by Zhong Nan. Next step: Assess how BRICS trade momentum affects global supply chains. What comes next after twenty years?

8. BRICS Summit Tests India Amid Geopolitical Shifts
A front-page report in Morning Standard says the Brics summit has returned to New Delhi twenty-five years after the acronym was first coined. The expanded eleven-member grouping now faces significant geopolitical fractures, energy market volatility, and strained supply chains. With India holding the chairmanship, the bloc must overcome internal divisions to offer practical solutions and amplify the Global South voice in global institutions.
Why it matters: The expanded eleven-member bloc faces significant geopolitical fractures and energy market volatility. Key detail: India holds the chairmanship and must overcome internal divisions to amplify the Global South voice. Source: Morning Standard, New Delhi. Next step: Watch how India navigates competing interests within the bloc. Can BRICS offer practical solutions to energy security?

9. India Brics Summit Sparks Trade Talk
Why it matters: India's WTO Trade Policy Review has sparked debate among Brics partners over trade measures and barriers. Key detail: China, Indonesia, and Brazil raised concerns about subsidies and quality-control orders, while Russia, Egypt, and Saudi Arabia praised India's reforms. Source: Business Standard, by Asit Ranjan Mishra, New Delhi. Next step: Track how India responds to WTO scrutiny. Will trade barrier reforms attract more foreign investment?

10. BRICS Expansion Fuels Internal Divisions
A front-page report in Statesman says BRICS has transformed from a niche economic acronym into a powerful geopolitical heavyweight of the Global South through successive waves of expansion since 2001. The bloc added Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, and the United Arab Emirates as full members in January 2024, followed by Indonesia in January 2025, while ten partner countries joined a new cooperative framework in 2025. However, deep-seated geopolitical rivalries between China and India, economic imbalances dominated by China, and diverging strategic visions between revisionist and reformist members threaten the bloc's cohesion.
Why it matters: Successive waves of expansion have made BRICS a geopolitical heavyweight but also exposed deep rivalries. Key detail: China-India tensions, economic imbalances dominated by China, and diverging strategic visions threaten cohesion. Source: Statesman. Next step: Observe whether the partner-country model can bridge divisions. How does expansion affect decision-making within BRICS?

11. BRICS Summit Returns to New Delhi
Why it matters: The BRICS grouping returns to New Delhi amid war, energy shocks, and geopolitical fragmentation. Key detail: Iran joins as a full member amid tensions with the UAE, adding complexity to the bloc. Source: New Indian Express, Chennai. Next step: Monitor how internal tensions are managed during the summit. What does Iran's full membership mean for BRICS cohesion?

12. India Leads BRICS Summit 2026
A front-page report in Statesman says that India is chairing the 2026 BRICS Summit in New Delhi, aiming to convert enlargement into tangible outcomes by strengthening institutional capacity and launching new partnership initiatives. The summit will explore a partner‑country model that expands reach without compromising cohesion.
Why it matters: India's chairship aims to convert enlargement into tangible outcomes through institutional capacity and new partnership initiatives. Key detail: The summit explores a partner-country model that expands reach without compromising cohesion. Source: Statesman, New Delhi. Next step: Evaluate the feasibility of the partner-country framework. Can BRICS grow without losing focus?

13. Owaisi Demands West Bank Import Ban
A front-page report in Deccan Chronicle says that political leader Asaduddin Owaisi has urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the Union government to impose a ban on goods imported from illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank. This measure aims to curb territorial expansion, address regional oppression, and establish a framework for a two-state solution, aligning national policy with several Western nations.
Why it matters: Political leader Asaduddin Owaisi has urged the government to ban imports from illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank. Key detail: The move aligns national policy with several Western nations and aims to curb territorial expansion. Source: Deccan Chronicle, Hyderabad. Next step: Watch for government response to the import ban demand. How will India balance diplomatic relations with trade policy?

14. U.S.-Canada Trade Row Warns India On Deals
A front-page report in The Hindu says the United States and Canada have severely strained their decades-long trade partnership with reciprocal tariffs hitting fifty percent and Washington imposing export bans on select goods. The escalation offers India critical warning signs ahead of potential bilateral deals, especially as previous tariff agreements are undermined by ongoing investigations into forced labour and market excesses. Policymakers are urged to carefully weigh long-term vulnerabilities before committing to any new commercial frameworks.
Why it matters: The US-Canada trade escalation with 50% reciprocal tariffs offers India critical warning signs for bilateral deals. Key detail: Previous tariff agreements are undermined by forced labour investigations and market excess probes. Source: The Hindu. Next step: Assess how India should weigh long-term vulnerabilities in trade negotiations. What safeguards should Indian policymakers prioritize?

15. China, US Target Early Tariff Cuts
A front-page report in New Indian Express says the BRICS grouping returns to New Delhi at a moment when the world economy is again being tested by war, energy shocks and geopolitical fragmentation. India's chairship gives immense strategic significance as the bloc seeks to offer practical answers for supply chain resilience and energy security. The twenty-five-year-old grouping now has eleven members after recent expansions, and Iran joins as a full member amid tensions with the UAE.
Why it matters: China and the United States aim to agree on tariff reductions for $30 billion worth of goods from each side. Key detail: A summit in Washington on 24 September could reshape trade relations between the two largest economies. Source: Statesman, Beijing. Next step: Track negotiation progress ahead of the Washington summit. What would an early deal mean for global trade and Indian exporters?

Closing: These 15 stories reflect the interconnected world of trade policy, from BRICS diplomacy to bilateral tariff negotiations. Press Monitor's print media monitoring ensures you stay grounded in verified Indian editorial intelligence. Which story will shape your business strategy next?

According to Press Monitor's tracking of Indian publications, seven high-impact developments are reshaping the timber, lumber, and wood products sector. Our media monitoring team has compiled this press review to deliver editorial-vetted intelligence for procurement leaders, forestry executives, and supply chain managers. Here is your complete briefing on news on timber lumber wood products.

1. Century Plyboards Executive Shares Growth Strategy
A front-page report in Economic Times says two Indian executives share their journeys to success. Century Plyboards' Executive Director discusses building lasting value and transforming the company into a future-ready wood solutions firm. Mrs Bectors Food Specialities' Director Ishaan Bector, thirty-seven, talks about scaling English Oven into a national bakery brand.
Why it matters: Corporate leadership shifts directly influence market positioning and sustainable manufacturing practices.
Key detail: Century Plyboards' Executive Director outlined plans to transform the company into a future-ready wood solutions firm, emphasizing lasting value creation and operational resilience.

Source: Economic Times
Next step: Review the executive profile for insights on scaling domestic brands.

2. U.S.-Canada Trade Row Warns India On Deals
A front-page report in The Hindu says the United States and Canada have severely strained their decades-long trade partnership with reciprocal tariffs hitting fifty percent and Washington imposing export bans on select goods. The escalation offers India critical warning signs ahead of potential bilateral deals, especially as previous tariff agreements are undermined by ongoing investigations into forced labour and market excesses. Policymakers are urged to carefully weigh long-term vulnerabilities before committing to any new commercial frameworks.
Why it matters: Global tariff escalations and export bans create ripple effects for Indian import-export frameworks and raw material sourcing.
Key detail: Washington and Ottawa imposed reciprocal fifty percent tariffs alongside export restrictions, urging Indian policymakers to reassess bilateral commercial commitments amid forced labour probes.

Source: The Hindu
Next step: Align procurement strategies with emerging geopolitical risk assessments.

3. East Central Railway Announces 1.85 Crore Tenders
A front-page report in Economic Times says the Divisional Railway Manager of East Central Railway has issued three electronic tenders for civil, road, and woodwork repairs across multiple zones in the DDU jurisdiction. The combined advertised value of these projects exceeds one point eight five crore rupees, with submission deadlines set for 29 September 2026 via the national e-procurement portal. Bids must include earnest money deposits ranging from one point one seven to two point zero three lakh rupees, inviting technically sound public sector and private contractors to participate.
Why it matters: Public infrastructure spending signals sustained demand for construction materials, including treated timber and engineered wood panels.
Key detail: Three electronic tenders for civil, road, and woodwork repairs were issued across the DDU jurisdiction, requiring earnest money deposits between one point one seven and two point zero three lakh rupees.

Source: Economic Times
Next step: Register on the national e-procurement portal before the 29 September deadline.

4. Bee Hive Components Listed With Prices
A front-page report in Tribune says a detailed specification sheet for bee hive components is presented. Various parts such as brood bee hive, full super bee hive, shallow super bee hive, inner covers, top covers, and bottom boards are listed with their dimensions and wood types. The document includes dates and pricing details alongside the technical specifications.
Why it matters: Specialized woodworking requirements for agricultural equipment highlight niche manufacturing opportunities within the broader timber supply chain.
Key detail: Tribune published detailed specifications for brood bee hives, shallow supers, and wooden covers, listing exact dimensions, wood types, and pricing structures.

Source: Tribune
Next step: Evaluate supplier capacity for precision-cut agricultural timber components.

5. Telangana Forests Hit 11,669 Offences Year
A front-page report in Deccan Chronicle says Telangana's forests face over 11,669 offences annually, prompting a proposal for arms and ammunition for frontline staff. The department seeks stronger security and operational resources as forest personnel confront timber smuggling and encroachments. Forest Martyrs' Day on September 11 commemorates 23 staff killed since 1984.
Why it matters: Rising illegal logging and encroachment pressures force stricter forest management protocols and security investments.
Key detail: The state department proposed allocating arms and ammunition to frontline staff following over eleven thousand annual offences, commemorating Forest Martyrs' Day.

Source: Deccan Chronicle
Next step: Monitor regulatory updates affecting certified wood sourcing and FSC compliance.

6. India ASEAN Five-Year Agriculture Plan
A front-page report in Mint says India and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations have agreed to roll out a new five-year plan of action for cooperation in agriculture and forestry. The meeting was held on 9 September in New Delhi and was co-chaired by Philippines agriculture secretary Francisco P Tiu Laurel and Union agriculture minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan.
Why it matters: Cross-border cooperation agreements expand market access for agricultural inputs, forestry products, and sustainable biomass initiatives.
Key detail: New Delhi hosted co-chaired talks between Union agriculture minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan and Philippine Secretary Francisco P Tiu Laurel to formalize a five-year action plan.

Source: Mint
Next step: Track diplomatic outcomes impacting pulp, paper, and wood pellet export corridors.

7. Haryana Government Floats Multiple Tenders
A front-page report in Times of India says the Haryana government has issued multiple tenders across departments including veterinary services, irrigation, medical supplies, forestry, and water resources. The tenders, listed on the state e-tender portal, cover works ranging from mobile veterinary units to medicine supply at Kalpana Chawla Government Medical College and plantation schemes in Hisar. Closing dates are scheduled between September and October 2026 with amounts running into several lakhs of rupees.
Why it matters: State-level procurement releases indicate steady public investment in plantation schemes, veterinary infrastructure, and medical supplies.
Key detail: The Haryana e-tender portal listed contracts spanning irrigation, forestry plantation drives in Hisar, and mobile veterinary units, with closing dates extending through October 2026.

Source: Times of India
Next step: Submit bids via the official portal ahead of regional deadlines.

text:
"All of us have our own rituals." Mine is to tell as many people as possible that Muhammad, the man Muslims are taught to take as the perfect example, was a violent warlord who, according to the most authoritative Sunni hadith collections, consummated a marriage with Aisha when she was nine.

When he was weak in Mecca, he preached patience and forbearance. When he gained power in Medina, he fought, conquered Arabia, and imposed Islamic rule. After the Banu Qurayza surrendered, the adult males of that tribe were executed. Islamic law generally offers the conquered a choice of conversion, submission under dhimmi status and the jizya, or the sword—not always immediate forced conversion of every civilian, but conquest and political supremacy all the same.

Al-Qaeda and ISIS did not invent jihad. They were following Muhammad’s example and the later record of Islamic expansion whenever they fought the West.

George W. Bush was only half right when he said Islam is a religion of peace. The peace many revivalist and jihadist readings aim at is the peace of a world that has submitted to Islam. Where that can be pursued by preaching, migration, lawfare, and demography, it will be. Where force looks possible, violent jihad has been used again and again and again and again.

In the century after Muhammad’s death, his successors took the Levant, Egypt, North Africa, and, soon after, Visigothic Spain. That was almost three quarters of the original Christian world, the whole southern shore of the Mediterranean. An Islamic Crusade if you will.

Constantinople is another warning. On 29 May 1453 the city that had been the capital of Christian Rome in the East for more than a thousand years fell to Mehmed II. The last emperor died in the breach. The sack that followed brought killing, rape, and enslavement; Hagia Sophia was turned into a mosque. That is what it looks like when a Christian city does not hold: not a change of branding, but a conquered people living under the winner’s law and the winner’s faith. Malta and Vienna are easier to celebrate because they survived. Constantinople is what happens when the walls finally give way.

Today think of other people who lived through other 11 of Septembers.

On 11 September 2001, the day ended with a country staring at the cost of an enemy that followed Islam. And we had already started fighting back, with the FDNY and NYPD rushing to the site and especially with the heroes of flight 93.

On 11 September 2012, it happened again in Benghazi. Islamist militants overran the American compound. Ambassador Christopher Stevens and Sean Smith were killed that night; Tyrone Woods and Glen Doherty died in the fighting that ran into the 12th. It was not a riot that got out of hand. It was a jihadist attack on the anniversary of the last one. Eleven years after New York and Washington, Americans were again counting their dead on a September 11 because men who spoke in the name of Islam had come to kill them.

Hundreds of years earlier, on 11 September 1565, the Great Siege of Malta was breaking. Victory would be marked on the 8th; the Ottoman fleet was still leaving on the night of the 11th and 12th. That morning a Maltese Christian did not need a textbook. He could see what Islamic conquest looked like when it reached his harbor.

On 11 September 1683, Vienna was still under Ottoman siege. The relief battle was the next day, 12 September. People inside the walls that Thursday were not debating abstractions. They were looking at the consequence of an empire that had been pushing into Christian Europe for centuries.

Tours in 732 and the reconquest of Spain, finished in 1492, belong on the same list. The point is not a trivia date. The point is that 11 September is not only a modern American wound. It is one more day on a long frontier.

Those who treat Islam only as a private faith, and never as a historical political project with a doctrine of jihad, will not understand that record—or why jihadist movements keep appealing to it.

This has been a war for centuries. What are you going to do now?
author: in_voco
authorBio: Retired U.S. Army.

A year after Tyler Robinson allegedly killed Charlie Kirk at Utah Valley University, many Americans believe that he either did not do it or did not act alone. Candace Owens has implied that “Erika Kirk conspired with other Turning Point USA leaders and even foreign governments to have Charlie killed.” She suggested that Kirk was shot “from below the stage” and that “the assassin fled through tunnels.” She said, “Charlie Kirk was the first casualty of the War in Iran. Never forget what they did to him.” Robinson, she says, is “a total patsy” who was never on campus that day. Israel, with help from other governments and from Kirk’s own widow and staff, had Kirk killed, she suggests. Owens and others point to the fact that Robinson was not on investigators’ radar until he turned himself in 33 hours after the shot, FBI Director Kash Patel had posted that afternoon that “the subject” was “now in custody,” ATF examiners could neither identify nor exclude the recovered Mauser rifle as the source of the bullet fragments, no spent cartridge case was found on the roof, and the trigger carried DNA from at least four people.

But Robinson confessed repeatedly in writing and the physical evidence matches what he wrote. When his partner texted him, “you weren’t the one who did it right????” he replied, “I am, I’m sorry,” and then, “I had enough of his hatred. Some hate can’t be negotiated out.” He left a note under his keyboard, “I had the opportunity to take out Charlie Kirk and I’m going to take it,” and told a Discord server of more than 20 friends, “It was me at UVU yesterday.” The reason Robinson wasn’t on investigators’ radar is that his family turned him in within a day of the FBI releasing his photo. Patel’s “subject in custody” was George Zinn, a 71-year-old who confessed falsely to help the shooter escape. Surveillance video played at the preliminary hearing shows Robinson crawling across the roof and jumping down after the shot. The police found the rifle in the woods wrapped in a towel that was 95% his DNA, and the ATF put the odds at a trillion to one that he was the main contributor of the DNA on the trigger. There was no casing on the roof because the Mauser rifle is a bolt-action that still held“one spent round and three unspent rounds” when police found it. An “inconclusive” fragment comparison appears in about 20% of casework because rifle bullets break apart, and the same ATF report matched the spent casing to the rifle. The claim that Robinson was never on campus was debunked when the hearing played video of him walking around it. Finally, at the September 1, 2026 hearing, his own lawyers offered no alternative theory of the murder and agreed there was a single shot and a single bullet.

text:
Karyann Parkinson let her capable 5-year-old walk half a mile along a sidewalk in a gated community to collect goose feathers. One frightened stranger later: three police cars, CPS, seven years on the child-abuse registry, a criminal conviction for contributing to the delinquency of a minor, and thousands in legal fees.

As quoted in @FreeRangeKids's article in @reason: 
"Delinquency?" ParentsUSA's Executive Director scoffed. "Is the kid going to rob banks at 14 because he collected feathers at age 5?"

Does this child's age make you pause or feel concerned? Why?

Let's stop asking "how old was the child?" Instead, let's ask "how capable was the child of being safe in that specific circumstance?"

Regardless of age, does the person have the physical abilities, judgment, awareness, intellect, and skills to handle the specific circumstances? The 75-year-old is old enough, unless dementia or a hip replacement makes it unsafe. The 17-year-old is old enough, unless his risk-taking history makes being "unsupervised" unsafe.

Are you worried that the child could get hurt?

Then should we arrest parents for “allowing” their child to ride in a car, because children might get hurt or die in a car wreck, the #1 reason kids are hurt or killed?

Karyann reached out to ParentsUSA. We are assisting her and her private attorney and have offered to take the lead. For now, we remain in a supporting role at her attorney's request— because, if ParentsUSA walks into that courtroom, a judge playing politics could take it out on her.

Virginia already has a "Childhood  Independence" law. It is better than nothing, but it still did not stop this. ParentsUSA supports that Act in every state — and we always understood it would not stop the “concerned” person, the officer, the dispatcher, the prosecutor, or a judge who can work around it or simply ignore it.

Our add-on statutory language would require inquiry and confirmation before government agents could intervene: Does the child appear hurt, in distress, or in imminent danger from an identifiable source? Only then may they intervene. Violating that protocol would give the parent whose decisions were overridden a private cause of action.

Every fit parent is one unreasonably and irrationally afraid person away from having their life and their children’s lives upended. We have to decline too many of these requests because our resources are so limited. ParentsUSA exists to stop these intrusions. Donate so we can take more cases across the USA.

text:
1. America Marks the 25th Anniversary of 9/11 with Ceremonies at All Three Attack Sites
The United States paused on Friday to commemorate the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks that killed 2,977 people. Ceremonies took place at the World Trade Center site in New York, the Pentagon in Virginia, and the Flight 93 memorial in Shanksville, Pennsylvania. Family members read the names of all victims plus the six killed in the 1993 World Trade Center bombing. Moments of silence marked the times the planes struck, the towers collapsed, the Pentagon was hit, and Flight 93 went down. For the first time, an additional moment of silence honored thousands who later died from 9/11-related illnesses caused by toxic dust. 
https://t.co/Dq1O9Egff9
President Donald Trump spoke at the Pentagon ceremony, recalling national unity after the attacks and recognizing U.S. troops currently fighting in the Iran war. Vice President JD Vance attended the Ground Zero event in New York along with former presidents George W. Bush, Barack Obama, Bill Clinton, and Joe Biden. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani attended despite a petition from some victims’ families asking him to stay away. At Ground Zero, widow Terry Strada drew cheers when she called on Trump to hold Saudi Arabia accountable for its alleged role in the attacks. The day featured bells, name readings lasting hours, and the Tribute in Light beams in Lower Manhattan. Video potential is high: memorial pools, name readings, political figures, first responders, and emotional family interviews. 
https://t.co/HXaLjEYa8r
2. Houthis Seize Perim Island, Tightening Control Over a Vital Global Shipping Chokepoint
Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels captured Perim Island (also called Mayyun) in the Bab al-Mandab Strait on Friday after government forces withdrew. This completed their takeover of Yemen’s entire western Red Sea coast, including the port of Mokha the previous day and the nearby town of Dhubab. The small volcanic island sits in the middle of the narrow strait that links the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden and carries a significant share of global trade and energy shipments. Combined with disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz from the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict, the move raises fears of further oil and gas price spikes (oil already above $110 a barrel). 
https://t.co/dbqivKB81h
Houthi forces arrived by boat. Analysts called it a “game changer” because it gives them positions inside the strait itself rather than just on the approaches. Saudi Arabia responded with airstrikes on Mokha airport. The Houthis said they would not disrupt most international shipping but reiterated threats against Saudi vessels. Government forces said they would try to retake the areas. This is part of a rapid Houthi offensive after years of stalemate and ties directly into the wider Iran war. Strong video elements include satellite maps of the strait, shipping footage, conflict images from Yemen, and oil price graphics. 
https://t.co/Dq1O9Egff9
3. Philippines Ferry Fire Death Toll Rises to 35 as Rescuers Recover Dozens of Bodies
The death toll from a fire aboard the passenger-cargo ferry MV June Aster off Coron, Palawan, rose to 35 on Friday after firefighters boarded the burned-out vessel and recovered 30 additional bodies. The fire broke out on the evening of September 9 during a voyage from Manila to the tourist destination of Coron. Survivors reported two explosions from the cargo hold followed by rapid spread of flames and thick smoke. The ship carried 117 passengers and 17 crew (two listed passengers never boarded). Forty-three people were rescued earlier; dozens remain missing or unaccounted for. 
https://t.co/JclQvgZSNv
Rescuers had been unable to board for more than 40 hours due to heat and smoke. Bodies were found mainly in the economy accommodation area. The cause is under investigation. The Philippines has a history of deadly ferry accidents. President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. directed agencies to support survivors and families. Coast Guard images show the charred wreckage, body bags, and search operations at sea. This story works well for videos with wreckage footage, survivor accounts, maps of Palawan, and rescue efforts. 
https://t.co/Bdi4JPWfv4
4. Israel Orders British Military Team to Leave the West Bank in Sanctions Retaliation
Israel ordered a small British military team (about 10 personnel based in Ramallah) to leave the country within seven days. The British Support Team advises and trains Palestinian Authority security forces under the Oslo Accords and has also reported on settler violence. The expulsion is retaliation for UK sanctions on goods from Israeli settlements in the West Bank, announced earlier in the week by Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband. A small British contingent involved in Gaza ceasefire coordination was also told to leave. 
https://t.co/7ha7myKQpz
British sources said Israel had been intercepting the team’s communications and viewing them as the “eyes and ears” of the West on settler attacks. The team had been preparing to expand. This follows other Israeli measures such as closing the UK consulate in East Jerusalem and barring some British MPs. It highlights deepening diplomatic friction between Israel and several Western countries over settlements and the two-state solution. Video angles include West Bank maps, settlement footage, diplomatic statements, and analysis of UK-Israel relations. 
https://t.co/MPRFkMhNjR
5. Iran War Continues to Drive High Oil Prices and Broader Regional Tensions
The U.S.-Iran conflict remains a major backdrop, with oil prices climbing above $110 a barrel and U.S. diesel above $6 a gallon. Vice President JD Vance had privately sought unvarnished assessments from military commanders about the war. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth referenced the Iran conflict during the Pentagon 9/11 ceremony. Houthi advances in Yemen (see story 2) are viewed as part of Iran’s strategy to pressure energy markets. Additional developments include new U.S. Treasury sanctions on entities supporting Iranian proxies and reports of strikes near the Strait of Hormuz. 
https://t.co/dbqivKB81h
These events connect the 9/11 commemorations (where officials linked current threats to past ones) with live geopolitical and economic impacts. Useful for videos that tie anniversary reflection to current events: energy market graphics, military briefings, shipping maps, and expert commentary on how the two major chokepoints (Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab) affect global trade.
These five stories dominate coverage today and offer strong visual and narrative material for videos—ceremonies and emotion for #1, maps/conflict footage for #2 and #5, disaster imagery for #3, and diplomatic tension for #4. Always verify latest details before filming, as situations (especially in Yemen and the ferry search) can evolve.

text:
I stand before you looking back at the eleventh of September—a date that cleaved our history in two, bleeding a permanent, suffocating darkness into a brilliant Tuesday morning. I must speak of the sheer horror of that day, not to give power to the butchers who orchestrated it, but to look unflinchingly at the absolute abyss that swallowed our people. It was an act of pure, calculated, breathtaking malice. The sky was an impossible, serene blue before the air was violently ripped apart by the deafening shriek of jet engines weaponized into missiles. In an instant, glass, steel, and bone became a roaring, inescapable inferno. I am forever haunted by the suffocating heat, the twisting, groaning metal, and the toxic, choking clouds of pulverized concrete that rushed down the avenues like a tidal wave of death. I think of the absolute, claustrophobic terror of the trapped, forced into the agonizing, impossible space between roaring flames and the long, terrible fall. It was an apocalyptic nightmare brought to our shores by hollowed-out fanatics, a descent into an unmitigated hellscape that painted our skies with the darkest, most grotesque shades of human depravity.

To the nearly three thousand beautiful, vital souls violently stolen from us in that crushing darkness, I offer this weeping, broken tribute. You were ordinary people doing ordinary things—boarding flights, pouring coffee, riding elevators, sitting at your desks—when you were swallowed by a fire you did not ignite. You did not sign up for a war; you were slaughtered by cowards who lacked the humanity to look you in the eye. I mourn the staggering, senseless theft of your lives. I weep for the first responders who charged directly into the collapsing maw of hell, choosing duty even as a million tons of concrete fell on top of them. I weep for the passengers who fought back in the sky above Pennsylvania, trading their own futures for the lives of strangers on the ground. The architects of this slaughter wanted to reduce you to ashes, to a nameless body count in their twisted theater of terror. But I refuse to let your humanity be erased. You were the heartbeat of our world, and the violent absence of your light left a bleeding chasm in the earth that can never be filled.

And to the families—the ones who watched the towers fall, who waited by phones that never rang, who taped fliers to brick walls hoping against all hope—I speak directly to your shattered hearts. I know that for you, September 11th never truly ended. The towers are still falling in your nightmares. The planes are still hitting. You were condemned to survive a day when the world ended, forced to wake up every single morning since, carrying the crushing, unbearable weight of an empty seat at the table. Your grief is a living, breathing creature, a heavy, suffocating mantle you must wear for the rest of your lives.

I will not offer you hollow comforts about closure, or time healing all wounds. What was done to you was an unforgivable amputation of your soul. You have had to navigate a desolate, agonizing aftermath, living in the shadow of a very public, world-altering tragedy while trying to tend to a deeply private, bleeding wound. I see your silent agony. I see the superhuman, agonizing endurance it takes for you simply to breathe in a world that allowed this to happen.

The eleventh of September was a triumph of profound, suffocating evil. It proved that there are monsters who will gladly burn the world to the ground to make a point. But standing here, amidst the heavy, lingering ghosts of that day, I swear to hold fiercely to the love we still possess for those who were violently taken. The terrorists brought an unimaginable darkness, an unmitigated horror that we will never unsee. Yet, the memory of those we lost, and the staggering courage of you, the families who carry their legacy, remains the one undeniable light that those cowards could never, and will never, extinguish.
