text:
Biggest brainwash operation started in 1945:

Adenauer’s Ties to the CIA

Close Relations

U.S. Treasury Secretary Henry Morgenthau’s plan to transform Germany into an agrarian state was replaced by the Marshall Plan: $13 billion flowed into the reconstruction of Europe by 1953. At the center of it all was the Federal Republic of Germany (FRG), serving as a bulwark against the communist threat from the East conjured up by the U.S.
In the U.S., the plan drew a barrage of criticism: The Chicago Tribune, for example, wrote that the Marshall Plan—which was rushed through Congress by Winthrop Aldrich, president of Chase Manhattan Bank and Nelson Rockefeller’s brother-in-law—was yet another Rockefeller scheme to fleece taxpayers. What comes closest to the reality is what can be read in the preamble. The plan’s goal was to “secure markets and stability for the United States.”

The Myth of the Marshall Plan
That is correct. By the end of the war, Europe owed the U.S. $11.5 billion; investments in infrastructure on the other side of the Atlantic helped absorb the excess capacity that the American economy had built up during the war.
As director of the Marshall Plan, W. Averell Harriman—son of Wall Street financier Edward Henry—decided how funds would be allocated. The Federal Republic of Germany (FRG) received 6.4 billion DM over four years, but during the same period had to allocate 24 billion DM to the federal budget to cover occupation costs. The FRG thus repaid the U.S. about four times more than it received in aid: the myth of the Marshall Plan.

As a result, government investment remained limited to the bare minimum—with consequences not only for economic performance and growth, but especially for the social problems faced by widows and orphans, war invalids, and displaced persons. Although only 40 percent of industrial facilities had been destroyed during the war, it took until 1951 for the FRG to once again reach the 1938 production level—three years later, it was just 30 percent above that level. With this record, the FRG lagged five years behind other Western European countries, such as Belgium.

Around the same time the plan was launched, John McCloy initiated a project to establish a state in the U.S. occupation zone based on the American model. Like his friend David Rockefeller, he had studied at Harvard and had resigned from his post as president of the World Bank to succeed Military Governor Lucius Clay. Although the lawyer was at the helm in the occupied West only until the end of 1952, he laid the groundwork for the instrumentalization of the Federal Republic of Germany (FRG) in the interests of the transatlantic financial oligarchy.

Investor Model “Occupation”
Thus, it was founded not as a state with a constitution, but with a Basic Law (GG), the drafting of which was overseen by the lawyer Adenauer in his capacity as President of the Parliamentary Council. After it was adopted by that very body in 1949, the Allied military governors approved it, allowing it to take effect. Crucial provisions include Article 79, which describes the “occupation-law order”; Article 120, which stipulates that the federal government bears the costs of the occupation; and Article 146, which states that the Basic Law loses its validity on the day a constitution enters into force that has been adopted by the German people through a free decision.

Against this backdrop, Carlo Schmid, chairman of the Parliamentary Council and an SPD politician, stated: “While acknowledging the Allies’ reservations, we are to adopt the Basic Law to organize the sovereign powers of the German people—which have now been restored—in one part of Germany. We are not to draft Germany’s constitution; we are not to establish a state.”

Adenauer’s Family
Ties to the FED
With the founding of the Federal Republic of Germany (FRG), the responsibilities of the military governors were transferred to the Allied High Commission (AHC), where McCloy was now in charge of laws, orders, regulations, and directives. His missions: to ensure the division of Germany and to integrate the FRG into NATO. Even before taking office, the American lawyer had set the course for key issues. He designated Adenauer as the candidate for the election campaign and also secured the necessary funding—shortly thereafter, the Bundestag elected the 73-year-old as chancellor.
But why did McCloy choose this retired politician from Cologne in particular? The answer is simple: both are rooted in the same family; they are related by marriage. In 1930, McCloy married the German-American Ellen Zinsser, a cousin of Konrad Adenauer’s wife Auguste; both were granddaughters of the industrial magnate Frederic G. Zinsser. He, in turn, was a partner of J.P. Morgan, one of the founders of the Federal Reserve System (FED) and a shareholder in the chemical conglomerate I.G. Farben.

This is worth noting because in 1924, McCloy joined the Wall Street law firm Cravath, Henderson & de Gerssdorff as a partner and, alongside J.P. Morgan, participated in an $110 million loan to the German government. In the 1930s, he represented—in Paris—not only J.P. Morgan (whose board of directors now included his other brother-in-law, John Zinnser) but also the Rockefellers’ Chase Manhattan Bank and the German-Jewish banker Paul Warburg, another founder of the Federal Reserve and an advisor to U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt.

German-American Business Ties
For the sake of completeness, another U.S. law firm that played a role within these business ties should be mentioned here. We are referring to the law firm Sullivan & Cromwell, where the future CIA director Allen Dulles and his brother John Foster were partners. In the U.S., the firm represented the interests of I.G. Farben and Vereinigte Stahlwerke, Europe’s largest steel producer at the time. Both companies also held stakes in the former Hermann Göring Works in Salzgitter.

Alongside Morgan and Rockefeller, other U.S. investors such as Du Pont, General Motors, IBM, and Ford were active in Germany at the same time. Meanwhile, McCloy was busy in France arranging loans for the fascist governments in Italy and Germany. Here, I.G. Farben recorded a large portion of the loans in its accounts; its director and largest shareholder was Max Warburg—who, incidentally, served as deputy to Reich Minister of Economics Hjalmar Schacht until 1938.
For Adenauer, however, the doors to the financial world’s most prestigious circles had been wide open long before his family’s high-profile marriage. For example, he was bound by a lifelong friendship with Robert Pferdmenges, who, together with Waldemar von Oppenheim, headed the Sal Oppenheim banking house, and later founded the CDU; as Adenauer’s most influential financial advisor, he oversaw the disbursement of Marshall Plan loans through the Reconstruction Loan Bank Association, the Kreditanstalt für Wiederaufbau.

Stock Market Speculator Adenauer
In the 1920s, Adenauer held no fewer than twelve seats on supervisory boards, including those of RWE, Deutsche Lufthansa, Ruhrgas AG, and Deutsche Bank. Adenauer, who had just joined Deutsche Bank’s supervisory board, immediately used this position to his own advantage. In 1928, he invested his own funds and one million marks borrowed from Deutsche Bank on the stock market. At first, he was successful: within a few months, he had earned around 800,000 marks from rayon stocks. He could have made a partial repayment of the loan, but he continued to speculate, and soon his account showed a deficit of 1.25 million marks. Deutsche Bank asked him to make up the shortfall.

Fritz Blüthgen, then CEO of Vereinigte Glanzstoff-Fabriken, who had brought the stock option to Adenauer’s attention, stepped in by depositing blocks of stock worth over one million marks into Adenauer’s account at Deutsche Bank as collateral. Although the bank used the stock to partially offset the debt, the future chancellor remained heavily in debt.
Blüthgen would come to the aid of his prominent friend on two further occasions, all the while wondering how the latter could possibly have access to such large sums of money on a salary as a municipal employee. In response to this generous gesture, Adenauer would later falsely claim that Blüthgen had advised him to buy the shares and that he had been harmed by Blüthgen’s fraudulent manipulations. Blüthgen—to whom Adenauer owed his second election as mayor of Cologne in 1929 and his election as Federal Chancellor 20 years later, both by a majority of one vote—would never receive a single pfennig back from him. Adenauer’s speculation also cost the Deutsche Bank around one million marks.

Adenauer’s Subsidy Policy
One of the first official acts of Cologne’s new—or rather, returning—mayor was to promise tax breaks to the anti-Semite Henry Ford in order to entice him to locate his automobile manufacturing plant—which had remained virtually undamaged during World War II—on the Rhine rather than in Berlin, as originally planned. This occurred at a time when the city of Cologne—partly as a result of Adenauer’s subsidy policy—ranked among the most heavily indebted local governments in Germany.
But let’s move forward to the early years of the Federal Republic of Germany: The main task of the new chancellor, who requested exclusive access to the American Chamber of Commerce in Germany (AHK), was to inspire West Germans with enthusiasm for capitalism and the American understanding of democracy. This was problematic because a large portion of the population identified with the socialist camp. Changing this was a CIA priority and the goal of a program to re-educate the Germans. Adenauer received the action plan for this from the U.S.

The Chancellor’s
Connection to the CIA
Funded by the United States Information Agency, “America Houses” sprang up in many cities. Their purpose was to promote a positive image of the U.S. in the West through exhibitions, lectures, and the “Amerika Dienst.” The result: starting in 1950, over twelve million citizens visited the facilities annually, and the CIA-produced newsreel “Welt im Film” reached over 17 million West German moviegoers every month.
Another measure in the American cultural campaign was the Congress for Cultural Freedom (CCF), a CIA organization disguised as a political forum for the non-communist left in West Germany. The CCF magazine “Der Monat—International Journal for Politics and Intellectual Life” successfully disseminated arguments regarding U.S. and West German policy among intellectuals, thereby gaining spokespeople to oppose efforts toward neutrality, particularly from the socialist party camp.

Pro-American Re-education of West Germans
The Free University of Berlin (FU Berlin) and the Institute of Sociology at the University of Frankfurt am Main became the first focal points for pro-American influence on the student body. Even before taking office, McCloy had enticed the institute’s founders—Max Horkheimer and Theodor Adorno, who had emigrated to the U.S. during the war—to return to the Federal Republic of Germany. Both sociologists, who had already been working for the CIA in the United States, were to shape postwar German culture as key figures in the U.S. re-education program.
With the power of veto, they initially oversaw the filling of positions in the government, universities, and the media. Later, Adorno—who knew how to publicly shape public opinion by promoting his sociology of anti-authoritarianism through radio and newspaper interviews on topics such as drugs, sex, and rock ’n’ roll—steered an entire generation toward the 1968 student movement.
Starting in mid-1950, the Korean War provided the U.S. with an opportunity to re-emerge on the world stage as a champion of freedom and democracy: Troops from the Democratic People’s Republic of North Korea—controlled by the Soviets and China—had attacked South Korea, which was occupied by the U.S. and fought back. War in Southeast Asia: this scenario sparked panic in Germany, which was also divided in two, and even British opposition leader Winston Churchill subsequently advocated in the Council of Europe for a Western European army into which German contingents would be integrated.

Adenauer Bypasses Parliament
Adenauer took up Churchill’s idea and wrote to McCloy requesting more occupation troops. When the chancellor then unilaterally bypassed Parliament and promised his brother-in-law a German troop contingent in the event that a European army were to be formed, the scandal was complete. After Adenauer’s cabinet learned of this proposal from the press, the then-Federal Minister of the Interior and CDU politician Gustav Heinemann resigned from office in October in “protest against this practice.”
Shortly thereafter, McCloy voluntarily undermined his own mission and provided fuel for a public controversy. In 1951, in a “gesture of reconciliation,” he pardoned 89 war criminals, including Friedrich Flick, one of the NSDAP’s biggest financiers, and Alfried Krupp von Bohlen und Halbach. Both industrialists even had the previously confiscated assets of their companies returned to them.

McCloy Pardons War Criminals
Fritz ter Meer, a member of the I.G. Farben executive board who established the Auschwitz III Monowitz concentration camp to have forced laborers produce military supplies there, also benefited from the High Commissioner’s gesture. McCloy, aware of the business ties between U.S. investors and I.G. Farben—the global banker Warburg had never been brought to trial—had, incidentally, spoken out in 1944 against the bombing of the rail lines leading to the Auschwitz concentration camp.
These and other events contributed to the West German population viewing the American occupiers with increasing skepticism. In addition, the Allies continued to dismantle industrial facilities. In particular, the demolition of the former Hermann Göring Works in Salzgitter had led to public riots. The dismantling of Europe’s most modern steel mill and the resulting loss of several thousand jobs put additional pressure on the already difficult economic situation in West Germany.

Systematic Mass Manipulation by the CIA
The more the “Old Man’s” popularity declined, the more McCloy had to come to his aid, and in 1952, the psychological operations plan codenamed “Pocket Book” went into effect. The Office of Policy, responsible for its implementation within the CIA, received a budget of $100 million and launched a public relations offensive.
While “RIAS” (Radio in the American Sector) and “Radio Free Europe” (RFE) had always broadcast propaganda—and RFE alone received $30 million annually from the CIA through the CCF until 1972—the Axel Springer publishing house was chosen to carry out mass manipulation in line with U.S. interests through the West German press. The media mogul clearly stated that he wanted to influence politics and society in a pro-American direction and even enshrined this in his company’s guiding principles. Springer alone was to receive $7 million from the CIA—more than any other publisher or major printing company. With these funds, the tabloid BILD was founded in 1952, and it continues to disseminate the U.S. worldview to this day.

Bribed Media, Unions, and Politicians
McCloy and his colleague Shepard Stone—who served as PR director for the AHK’s press fund—also needed the media in their fight against the Soviet bloc. They, too, financed newspapers to place editorial content and topics from U.S. sources. Stone’s list included 44 publications, among them the *Süddeutsche Zeitung*, which received 500,000 DM; in addition, the *Frankfurter Rundschau* initially received 1.6 million DM for the construction of a new editorial office and printing plant.

However, since the newspaper had overextended itself financially—and out of concern that it might fall into the hands of the Social Democrats—he devised a rescue plan: Stone provided another one million DM to keep the paper in operation, and the AHK became a partner in the *Frankfurter Rundschau*, which, incidentally, was the first daily newspaper in West Germany to be licensed by the Allies in 1945.
The next target for corruption: the German working class, 40 percent of whom were unionized—including a high proportion of communists. The American Federation of Labor, which had been infiltrated by the CIA, was responsible for controlling the unions. It used union committees that U.S. officials had set up with their German counterparts to, for example, determine the composition of the DGB executive board. For payments to unions, the U.S. intelligence agency initially had 200,000 dollars at its disposal, later one million dollars per year: politicians from all sides were bribed, all the way up to the SPD leadership under Willy Brandt.

Corrupt Decisions at International Level
The CIA also played a leading role in major international decisions. To ensure that the Bundestag would approve the Franco-German Coal and Steel Community—the Schuman Plan—McCloy, who was well aware of the importance of these relations for Western Europe, once again had votes bought. With the ratification of the plan in July 1952, the Bundestag then laid the foundation for the permanent division of Germany. Thomas Braden, the CIA officer responsible for the bribery scheme, would later reflect that he was glad the CIA was “immoral.”
Thanks to Adenauer’s cooperation, McCloy was indeed able to report phased success for his missions—working in close collaboration with his brother-in-law, he had prevented a united, non-aligned Germany. But at a high price. For at the same time, former business leaders and politicians with Nazi pasts regained influence and found a political home, particularly within the FDP.

Example: Ernst Achenbach, an FDP member and lawyer who actively campaigned for the rehabilitation of Nazi perpetrators. He urged Federal Minister of Justice and fellow party member Thomas Dehler to manipulate legal proceedings. One such case involved NSDAP politician Karl Rudolf Werner Best, who had ordered the murder of a fellow Nazi party member in 1933. Achenbach emphasized to Dehler that the German Reich had granted amnesty for such acts in 1934. Dehler, in turn, intervened with the Bavarian judiciary, which ultimately dismissed the case.

Nazi politicians play parliamentary democracy
Later, the Bundestag also spoke out in favor of a lenient approach in the investigative committees regarding war crimes convictions. The result was a wave of pardons. But while former Nazi officials played at representative parliamentary democracy and continued to live well as ever, the population watching from the stands of this political theater continued to suffer from poverty and unemployment.
After Adenauer squandered Germany’s chance at a peace treaty and reunification, approval of his policies hit rock bottom despite an assassination attempt. Stalin had proposed in a note the restoration of a German state. The condition: renouncing the territories east of the Oder and Neisse rivers, as well as joining a military alliance directed against a former enemy. In other words: non-alignment. Yet the “Chancellor of the Allies” rejected the offer as communist propaganda without giving it closer consideration.

Adenauer Rejects the Peace Treaty
Just as McCloy had expected of his brother-in-law, Adenauer decided against neutrality—without regard for the common good of all of Germany—and opted for full integration into the West. As a reward for his obedience, Adenauer once again received first-rate campaign support: In late 1952, the U.S. government invited him on a tour of America lasting several weeks. The highlight was a reception at the White House with full military honors. The message of this staged diplomatic maneuver: Seven years after the end of World War II, the Federal Republic of Germany was rejoining the chorus of the international community of democratic states.
Back home, Adenauer’s Minister of Economics, Ludwig Erhard, pursued a different strategy to maintain power. Just in time for the federal election, he called on business leaders to launch an initiative to promote the market economy. Bosch, Remtsma, as well as Bayer, BASF, and Hoechst—which had been part of the I.G. Farben cartel—joined the effort. The association “Die WAAGE. Community for the Promotion of Social Balance” began its activities with a budget of two million DM.

Business Lobbyists Are Infiltrating Clubs and Associations
With the slogan “The Social Market Economy Benefits Everyone,” the lobby group sought to anchor the idea of the social market economy in the West German consciousness as “an ideology that harmonizes the conflicting interests of capital and labor” through newspaper ads with a circulation of over twelve million, commercials shown before movie screenings, posters, and informational events. In total, German business leaders poured 3.8 million DM into the campaign.
Now for the last key player whose public relations efforts were crucial to securing Adenauer’s chancellorship: the Working Group of Democratic Circles (ADK). At the helm of the team was Hans Edgar Jahn, an expert in political marketing. He, too, had earned his stripes during the Third Reich. The association’s bylaws state that the ADK is dedicated to “winning over citizens through objective education.” This does not tell the whole truth. For the ADK, financed by McCloy and the business community, intended to infiltrate the system of clubs and associations with intermediaries in order to conduct political education in the interests of the government and industry.

The organization was to demonstrate its capabilities in the context of military buildup and rearmament: through countless events, West Germans were psychologically prepared for the new German armed forces, so that the socially controversial rearmament could ultimately be successfully implemented. In this PR coup, Jahn was also supported by opinion pollster Elisabeth-Noelle Neumann, who provided expert advice. During this time, his former fellow student helped the still-young discipline of public opinion polling achieve a breakthrough as a tool for political manipulation.

CIA Sponsors German Guerrilla Group
At the same time, the CIA supported the establishment of covert underground movements to divide organizations that spread “hostile ideologies.” For example, the neo-fascist Bund Deutscher Jugend (BDJ) received six-figure sums in German marks to compile lists of politicians deemed hostile to the system, who were to be assassinated in the event of a Soviet invasion. When the guerrilla group’s activities became public in mid-1952, politicians demanded that those behind them be prosecuted. However, this never happened, because the BDJ received financial support from both the Federal Ministry of the Interior and the Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution (BfV)—meaning that even the chancellor was aware of the payments.
The BfV had been established two years earlier in Cologne as an “agency for gathering information on subversive activities directed against the Federal Republic of Germany.” Its first president was Otto John, a trusted ally of the British. Adenauer rejected the “British stooge,” as he called John, and tried to push through his own candidates. However, this failed due to resistance from the British High Commissioner; even his brother-in-law McCloy had no objections to John after vetting him.

The “Old Man” Has Party Colleagues Spied On
Adenauer subsequently withheld the BfV director’s letter of appointment for a year. Afterward, as virtually his first official act, he demanded that he spy on a party colleague. The chancellor was interested in the Eastern contacts of Jakob Kaiser, who—unlike Adenauer—had always advocated a policy of neutrality and reunification, and whom he suspected of having leaked the plans for the “European Defense Community” to the SED.
Adenauer also received intelligence from Reinhard Gehlen, who harbored deep resentment toward John for defecting to the British. To stay up to date, he had his wartime comrade Albert Radke infiltrate the BfV as an informant early on; Radke would later be appointed John’s deputy.
Gehlen himself had been Hitler’s last chief of foreign intelligence. After the surrender, the retired general offered his services to the Americans, who—lacking their own intelligence structure in the East—immediately showed interest in his expertise. In Washington in 1946, he discussed future German-American intelligence cooperation with U.S. President Harry S. Truman and Allen Dulles.

text:
In 1949, Cadillac and Oldsmobile introduced overhead-valve V8s that were supposed to make the flathead obsolete overnight. Valves on top of the combustion chamber instead of beside it. Better breathing. Better thermal efficiency. More power per cubic inch. The OHV V8 was the future. Every manufacturer in Detroit knew it. Including Hudson, which couldn't afford a new engine and kept selling its flathead inline-six while the rest of the industry moved on. Then that flathead six won three consecutive NASCAR Grand National championships. 1951. 1952. 1953. The engine the industry declared dead beat the engines the industry declared superior. On the track that mattered most.

The Hudson 308 displaced 308 cubic inches from an inline-six with an L-head flathead architecture. Bore 3.8125 inches. Stroke 4.50 inches. Massively undersquare. The longest stroke of any American passenger car engine in the early 1950s. That stroke was the first advantage: more leverage on the crankshaft per combustion event meant more torque at lower RPM. The Hudson made its power where stock car racing happened in 1951: between 3,000 and 4,500 RPM on dirt and asphalt ovals where corner exit acceleration mattered more than top-end horsepower. The OHV V8s from Olds and Cadillac revved higher and made more peak horsepower. The Hudson made more torque where the driver's right foot was actually working.

The "Wide Block" was the second advantage. Hudson's engineers designed the 308 with an unusually wide cylinder bore spacing that created room for intake and exhaust ports larger than any other flathead six in production. The flathead's fundamental weakness was always the ports: with valves in the block beside the cylinders, the intake and exhaust passages were short, cramped, and restricted. Hudson's wider block gave the ports more cross-sectional area than competing flatheads could achieve. The 308 breathed better than its architecture should have allowed because the block was wider than it needed to be for the bore diameter. The extra width existed entirely for port volume.

Twin-H Power was the third advantage. Two Carter one-barrel carburetors on a dual-intake manifold, each feeding three cylinders through dedicated runners. One carburetor for cylinders one through three. The other four cylinders are for four through six. Equal-length runners to each group. Better fuel distribution than a single carburetor feeding six cylinders through runners of varying length and geometry. The "H" stood for the horsepower designation. The "Twin" was the dual carburetors. The combination added approximately 25 HP over the single-carburetor version, pushing output to 170 HP at 3,800 RPM with 9.2:1 compression.

A flathead at 9.2:1 compression was the fourth advantage and the one that nobody expected. Conventional flatheads ran 7.0:1 to 8.0:1 because the L-head combustion chamber design created hot spots where the exhaust valve sat exposed to the burning charge, promoting detonation at higher compression ratios. Hudson's engineers redesigned the chamber geometry to reduce the hot-spot tendency, allowing 9.2:1 compression on premium fuel. Higher compression meant more thermal efficiency, which meant more power per cubic inch from the same airflow. The Hudson 308 at 9.2:1 extracted more work from each combustion event than any other flathead in production.

Marshall Teague and Herb Thomas drove the Hornets to three championships against Oldsmobile Rocket 88s that had overhead valves and more peak horsepower. The Hudson won because the total package, displacement, torque curve, Twin-H carburetion, and the step-down unibody chassis that lowered the car's center of gravity below anything else on the track were more competitive as a system than any individual component advantage the OHV V8s offered. The Olds V8 breathed better. The Hudson cornered better. The Olds revved higher. The Hudson pulled harder off the corner. On oval tracks where corner exit matters more than straightaway speed, the Hudson's torque advantage at 3,500 RPM was worth more than the Olds' horsepower advantage at 5,000.

Hudson merged with Nash in 1954 to form American Motors. The 308 was discontinued. The championships ended. The flathead six that had beaten OHV V8s for three straight years was replaced by Nash and AMC engines that were cheaper to produce but carried none of the racing pedigree. The Hudson Hornet's three-year domination of NASCAR remains one of the most improbable winning streaks in American racing history. A flathead inline-six. L-head. Valves in the block. An architecture that Cadillac and Oldsmobile had made obsolete in 1949. Winning championships in 1951, 1952, and 1953 against the engines that were supposed to replace everything like it.

text:
Helping others shows care.
Asking others to help you shows respect.

Leaders need to do both.

When you only give support, you’re showing kindness - but when you’re also willing to ask for it, you’re showing humility. And humility builds trust.

The best leaders don’t pretend to have all the answers. They create an environment where people feel safe to say, “I don’t know,” or, “Can you help me with this?” 

Support is a two-way street.
We all need it, and we can all offer it. 

But there’s a big difference between support and validation. 

When you ask for support, you’re inviting growth. When you ask for validation, you’re inviting ego.

Ask for support, not validation.
Provide support, not judgment.

Life is good.
Marshall

text:
🎤 How is AI reshaping not only what we do, but who we are?

In this episode of @HumansofAIPod, I chat with Andrew McLuhan (@amicusadastra), a poet, writer, researcher, and the founder and director of The McLuhan Institute (@McLinstitute), where he develops and teaches ways of analyzing the nature of technologies and their personal and social effects.

​As the grandson of renowned media theorist Marshall McLuhan and the son of Eric McLuhan, Andrew brings a perspective shaped by three generations of thinking about how media and technology transform human life.​

Andrew explains why artificial intelligence should be understood as more than just another tool. AI is becoming part of the environment around us, reshaping how we think, create, communicate, trust information, and understand ourselves.

​We unpack Marshall McLuhan’s famous idea that “the medium is the message,” why focusing only on the content produced by AI can distract us from its deeper effects, and what earlier shifts—from oral culture and print to radio, television, and the internet—can teach us about the present moment.

We also explore how AI overviews and agents are changing search, discoverability, and the economics of publishing; why the risks of AI extend beyond automation to mental fatigue, weakened judgment, trust erosion, and value misalignment; and how every technology strengthens certain human abilities while allowing others to fade.

Andrew offers a practical way to evaluate new technologies against our personal, family, and community values and asks which parts of ourselves we should be unwilling to outsource.

Andrew also shares his unconventional path from punk rock, poetry, and furniture upholstery to carrying forward the work of Marshall and Eric McLuhan. The result is a wide-ranging conversation about media, culture, identity, consciousness, and the question underneath nearly every debate about AI: not only “What can this technology do?” but “What is it doing to us?”

Corn Futures Weekly Outlook - September 7–11, 2026

Top News Story: September WASDE Slashes Corn Yield to 178.5 Bu., Pulling Production Below 16 Billion Bushels
The corn market capped off a volatile, highly anticipated trading week with modest late week gains following the release of the USDA’s September 11 WASDE report. Integrating its first objective field sample data of the season, the agency trimmed national corn yield projections down 2.2 bushels per acre from August to 178.5 bpa aligning closely with average trade expectations of 178.2 bpa. 

Total 2026 production was cut by 213 million bushels down to 15.8 billion bushels, while 2026/27 domestic ending stocks eased 86 million bushels lower to 1.567 billion bushels. Although some market bulls hoped for a deeper yield reduction toward private tour estimates, the tightening balance sheet lifted the season average farm price by 30 cents to $4.80 per bushel, keeping a solid floor under front month and new crop futures as harvest begins to accelerate.

This Week

The trading week ending Friday, September 11, 2026, concluded with futures consolidating near multi-month high boundaries. Managed money accounts maintained a firm net-long stance, absorbing seasonal commercial hedging pressure as early combine runs expanded beyond southern states into the central Belt.

Tuesday’s delayed USDA Crop Progress report (issued post-Labor Day) showed national corn condition ratings sliding another point to 56 percent good to excellent. Development continues at a rapid pace, with 95 percent in the dough stage, 74 percent dented, 23 percent reaching maturity, and initial national harvest reaching 5 percent complete. 

On the processing side, Thursday’s EIA report showed daily fuel ethanol production easing slightly to 1.092 million barrels per day, while commercial inventories drew down 420,000 barrels to 24.3 million barrels to reflect strong early-autumn blending and export demand.

Price Action

CME Group Data as of Friday Market Close, September 11, 2026:

September 2026 (ZCU26): $5.09-4 (Change from Monday Open: -$0.02-4)
December 2026 (ZCZ26): $5.32-2 (Change from Monday Open: -$0.03-6)
March 2027 (ZCH27): $5.51-0 (Change from Monday Open: -$0.04-4)

Cash Trade and Technicals:
Settlement Prices: December corn held firm following post-WASDE trade to settle Friday at $5.32-2 as commercial short covering offset immediate profit-taking.

National Avg Cash Price: $4.87 (Reflecting strong interior processor demand as combines begin initial runs).

Local Basis (O’Neill, NE): Cash basis across north-central Nebraska remains firm at roughly 20 to 24 cents under September futures ($4.85–$4.89 flat). Local ethanol facilities and commercial cattle feeders continue to offer attractive spot premiums for immediate delivery ahead of local harvest volume.

Technical Levels: 1st Resistance: $5.40; 1st Support: $5.22.

RSI Indicator: 63.4 (Holding in a solid, constructive neutral-bullish range).

Key Market Factors
WASDE Yield Cuts: The USDA's yield cut to 178.5 bpa and production trim to 15.8 billion bushels confirms that mid-August heat permanently clipped national crop potential.

Tightening Ending Stocks: Projected 2026/27 ending stocks dropped to 1.567 billion bushels, tightening the U.S. supply cushion.

Initial Harvest Progress: National harvest reached 5 percent complete, with early yield reports verifying variable field results across drought-impacted pockets of the Western Belt.

Robust Export Baseline: U.S. export sales commitments remain steady at 3.3 billion bushels, supported by constrained exports out of Black Sea channels and heat-damaged European yields.

USDA Upcoming
With September government data behind the market, trade focus shifts to harvest momentum and early field yield reports:

Weekly Crop Progress (September 14): Will track mature crop percentages and evaluate harvest expansion across Nebraska, Iowa, and Illinois.

Weekly Export Sales & EIA Ethanol Data (September 16–17): Monitoring whether global end-users continue booking commitments at $5.30+ December futures.

Funds Activity
Managed money managers maintained a cautiously bullish posture through the week's report events.

Net Position: Speculative funds were modest net buyers on Thursday post-report before taking minor profits on Friday to close out the week.

Sentiment: Institutional sentiment remains constructive as smaller crop size projections and elevated farm gate price estimates protect downside risk.

Current Bias: Moderately Bullish.

Outlook for the Week Ahead
The corn complex enters mid-September anchored by solid technical support at $5.22 on December corn. Heading into next week, December futures are expected to trade within a $5.25 to $5.42 range as seasonal harvest pressure interacts with tight interior basis levels. Unless widespread combine yield results across the central Belt indicate an even smaller crop than the USDA's 178.5 bpa estimate, heavy harvest hedge selling will likely keep near-term rallies capped near the $5.40 mark.

Key Events:
September 14: USDA Weekly Crop Progress (4:00 PM ET).
September 16: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report.

September 17: USDA Weekly Export Sales.

Trend: Range-Bound / Constructive Underlying Tone. For agricultural producers and elevator operators in north-central Nebraska, December futures near $5.32 offer a strong pricing floor. Finalize remaining spot sales to capture strong local basis ahead of harvest pressure, and evaluate scale in hedge targets or price floors on new-crop production on any post WASDE bounces toward $5.40.

Little Office of the Blessed Virgin Mary

FRIDAY

Morning Prayer
God, come to my assistance.
- Lord, make haste to help me

Glory to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit
as it was in the beginning, is now, and will be forever.  Amen.

Virgin of virgins,
I choose you today
as my sovereign, my queen, my empress,
and I declare myself, as I am in fact,
your servant and your slave.
I invoke your royal name of Mary,
that is, sovereign Lady,
and beg of you with all my heart
to admit me into the privileged circle¡
of your family
as one of your servants,
to do your will
as a humble slave and a loving child.
As a sign of your acceptance
engrave on my heart
with the fire of your love,
not the brand of an unwilling slave,
but those two gracious words of the angel:
Ave Maria.
As long as I draw breath
may your burning love ensure
that I bear these words
in my heart and in my memory,
and that until my dying breath
my will may be always on fire
with my great desire to serve you,
my sovereign and my queen,
glorious in your majesty.
Though I am in every way unworthy
of so honorable a title,
I resolve sincerely to be your slave,
to serve you wholeheartedly,
to protect your name,
and that of your Son,
against every insult,
as far as it may rest with me,
and never to allow anyone in my charge
to offend your Son in any way.
By your tender love for your Son,
by the glories you have received
from the Most Holy Trinity,
do not reject me from your service
but as my sovereign and my queen
preside over all my actions,
command whatever you will,
direct all my work,
remedy all its defects.
During my whole life
rule over me
as your servant and slave.
At the hour of my death,
as I hope for
at the end of my loving servitude
among the privileged members of your family,
receive my soul and escort it
into the presence of God.

St Bartolome de Los Rios(1580-1652)

PSALMODY

Ant.1 My soul clings to you, Lord Jesus Christ.

Psalm 51
O God, have mercy on me
Your inmost being must be renewed, and you must put on the new man. (Eph 4:23-24)
Have mercy on me, God, in your kindness.
In your compassion blot out my offense.
O wash me more and more from my guilt
and cleanse me from my sin.
My offenses truly I know them;
my sin is always before me
Against you, you alone, have I sinned;
what is evil in your sight I have done.
That you may be justified when you give sentence
and be without reproach when you judge,
O see, in guilt I was born,
a sinner was I conceived.
Indeed you love truth in the heart;
then in the secret of my heart teach me wisdom.
O purify me, then I shall be clean;
O wash me, I shall be whiter than snow.
Make me hear rejoicing and gladness,
that the bones you have crushed may thrill.
From my sins turn away your face
and blot out all my guilt.
A pure heart create for me, O God,

text:
🚨George Russell has shared his concerns around “the big question mark” that will impact the rest of the Spanish Grand Prix weekend, with the Mercedes driver predicting that tyre degradation will play a significant role.

After admitting that his team mate Kimi Antonelli, who leads the standings by 66 points, has done “a better job” this season, Russell went on to top the times in the first hour of practice at the brand-new Madring.

He then dropped to P5 behind the Italian, the Ferrari pair and Racing Bulls’ Arvid Lindblad in FP2, and later offered his thoughts on getting to grips with the latest addition to the calendar.

“It was very fun driving the track for the first time,” he said. “It’s always a great experience driving a new circuit. FP1 was a strong session. FP2 we made some set-up changes – it wasn’t quite as good, so we’ll probably revert back on that. So far, so good.

“I think there’s a big question mark over the tyre degradation. In FP1 with the tyre degradation we all had, we think a six-stop race would probably have been the fastest way!

“I don’t think anybody’s going to do a six-stop race on Sunday and I’m sure tyre deg will be better, but with that big long corner – La Monumental – it really hurts the tyres. That’s going to be a real challenge for everyone.”

La Monumental is arguably the most striking feature of the Madring with its extreme banking and horseshoe shape, but FP1 and FP2 showed that it can be punishing for both the drivers and their tyres.

Mercedes Deputy Team Principal Bradley Lord appeared less concerned about regular tyre degradation, focusing instead on the loss of running that came as a result of Lindblad’s crash on Friday afternoon.

“You could see some unusual tyre effects just because they’re going to be running so hot,” he explained. “You’ve got a lot of cornering sequences without a real chance for the tyres to have a breather around the lap.

“It’s not like it’s corner, long straight, corner – it’s corner after corner after corner. How the tyres cope with that is going to be decisive, so even though it’s a very smooth surface and wear may not be as high as we might expect, we might see some other thermal effects that could push you into more stops than the computers before might expect you to make.

“I think it was a very solid day and a good feeling. We’ve come out of Monza with a bit of a spring in our step and need to reset and then tick all the boxes on a busy Friday. It was good to see both drivers up there in both sessions.

“We didn’t really see the single lap play out in FP2 because of the crash, and then that curtailed the long runs so again, it leaves us with more unknowns than maybe we’d like as F1 teams going into the race on Sunday. That generally produces the unexpected and something exciting for the fans.” (via F1) #Lord #Russell #SpanishGP #F1

text:
Guards/Twins

Messick’s underlying profile is genuinely strong: 26.1% K, 6.8% BB, 31.4% chase, 26.3% whiff, .271 xwOBA, .222 xBA and .335 xSLG allowed. He is not just living off ERA suppression. The contact quality is excellent too: 87.3 mph EV, 32.7% hard-hit and only 5.0% barrels.

Minnesota gives him enough strikeout pockets without being an all-or-nothing offense. Royce Lewis is at 24.8% K / 32.4% whiff, Kreidler 22.0/30.9, Alex Jackson 33.3/30.7, Walker Jenkins 26.8/33.3, while Clemens, Bell, Larnach and Culpepper all offer either chase or whiff paths. The softer part of the lineup is Jeffers/Lee/Keaschall, so this is not a matchup where I would ladder him aggressively, but 5 is still a very reachable threshold.

The market is the part that really matters. FanDuel currently has Messick O5.5 Ks +112, versus Under -142. Bradley is O5.5 +100.  The broader game market has Cleveland around -120 to -122, Minnesota around +100/+101, and the total at 7.5. 

That +112 requires only 47.2% to break even. For a pitcher averaging 6.2 Ks per appearance with this swing-and-miss/contact-suppression profile, I make 6+ closer to roughly the 52–55% range before lineup confirmation. That is enough for a legitimate price edge.

Cleveland is 74-73 and this series matters materially in the AL race. Minnesota is 69-77 and can still play spoiler, but Cleveland has the stronger bullpen profile and one of the better defenses in baseball. A current series preview has Cleveland’s bullpen third in MLB with a 2.86 ERA and the defense sixth overall. 

That matters for Messick because Cleveland does not need to push him deep if traffic develops. For the K prop, I want the strikeouts to come through efficiency over five-to-six innings rather than relying on a seven-inning workload.

Taj Bradley is more volatile. His 27.3% K looks attractive, but he carries a 10.1% BB rate, 90.9 mph EV and 45.1% hard-hit allowed. Cleveland also has several difficult K victims near the top: DeLauter 14.7%, Genao 14.0%, José Ramírez 12.8%, Rocchio 14.4%, Kwan 9.9%. That is why I still prefer Messick O5.5 +112 over Bradley O5.5 +100.

Cleveland ML -120/-122 — B+

Messick + bullpen + defense gives Cleveland the cleaner full-game pitching path. Current market consensus is around -122.

text:
Phillies/Braves 

Atlanta comes in 86-61, four games ahead of Philadelphia in the NL East, so this is a legitimately high-leverage divisional series rather than a meaningless September spot. Sale has also been excellent recently: over his last five starts he owns a 2.18 ERA with a 1.55 FIP, and he has allowed only three earned runs across 19 innings against Philadelphia this year. Nola, however, has quietly turned his season around too, posting a 2.31 ERA over his last eight starts. 

The market reflects that pitching gap: Atlanta is roughly -187 to -196, Braves -1.5 around +112 to +135, and the total is 7.5. 

Statcast read

Sale’s underlying profile is elite:

30.6% K
4.8% BB
36.9% chase
30.1% whiff
.272 xwOBA allowed
.222 xBA
.332 xSLG
5.9% barrel rate

That combination is exactly what we want in a high-leverage start: he misses bats, does not issue free passes, and suppresses damaging contact.

Philadelphia does have some strikeout pockets:

Schwarber 32.4%
Derek Hill 33.0%
Marsh 24.9%
Turner 21.4%
Realmuto 21.3%
Harper 21.2%

But this lineup also contains several extremely difficult K victims:

Arraez 4.3%
Bohm 14.7%
Stott 17.2%
Crawford 17.7%

Nola is the more interesting pitcher from a hidden-edge standpoint. His season ERA looks mediocre, but the process is substantially better:

24.4% K
7.8% BB
32.9% chase
27.6% whiff
.307 xwOBA
.238 xBA

His curveball usage at 33.1% is particularly important because Atlanta has several aggressive hitters who can be expanded: Harris has a massive 44.5% chase rate, Albies 38.3%, Dubón 37.8%, Baldwin 33.8%, Riley 32.5%.

So I do not view this as “Sale elite, Nola trash.” That is exactly the kind of lazy handicap we want to avoid.

Weather matters a lot here

This remains the biggest complication.

Current forecasts are inconsistent but still show meaningful thunderstorm risk around Atlanta today. Weather Underground has roughly a 50–80% daytime thunderstorm chance depending on station, while a more game-specific projection has around 40% precipitation at game time. 

That means I am not making starter outs a primary bet yet.

A pregame delay is usually manageable. A mid-game interruption is disastrous for:
Sale outs
Nola outs
F5 unders
starter-heavy NRFI/F5 positions

So radar 30–60 minutes before first pitch matters more here than in almost any other game today.

The important nuance is that Nola’s breaking stuff is still legitimately excellent. That 95th-percentile breaking-ball run value is why his recent improvement makes sense and why I would not blindly fade him.

But his fastball ecosystem is completely different.

Nola: 1st-percentile fastball value.
Sale: 95th-percentile fastball value.

That is a massive distinction in a postseason-type divisional matchup. Nola is much more dependent on getting hitters into counts where his curve can finish them. If Atlanta forces him into fastball counts or simply refuses to chase the breaking ball, the vulnerability shows up quickly.

Sale has far fewer escape hatches opponents can target. His stuff works across the board: elite whiff, elite chase, elite command, elite contact suppression, elite run value.

Sale U2.5 ERA + Braves -1.5 at +120/+125 or better — B+/A-

The starting-pitching gap is more substantial underneath than Nola’s recent ERA alone suggests. Good SGP IMO. 

NRFI — B+/A- if weather is clean
Both starters have a real first-inning path, but weather still matters. 

Nola O5.5 Ks around -105/even — B+ value angle

Excellent breaking stuff versus several Atlanta swing-and-miss pockets.

#MLB

text:
George Foreman sold 120 million grills with his face on the box and made more from that than from every fight of his career. He was offered a flat endorsement fee like every other athlete. He asked for 45% of the profits instead.

He only went looking for a product because he had gone broke.

He grew up mugging people in Houston. One night the police chased him under a house and he covered himself in sewage mud so the dogs could not smell him, listening to his mother's voice in his head saying nobody in this family has ever been a thief.

He won the title, made millions, retired at 28 and spent 10 years preaching on a street corner. Then the youth center he had opened in Houston ran out of money.

"There wasn't a dime in the mail."

The 20 minutes attached to this post are him alone in front of the Oxford Union, telling it without a host and without flinching. The mugging, the money, and what it cost him to go back and get it.

Watch the part where a preacher passes a plate around for him.

He is in a church he has been speaking at for three days, and the preacher takes up a collection for the youth center. The man counts it, says it is not enough, and passes it again. Foreman stands there thinking about the Rolls Royces he used to own.

He decided in that room he would never ask anyone for anything again. He was 38, he weighed 315 pounds, and the plan was to become heavyweight champion of the world.

7 years later he knocked out a man young enough to be his son and took the title back at 45.

Everyone wrote to tell him not to do it. Not one of those letters had money in it. That is why he ended up asking for a percentage instead of a cheque.

A fee pays you for being famous. A percentage pays you for being right, and it keeps paying after the fame stops working.

Nobody is confused about which of those two is better. The problem is that the fee arrives on Friday and the percentage might arrive never.

He says the thing athletes forget is that $20 million has nothing to do with tomorrow. You will nod at that and still take the cheque.

He was not the first person shown that grill. The company had it sitting there and nobody wanted to be bothered with it. He was just the first who asked for a share instead of a fee, and that question paid him more than both his titles did.

text:
Read and stop crying...

Though there are differences of opinion, both Persian and Sikh sources agree that the Guru posed a political challenge to the state security and the authority of the Mughals. Such political challenges, during the 17th century were not tolerated and therefore brutally suppressed. Whilst acknowledging that a religious figure was executed, it is of utmost importance, to judge the event based on the accepted norms of the 17th century and not with a 21st century inclination.
Points to consider :
The popular account of the Sikh Guru, being executed for his support of Hindu Kashmiri's is doubtful, for it first appears several decades after the execution of the Guru. It also should be noted that Aurangzeb was not present during the execution, due his occupation with the Pashtun revolt, therefore accounts of Aurangzeb requesting the Guru to perform a miracle and forcing him to accept Islam needs to be questioned.
For the historians, difficulties have been created because the execution of Guru Tegh Bahadur at Delhi in 1675 is not mentioned in any of the contemporary Persian sources. Nor are there any Sikh contemporary accounts, those written towards the end of the 18th century depending on "the testimony of trustworthy Sikhs''. They are, therefore, often conflicting. The earliest account of the events leading to the Guru's execution is in Siyar ul Mutakharm by Ghulam Husain in 1780, more than a century after the event of the Gurus execution.
Below are a number of accounts on why the Sikh Guru was executed. These are accounts, which may be considered factual, an interpretation of events, questionable, or perhaps an accumulation of events which led to the execution of the Sikh Guru.
1) The traditional Sikh narrative.
Emperor Aurangzeb, a zealous Muslim, aspired to forcefully convert Hindu’s into the fold of Islam. Moreover, since the time of Jahangir, the Mughal Emperors viewed the Sikh Guru’s with suspicion. During the era of Guru Teg Bahadur, the Kashmiri Hindu Pandits, against their will, were being forced into the fold of Islam, via Mughal authorities of Kashmir (Saif Khan is generally named), as per the injunctions of Aurangzeb.
The Kashmiri Hindus pleaded with the Guru to intercede on their behalf. Moreover the Mughal officials across the Punjab began mistreating the peasantry and under the orders of Aurangzeb, a number of Sikh temples were confiscated, destroyed, or converted into mosques. Thus the Guru took it upon himself to travel to Delhi and to boldly reprimand the bigoted emperor for his policies.
The Guru was treated coldly and humiliated at the court. The emperor asked the Guru to convert and perform a miracle, but when the Guru heroically refused and stood firm by his faith, he was executed.
2) The account of Guru Gobind Singh in the “Bachittar Natak”.
Bachittar Natak written by Tegh Bahadur's son and the tenth Guru, Gobind Singh is often cited as the only Sikh contemporary source of the Guru’s execution. Tegh Bahadur is described as the protector of the sacred tilak and the sacred thread of Hindus. The book also states that the Guru courted martyrdom to uphold his religious beliefs.
Note : Satish Chandra questions the use of Bachittar Natak as a contemporary source. "Bachittar Natak is a religious account. It is not history in the strict sense. Moreover, it does not explicitly mention that Hindus came to the Guru and protested. It does not even mention that Tegh Bahadur was asked by Emperor Aurangzeb to perform a miracle to prove his divine powers".
Further, the ‘Bachittat Natak’ is a part of the ‘Dasam Grant’, a text that has 30 different adaptions today, which has been an issue of controversy for the Sikh community.
Robin Rinehart states : “The Dasam Granth is a 1,428-page anthology of diverse compositions attributed to the tenth Guru of Sikhism, Guru Gobind Singh, and a topic of great controversy among the Sikhs. The controversy stems from two major issues : a substantial portion of the Dasam Granth relates tales from Hindu mythology, suggesting a disconnect from normative Sikh theology; and a long composition entitled Charitropakhian tells several hundred rather graphic stories about illicit liaisons between men and women.
Sikhs have debated whether the text deserves status as a "scripture" or should be read instead as "literature." Sikh scholars have also long debated whether Guru Gobind Singh in fact authored the entire Dasam Granth”.
3) The account of Sri Gur Panth Prakash : Rattan Singh Bhangoo, 1841.
The Panth Prakash written between 1809 and 1841, and is considered as a Sikh primary source. The source follows the Sikh narrative that Aurangzeb and his ministers began oppressing the Kashmiri Hindu’s when they did not accept to convert to the faith of Islam. The Brahmins gathered together and decided to write a petition which was dispatched to the Guru.
Note : Interesting to note that Brahmins, not just from Kashmir but also from Benares and the wider Gangetic plains are mentioned in this source to have wrote to the Guru which is not mentioned in other sources. Moreover there is no official edict from Aurangzeb demanding the conversion of the Hindu’s from Kashmir.
Satish Chandra states : “However, the persecution of the Hindus is not mentioned in any of the histories of Kashmir, including the one written by Narayan Kaul in 1710. Saif Khan, the Mughal governor of Kashmir, is famous as a builder of bridges. He was a humane and broad-minded person who had appointed a Hindu to advise him in administrative matters. His successor after 1671, Iftekhar Khan, was anti-Shia but there are no references to his persecuting the Hindus."
4) The cotemporary account of Bhimsen, a Hindu subject of Aurangzeb, Tarikh-i Dilkusha, 1707.
Bhimsen refers to Guru Nanak's service (naukari), his association with religious men, his disciples in the territory of Lahore and Multan, his compositions, and his deputies. No country, city, township or village was there now without his followers. Offerings were carried to his 'descendants' who are his 'successors'. They spent their life in splendour and some of them took to the path of rebellion. Guru Tegh Bahadur was among them. He called himself 'Padshah' and a large number of people gathered around him. When Aurangzeb came to know of his activity, he summoned the Guru to the Court, and he was executed.
5) Account of Muhammad Qasim, Ibratnama, 1719.
"The Emperor (Aurangzeb) had regard for royal power but he also associated with religious men. Some of the mystics aligned with him of their own accord. Others, like Sarmad, tasted martyrdom. Guru Tegh Bahadur was in the latter category. He was condemned not only for religious reasons but also because he lived in great splendour and his followers claimed sovereignty for him. In fact, a large number of people had begun to follow Guru Har Rai (who is wrongly mentioned, must be Guru Teg Bahadur), and to glorify him."
6) The account of Khafi Khan, a Mughal historian, Muntakhab-ul-Lubab, 1722.
"There is a sect of infidels called Guru, more commonly known as the Sikhs. Their chief, who dresses as a fakir, has a fixed residence near Lahore. From old times he has built temples in all the towns and populous places, and has appointed one of his followers to preside in each temple as his deputy. When anyone of the sect brought presents or offerings for the Guru to the temple, the deputy had to collect them, and after deducting sufficient for his own food and expenses, his duty was to send the balance faithfully to the Guru.
This sect consists principally of Jats and Khatris of the Punjab and of other tribes of infidels. When Aurangzeb got knowledge of those matters, he ordered these deputy Gurus to be removed and the temples to be pulled down."
7) Account of Ghulam Husain, 1782, official Mughal court historian.
“Tegh Bahadur, the eighth successor of (Guru) Nanak became a man of authority with a large number of followers. (In fact) Several thousand persons used to accompany him as he moved from place to place and thus aspired sovereign power. His contemporary Hafiz Adam, a faqir belonging to the group of Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi's followers, had also come to have a large number of murids and followers.
Both these men (Guru Tegh Bahadur and Hafiz Adam) used to move throughout the Punjab, adopting a habit of coercion and extortion. Tegh Bahadur used to collect money from Hindus and Hafiz Adam from Muslims. The royal waqia navis (news reporters and intelligence agents) wrote to the Emperor Aurangzeb of their manner of activity, added that if their authority increased they could become even refractory”.
Note : Satish Chandra questions the above, as he argues that Hafiz Adam was either banished or died before the events. Moreover a number of Sikh and Punjabi Historians such as Dr Ganda Singh, Khuswant Singh and A.C Banerjee have preferred the use of the following translation of the above as the translation makes no mention of ‘subsiting by plunder’.
"Tegh Bahadur, gathering many disciples, became powerful, and thousands of people accompanied him. A contemporary of his, Hafiz Adam, who was a fakir belonging to the order of Sheikh Ahmed Sirhindi, had gathered about him a great multitude of followers. Both of these took to the practice of levying forcible exactions and moved about in the land of the Punjab. Tegh Bahadur took money from Hindus and Hafiz Adam from Mussalmans. The royal news writers wrote to the Emperor that the two fakirs, one Hindu and the other Muslim named so-and-so, had taken to the practice. It would not be strange if, with the increase of their influence, they created trouble."
📷 Sohan Lal, Umdat Ut Tawarikh, historical document on the life and times of Maharaja Ranjit Singh,1839.
"With the passage of time, thousands of soldiers and horsemen used to be with him and camels and goods of all kinds remained at his disposal. Furthermore, those who were refractory towards the amirs, the zamindars, the ijaraddars, the diwans and the officials in general used to take refuge with Guru Tegh Bahadur. Regardless of the numbers present with the Guru, they were all fed by him. Pain inevitably follows comfort.
Some degraded persons reported to Emperor Alamgir that Guru Tegh Bahadur was staying in the country (Doab) of Malwa (in Punjab) with thousands of soldiers and horsemen, whosoever was refractory towards the officials took refuge with him. They warned the Emperor that if no notice of the Guru was taken it would be an incitement to insurrection; and that if he was allowed to continue his activities for a long time, it would be extremely difficult to deal with him (later).''
9) Account of JD Cunningham, 1849.
For JD Cunningham, the story of the Guru’s execution due to his opposition to the alleged forceful conversion of Kashmiri Hindu’s makes at best, simplistic reading. Cunningham argues that the affair rather stemmed from the internal politics of the Sikh community at the time. JD Cunningham claims that the accession of Teg Bahadur as the Guru was contested politically.
Guru Har Rai (D 1661), had two sons, the elder being Ram Rai (15 years of age) and the younger Har Kishan (7 years of age). However, since Ram Rai was born through a “handmaiden” (or a lesser wife), Har Kishan’s appointment was considered more appropriate. The matter was contested, and had reached the court of Aurangzeb. It is alleged that Aurangzeb had recognised Har Kishan, the 7 year old as the legitimate Guru of the Sikh’s, but on his way back from Delhi, the infant Guru died due to contraction of small pox. It is claimed that the infant Guru, before dying appointed Teg Bahadur, a relative, as the next Guru.
Though the transition of one Guru to another did not lead to violence, it did however stir divisions and political intrigue within the fledgling Sikh community. As an example, Guru Hargobind’s authority was challenged by his uncle, whose own son and later his grandson set themselves up as alternative line of Gurus.
Claimants would often appeal to influential members of the Sikh community, known as the ‘Masanads’. Richard Eaton, explains their role in the following : “the gurus masands, - the institutional link between the gurus and the bulk of their followers were appropriating power for themselves, appointing their own deputies for collecting offerings from the faithful, following rival claimants to the guruship, and interfering in succession struggles.
But claimants, not only vied for the support of the masands, but also the local Mughal authority for recognition and in fact some received favourable grants to placate their claims, for example Dhir Mahl, a claimant was granted a revenue free land in Kartarpur by Shah Jahan and Ram Rai also was granted a revenue free land (four to seven villagers) in Dehradun by Aurangzeb, were a Sikh Gudwara was constructed.
Nonetheless the appointment of Teg Bahadur had been questioned by a total of 22 claimants to the Guruship, including Ram Rai (Dehradun), Dhir Mahlh (Kartarpur), and Harji (Amritser). In fact the Guru himself was opposed by his younger brother Suraj Mal and unable to find a location at a safe distance from the claimants, attempted to form new political alliances so that he could compete with the contesting claims to the Guruship. Situations led to an individual named Shihan, a devotee of Dhir Mahl to follow an attempt on the Guru’s life with a matchlock, as he failed; he and his men are reported to have ransacked the Guru’s property.
As Teg Bahadur’s difficulties increased, he subsequently was forced to move to the Shivalik hills. A devotee of the Guru and a number of fellow accomplices retaliated by plundering the property of Dhir Mahl, however matters seemed to have settled as the Guru, benevolently returned the property to Dhir Mahl. However Dhir Mahl continued his opposition and attracted followers eventually forming the Sikh sect known as ‘Dhir Mahlias’.
Ram Rai however remained the most incessant rival. Ram Rai wanted to secure the Guruship for himself, and thus plotted incessantly against Teg Bahadur, lobbying with a few prominent Sikh leaders and trying to convince the Sikh community that he was, in fact, the rightful spiritual descant of Nanak’s Sikhism. His claims however were rebuked as Teg Bahadur was firmly supported and recognised as the Sikh Guru. Ram Rai would thus remain a thorn at the side of Teg Bahadur and continued to assert his claims but to no avail. Ram Rai and his follower came to be known as the Sikh sect of ‘Ramraiya’.
At this time, Teg Bahadur also gained the attention of the Jaipur Chieftain Raja Ram Singh, who requested the Guru to travel on campaign to Aasam with him. It is reported that once the Guru returned to the Punjab, it was reported to Delhi (Ram Rai’s involvement is questioned) that the Guru was involved in certain anti state activities which are quoted below:
“After a time Teg Bahadur returned to the Punjab and bought a piece of ground, now known as Makhowal, on the banks of the Sutlej, and close to Kiratpur, the chosen residence of his father. But the hostility and the influence of Ram Rai still persuaded him and the ordinary Sikh accounts represent him, a pious and innocent instructor of men, as one once more arraigned at Delhi in the character of a criminal; but the truth seems to be that Tegh Bahadur followed the example of his father with unequal footsteps, and that, choosing for his haunts the wastes between Hansi and the Sutlej, he subsisted himself and his disciples by plunder, in a way, indeed, that rendered him not unpopular with the peasantry.
He is further credibly represented to have leagued with a Muslim zealot, named Adam Hafiz and to have levied contributions upon rich Hindus, whilst his confederate did the same upon wealthy Muslims. They have a ready asylum to all fugitives and their power interfered with the prosperity of the country, the imperial troops marched against them, and they were at last defeated and made prisoners. The Muslim was banished, but Aurangzeb determined that the Sikh should be put to death”.
10) Account of James Browne, 1788.
Browne, in his India tracts claim that Aurangzeb had executed the Guru due to claiming the honorific, "Sacha Padshah" (the truthful King). Cunningham asserts that it was around this time that the Sikh Gurus came to talk of themselves, and to be regarded by their followers as 'Sacha Padshah'.
Note : The meaning of Sacha Padshah could have several interpretations, including a veritable interpretation. The term could have likely been used in the spiritual context; in fact the Sufi saints were also referred in this manner by their disciples. Therefore Brown's assertions could be questioned as Aurangzeb is unlikely to have misinterpreted such an honorific, for he would have been familiar with such rhetoric, in fact he was also referred to as “Zinda Pir”, or the living saint during his life time.
However it needs to be noted that had the Guru claimed the honorific 'Sacha Padshah', and at the same time carried out unrest in the Punjab, as cited by Bhimsen, it was a possibility that the Mughal's not only considered and interpreted the Guru's actions as a revolt, but also a challenge to the Timurid notion of sacred kingship which was associated with the person of the Emperor.
11) Account of Audrey Truschke, 2017.
Aurangzeb’s most controversial state killing is his execution of Tegh Bahadur, the ninth Sikh guru, in 1675. In the mid- to late-17th century, Tegh Bahadur caused unrest in Mughal-controlled Punjab, thereby posing a threat to state security and Aurangzeb’s authority. Contemporary Mughal sources do not even mention his execution, probably because, from a state perspective, it was unexceptional.
Many moderns perceive this episode as a case where an Islamist king sought to stamp out Sikhism in its early days. A commonly repeated story is that Aurangzeb asked Tegh Bahadur to convert to Islam and then executed him when the Sikh guru stood firm in his faith. Given Aurangzeb’s typically harsh actions against state enemies, I find it unlikely that conversion, even if offered, would have saved Tegh Bahadur.
12) Account of Abraham Eraly, 1997.
Abraham Eraly, not an Aurangzeb enthusiast notes the following: “The third major uprising was that of the Sikhs. This was of a different class altogether from the other two, though here too the issue was more political then religious. The Sikhs had by the mid seventeenth century transformed themselves from a syncretism religious sect into a political community. Their guru was as much a monarch as a spiritual head, and was therefore a potential threat to the Mughal authority. Political as well as religious considerations therefore induced Aurangzeb to bear down on the Sikhs. This drove Teg Bahadur, the Sikh Guru into rebellion, but he was arrested, tortured, and beheaded”.
Note : Interestingly  certain accounts refer to the followers of the Guru proclaiming his sovereignty. Richard Eaton notes that with regards to Guru Gobind Singh, that ‘Alamgir ordered local officials to leave the guru alone as long as he adopted a modest life style like other spiritual mendicants, but to make him submit and pay taxes if imitated kingly ways’. Here it appears that Aurangzeb had no issue with the Guru, as long he followed the path of his predecessors, but if they adopted ways of kingship, they must, like other vassals, recognise the Mughal authority and pay taxes.

text:
This scripture is fitting for today...

Psalm 27 — 
The Lord is my light and my salvation;
whom shall I fear?
The Lord is the strength of my life;
of whom shall I be afraid?
When the wicked, even mine enemies and my foes,
came upon me to eat up my flesh,
they stumbled and fell.
Though an host should encamp against me,
my heart shall not fear:
though war should rise against me,
in this will I be confident.
One thing have I desired of the Lord,
that will I seek after;
that I may dwell in the house of the Lord
all the days of my life,
to behold the beauty of the Lord,
and to inquire in his temple.
For in the time of trouble
he shall hide me in his pavilion:
in the secret of his tabernacle shall he hide me;
he shall set me up upon a rock.
And now shall mine head be lifted up
above mine enemies round about me:
therefore will I offer in his tabernacle
sacrifices of joy;
I will sing, yea, I will sing praises unto the Lord.
Hear, O Lord, when I cry with my voice:
have mercy also upon me, and answer me.
When thou saidst, Seek ye my face;
my heart said unto thee,
Thy face, Lord, will I seek.
Hide not thy face far from me;
put not thy servant away in anger:
thou hast been my help;
leave me not, neither forsake me,
O God of my salvation.
When my father and my mother forsake me,
then the Lord will take me up.
Teach me thy way, O Lord,
and lead me in a plain path,
because of mine enemies.
Deliver me not over unto the will of mine enemies:
for false witnesses are risen up against me,
and such as breathe out cruelty.
I had fainted,
unless I had believed to see the goodness of the Lord
in the land of the living.
Wait on the Lord:
be of good courage,
and he shall strengthen thine heart:
wait, I say, on the Lord.

text:
🌍 Your passport is now worth less than your employer! ➡️🏢

Sounds crazy, right? But hear me out. There is a method in my madness. 😊 

For millennia, where you were from shaped almost everything about your life.

That's changing. Fast!

Countries mostly provide you with tangible benefits: roads, police, firefighters, and perhaps, if you're lucky, healthcare. And that's assuming you're not living in a corrupt 2nd/3rd world country run by a dictator or kleptocracy (but that's a different subject altogether).

In return for these oh-so-wonderful "benefits", they take 20–55% of your income in taxes.

But the world is becoming digital-first. And by that I mean an AI‑driven world. The real leverage isn't physical infrastructure anymore. No, no, it’s now:

🔐 How strong is your cybersecurity
🤖 Which AI models can you access
⚙️ How much compute/tokens can you burn
🧠 What internal tools, automations, and infrastructure can you access
🚀 And lastly, whether you can stay on the cutting edge of AI

No country is going to give you unlimited tokens, internal LLMs, or world‑class development tools.

Great companies will.

A great employer can offer you:

✅ Access to the latest (sometimes internal) AI models
✅ Self‑hosted/local models and powerful internal software
✅ Serious investment in your skills and education
✅ Proper security and infrastructure so you can build fast and safely

In other words, a company is the new country.

Sounds bizarre if you think about it, but that's the world we're living in currently.

Over the next decade, who you work for will matter far more than which passport you hold.

We're already seeing AI companies with more practical power than many nation-states. 

Can you imagine 10,000 coordinated AI agents targeting a country's digital infrastructure?

That's not sci‑fi anymore. It's now sci-fa (is that even a word?)

So if you're planning your career in 2026 and beyond, don't just ask:

"Which country should I move to?" 🌎

Start asking:

"Which company's infrastructure, tools, and AI ecosystem do I want to plug my life into?" 

Because your employer might end up being the most important "country" you ever join.

text:
September of senior year in High School walking into the cafeteria on a passing period and hearing a friend of mine from band class, he was the drummer, say "a plane has struck the twin towers." I didn't quite believe it. It was about 9am, I was hungry because I'd skipped breakfast, but both planes had struck while I was in second period and I was moving on to the next class. I remember thinking "well the towers survived that other bombing, they'll be ok." I went off to class.

My school was in a Connecticut commuter suburb of New York City. A large number of families had at least one parent who drove into the city for work. I don't think the next class had a TV in it, the whole school was trying to stay normal and carry on with the day. Somehow we got news in that third period that the Pentagon was also hit.

The damn burst and the day then blurs. Sit, move from room to room listening/watching for news, talking about news. I remember they had the footage on in the lunchroom on TVs and whether live or in replay we saw the towers fall. Those who had family and relatives working in the city were almost holding their breath and you didn't want to talk to them about it because you knew they didn't know. This was before ubiquitous cell phones, and an era of spotty service, so the news was coming in at a trickle.

Late in the day before we headed home the Principal got on the speaker system and offered some solemn words. He gave the facts as he knew them, then talked about our nation, I think he might even have mentioned God, then he said after school activities were canceled and advised folks to remain calm and return home. By the end of the day we knew at least a few people from town had died or were missing. We later came to find out twelve people closely connected to the town in total died, one a father of school aged kids that lived around the corner from my friend. It turned out another one was a guy my older brother used to play basketball with, Tyler Ugolyn.

My brother was away at college and I remember calling him when I got home (or later that evening). I remember it was good to hear his voice. 

Every year I think about Tyler Ugolyn. He died at 23. Sports Illustrated published a piece on him. As a way to reflect and remember my brother and I read it every year.

This morning, we gathered at the Fire Museum of Memphis to mark the 25th anniversary of September 11, 2001—a day that forever changed our nation and the lives of countless families.

Memphis Fire Department Chief Colin Burress and Memphis Mayor Paul Young offered special remarks as the Shelby County Sheriff’s Office Ceremonial Guard stood alongside members of the Memphis Fire Department, Memphis Police Department    est.1827 Ceremonial Guard, Southaven Police Department, Southaven Fire Department, and Germantown Fire Department.

As Shelby County Sheriff's Office Pipes & Drums Pipe Major Kenneth Hiner performed Amazing Grace, we paused to remember that the lives lost that morning were more than a number. They were mothers and fathers, sons and daughters, friends and coworkers, first responders and ordinary citizens whose absence is still deeply felt.

We honored those who ran toward danger while others fled, those who made the ultimate sacrifice, and those who have carried the weight of that day for the past quarter-century.

Time may move forward, but our responsibility to remember remains.

We will never forget.
