𝐁𝐔𝐒𝐇 𝐀𝐍𝐒𝐖𝐄𝐑𝐒 𝐓𝐇𝐄 𝟐𝟓-𝐘𝐄𝐀𝐑 𝐂𝐋𝐀𝐒𝐒𝐑𝐎𝐎𝐌 𝐒𝐌𝐄𝐀𝐑: 𝐌𝐘 𝐉𝐎𝐁 𝐖𝐀𝐒 𝐓𝐎 𝐃𝐄𝐅𝐄𝐍𝐃 𝐓𝐇𝐄 𝐂𝐇𝐈𝐋𝐃 𝐑𝐄𝐀𝐃𝐈𝐍𝐆 𝐓𝐎 𝐌𝐄

For a quarter century, one image has been used against George W. Bush more than any other: the president sitting in a Sarasota classroom after Andy Card whispered in his ear, continuing to listen to a second-grader read. Critics built an entire genre out of it. He froze. He did nothing. He should have leapt from the chair.

On the 25th anniversary, Bush gave his answer, and it is not the one his defenders usually offer.

𝘐 𝘸𝘢𝘴 𝘪𝘯 𝘢 𝘤𝘭𝘢𝘴𝘴𝘳𝘰𝘰𝘮 𝘭𝘪𝘴𝘵𝘦𝘯𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘵𝘰 𝘢 𝘭𝘪𝘵𝘵𝘭𝘦 𝘤𝘩𝘪𝘭𝘥 𝘳𝘦𝘢𝘥, he said. 𝘈𝘯𝘥 𝘈𝘯𝘥𝘺 𝘊𝘢𝘳𝘥 𝘸𝘩𝘪𝘴𝘱𝘦𝘳𝘦𝘥 𝘪𝘯 𝘮𝘺 𝘦𝘢𝘳, 𝘴𝘦𝘤𝘰𝘯𝘥 𝘱𝘭𝘢𝘯𝘦. 𝘐 𝘬𝘯𝘦𝘸 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘧𝘪𝘳𝘴𝘵 𝘱𝘭𝘢𝘯𝘦 𝘩𝘪𝘵 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘵𝘰𝘸𝘦𝘳. 𝘐 𝘵𝘩𝘰𝘶𝘨𝘩𝘵 𝘪𝘵 𝘸𝘢𝘴 𝘢𝘯 𝘢𝘤𝘤𝘪𝘥𝘦𝘯𝘵. 𝘈𝘯𝘥 𝘈𝘮𝘦𝘳𝘪𝘤𝘢 𝘪𝘴 𝘯𝘰𝘸 𝘶𝘯𝘥𝘦𝘳 𝘢𝘵𝘵𝘢𝘤𝘬.

Then the part nobody has heard him put this way: 𝘐 𝘥𝘰𝘯'𝘵 𝘩𝘢𝘷𝘦 𝘮𝘶𝘤𝘩 𝘵𝘪𝘮𝘦 𝘵𝘰 𝘱𝘳𝘰𝘤𝘦𝘴𝘴 𝘵𝘩𝘢𝘵, 𝘣𝘶𝘵 𝘪𝘵 𝘸𝘢𝘴 𝘱𝘳𝘦𝘵𝘵𝘺 𝘤𝘭𝘦𝘢𝘳 𝘵𝘰 𝘮𝘦 𝘵𝘩𝘢𝘵 𝘪𝘧 𝘸𝘦 𝘸𝘦𝘳𝘦 𝘶𝘯𝘥𝘦𝘳 𝘢𝘵𝘵𝘢𝘤𝘬, 𝘵𝘩𝘦𝘯 𝘮𝘺 𝘫𝘰𝘣 𝘸𝘢𝘴 𝘵𝘰 𝘥𝘦𝘧𝘦𝘯𝘥 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘤𝘩𝘪𝘭𝘥 𝘵𝘩𝘢𝘵 𝘸𝘢𝘴 𝘳𝘦𝘢𝘥𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘵𝘰 𝘮𝘦, 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘩𝘦𝘳 𝘧𝘢𝘮𝘪𝘭𝘺, 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘩𝘦𝘳 𝘤𝘰𝘶𝘯𝘵𝘳𝘺.

𝘈𝘯𝘥 𝘴𝘰 𝘪𝘵 𝘸𝘢𝘴 𝘢 𝘮𝘰𝘮𝘦𝘯𝘵 𝘰𝘧 𝘤𝘭𝘢𝘳𝘪𝘵𝘺, he said. 𝘐 𝘣𝘦𝘤𝘢𝘮𝘦 𝘢 𝘸𝘢𝘳𝘵𝘪𝘮𝘦 𝘱𝘳𝘦𝘴𝘪𝘥𝘦𝘯𝘵. 𝘛𝘩𝘦𝘳𝘦 𝘸𝘢𝘴 𝘯𝘰 𝘥𝘰𝘶𝘣𝘵 𝘪𝘯 𝘮𝘺 𝘮𝘪𝘯𝘥 𝘵𝘩𝘢𝘵 𝘵𝘩𝘪𝘴 𝘸𝘢𝘴 𝘯𝘰𝘵 𝘢 𝘭𝘢𝘸 𝘦𝘯𝘧𝘰𝘳𝘤𝘦𝘮𝘦𝘯𝘵 𝘦𝘷𝘦𝘯𝘵.

That reframes the famous seven minutes entirely. The charge was always that he was paralyzed — that nothing was happening behind his face. His account is the opposite: the presidency changed in that chair, and the first decision was that a room full of seven-year-olds would not watch the President of the United States panic.

Ari Fleischer, who was in the room, notes what his critics never had to account for: 𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫𝐞 𝐰𝐚𝐬 𝐧𝐨𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐁𝐮𝐬𝐡 𝐜𝐨𝐮𝐥𝐝 𝐡𝐚𝐯𝐞 𝐝𝐨𝐧𝐞 𝐟𝐫𝐨𝐦 𝐚 𝐅𝐥𝐨𝐫𝐢𝐝𝐚 𝐜𝐥𝐚𝐬𝐬𝐫𝐨𝐨𝐦 𝐭𝐨 𝐬𝐭𝐨𝐩 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐨𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐡𝐢𝐣𝐚𝐜𝐤𝐢𝐧𝐠𝐬. The Secret Service moved him to the motorcade quickly — the Pentagon was struck while they were still driving — and when Air Force One lifted off, they believed six unidentified aircraft were still airborne and unaccounted for.

𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐲 𝐬𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝟐𝟓 𝐲𝐞𝐚𝐫𝐬 𝐬𝐚𝐲𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐡𝐞 𝐟𝐫𝐨𝐳𝐞. 𝐇𝐞 𝐬𝐚𝐲𝐬 𝐡𝐞 𝐰𝐚𝐬 𝐝𝐞𝐜𝐢𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐧𝐨𝐭 𝐭𝐨 𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐫𝐢𝐟𝐲 𝐚 𝐜𝐥𝐚𝐬𝐬𝐫𝐨𝐨𝐦 𝐨𝐟 𝐜𝐡𝐢𝐥𝐝𝐫𝐞𝐧 𝐰𝐡𝐢𝐥𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐢𝐫 𝐜𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐭𝐫𝐲 𝐰𝐚𝐬 𝐛𝐞𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐚𝐭𝐭𝐚𝐜𝐤𝐞𝐝.

text:
The last time I was in NYC before the attacks, it was almost exactly year earlier to the day. My BFF from high school, A, married a guy she met while she was at Pace University. I remember from that weekend the banquet in Chinatown with their college friends and extended families, and then buzzedly winding my way through lower Manhattan back to the hotel at the WTC for which I had gotten a cheap last minute rate on Expedia. The towers looked so big that September night.

A and her new husband came down to WTC next day to see me off as I had traveled the farthest for the wedding. I vividly remember walking through the marbled WTC mall with them (marveling at the Ben and Jerry's since at the time I was living in Vermont) and saying goodbye outside the towers. My one life regret was not taking them up on the offer to go up to the observation deck together, thinking, "It'll be here the next time I come to the city."

Growing up in North Jersey, life was unreservedly tied to NYC. My folks would watch the local news every night on the TV. My Dad and countless neighbors commuted into the city for work. In high school, friends found a cleared construction lot on a hill where we could park and watch the skyline lights at night. While I was at Rutgers, I would regularly take the train in pursuing some excitement -- a concert or a museum, hanging out with A, meeting boys. To me, the NYC skyline meant adventure.

Ticking off the ties to 9/11 seems overwhelming. A and her husband, her parents who had moved to the city, and their extended families living in Chinatown. A's cousin J, another HS friend, had started a new job after college in the South Tower in the months before, and only survived because the urge to evacuate was too great. HS and college friends who moved to the city to live and work. A friend and fraternity brother of mine from Rutgers lost her husband at the Pentagon, they were newlyweds. There were others who didn't return home to the places where I grew up and went to school.

We were just starting our lives -- and then it all changed.

text:
Bumpy Johnson was one of the most influential figures in Harlem's criminal underworld during the mid-20th century. Rising to power at a time when racial segregation limited opportunities for many African Americans, he built a reputation as both a feared gangster and a respected community figure, earning the nickname "Godfather of Harlem."

Born Ellsworth Raymond Johnson in 1905 in Charleston, South Carolina, he moved to Harlem as a child during the Great Migration. After working a series of odd jobs, he was drawn into organized crime, where his toughness and loyalty helped him rise through the ranks. His career took off when he became the trusted lieutenant of the legendary numbers queen Stephanie St. Clair, helping defend her gambling empire during its violent rivalry with gangster Dutch Schultz.

Following Schultz's downfall, Johnson emerged as Harlem's dominant crime boss. Rather than wage war against the Italian Mafia, he reached an agreement with Lucky Luciano that allowed him to maintain control over much of Harlem's illegal gambling operations. At the height of his power, few criminal enterprises in the neighborhood operated without his approval.

Johnson spent much of his life in and out of prison, including a lengthy sentence at Alcatraz Federal Penitentiary on narcotics charges. Even while incarcerated, he was believed to have retained significant influence over Harlem's underworld. Outside of crime, he developed a reputation for generosity, donating money to struggling families, hosting holiday meals, and maintaining a friendship with Malcolm X, who respected Johnson's influence but declined his offers of protection.

Bumpy Johnson died of heart failure in 1968 at the age of 62. His life has inspired numerous books, films, and television series, including the drama Godfather of Harlem. https://t.co/pAUcwaWGO7

text:
DIESEL, GASOLINE, JET FUEL AND REGIONAL DIFFERENCES

Diesel is particularly relevant because the current distillate inventory deficit is larger, in percentage terms, than the gasoline deficit. However, EIA’s latest 4-week domestic product-supplied measures were below year-earlier levels for both gasoline and distillate. The current tightness should therefore not be interpreted simply as rapidly accelerating U.S. end-user consumption. Capacity analysis must incorporate inventories, exports and international availability rather than relying exclusively on domestic demand growth. 

Diesel-oriented investment would require demonstrated increases in specification-compliant middle-distillate production. Jet fuel and diesel also compete within parts of the refinery’s middle-distillate processing and blending system. Greater flexibility can improve the ability to respond to whichever product is tightest, but switching production toward jet does not necessarily increase the combined volume of jet and diesel. A project described as increasing jet production could represent product reallocation rather than an equivalent increase in total transportation-fuel supply. 

For gasoline, specification changes can sometimes affect available supply faster than new construction. EPA had already issued 2026 fuel waivers, including measures affecting seasonal volatility requirements and a September 8 renewal concerning federal enforcement of certain state gasoline-volatility provisions. These measures operate under separate legal authorities and should be included in the existing supply baseline. Their effects should not be counted again as incremental DPA capacity. They also should not be interpreted as unrestricted permission to disregard every fuel-quality requirement. 

Geography can be as important as aggregate production. An additional Gulf Coast barrel does not automatically resolve a shortage in California or Arizona when transportation routes are constrained. Product pipelines, terminals and storage can increase effective delivered supply without adding refining capacity. Conversely, an isolated region can retain a substantial price premium despite increasing national production. The relevant comparison is delivered, specification-compliant fuel at the constrained destination—not aggregate barrels produced elsewhere. 

The proposed Western Gateway system illustrates this distinction. Phillips 66, Kinder Morgan and HF Sinclair have announced a final investment decision for a refined-products pipeline system with a design capacity of 230,000 barrels per day, including a new Borger-to-Phoenix route and reversal of an existing line into California. Completion is targeted for 2029, subject to approvals. This is a logistics addition rather than a refinery addition, and it was already announced before the September DPA discussion. Its relevance is the potential to change western delivered-supply economics, not to provide immediate new refining output. 

PROJECT ECONOMICS AND THE ADDITIONALITY TEST

Government support can make a project more attractive without proving that the project creates incremental industry capacity. The central counterfactual is what the company would have built, when it would have built it, and how it would have operated without assistance. Funding a project already fully approved and underway may transfer capital cost to the government while producing little additional supply. Advancing commissioning, increasing project scope, removing a financing barrier or preventing a credible closure would produce different degrees of additionality.

An illustrative project costing $800 million and adding 25,000 barrels per day at 90 percent utilization would process approximately 8.2 million incremental barrels annually. At an assumed $12-per-barrel contribution after variable costs but before additional fixed costs, taxes and sustaining capital, annual contribution would be approximately $99 million. A $300 million capital grant would reduce the owner’s investment to $500 million and increase that simple contribution-to-private-capital ratio from approximately 12.3 percent to 19.7 percent. Those figures are not internal rates of return and exclude construction timing, ramp-up, working capital and terminal value.

The industry margin effect can outweigh the incremental volume benefit. An illustrative operator processing 1 million barrels per day would experience approximately $365 million of annual pre-tax contribution sensitivity to a sustained $1-per-barrel change in realized margin, assuming unchanged volume and costs. The $99 million contribution from the hypothetical expansion would be offset by only about $0.27 per barrel of margin compression across that existing throughput. The precise sensitivity would vary with product mix and hedging, but the arithmetic explains why capacity support is not automatically bullish for incumbent refiners.

The valuation framework should therefore separate reduced private capital spending, incremental operating cash flow, changes in working capital and any margin effect on existing production. A grant should not automatically be capitalized as recurring EBITDA. A loan guarantee is not equivalent to cash equity. An offtake contract can reduce risk while limiting commercial flexibility, depending on its terms. The relevant investment outcome is the change in after-tax cash flow over the project’s life, not the headline amount of government support.

IMPLICATIONS FOR MPC, VLO, PSX, DINO AND DK

Marathon Petroleum has direct examples of the engineering distinctions that matter. Its second-quarter disclosures identified a 90,000-barrel-per-day Galveston Bay distillate hydrotreater targeted for year-end 2027 and a Garyville feedstock-optimization project expected to add 30,000 barrels per day of crude throughput on a similar schedule. The hydrotreater’s rating should not be interpreted as 90,000 barrels per day of entirely new diesel production. MPC also placed El Paso yield improvements and Robinson product-flexibility investments in service during the second quarter, with Robinson enabling approximately 10,000 barrels per day of incremental jet production. These projects demonstrate an existing investment pipeline, not newly identified DPA additions. 

For MPC, potential benefits would include lower project capital requirements, faster execution and improved yield or reliability. The counterweight is margin exposure across a much larger operating system. Its midstream business provides a separate source of earnings and potential volume participation, but that does not eliminate refining-margin sensitivity. The company’s DPA-related investment case would depend on specific awards and their incremental economics, rather than a general inference that the largest refiner necessarily gains most from industry expansion. 

Valero offers a similar distinction between financing capacity and investment incentives. At June 30, it reported approximately $7.9 billion of cash, while its $230 million St. Charles fluid catalytic cracking optimization project was expected to enter operation in the third quarter of 2026. That comparison indicates that the availability of cash is not necessarily the principal constraint for a well-capitalized refiner undertaking a targeted project. Long-run returns, execution risk and the durability of product margins remain relevant. St. Charles was already progressing and should not be classified as a new consequence of the September proposal. Valero could benefit from support for additional projects, but lower industry cracks would also affect its existing production. 

Phillips 66 has exposure through both refining and the infrastructure that moves products to market. Its second-quarter release reported 96 percent refining utilization and an 86 percent clean-product yield, alongside a diversified operating portfolio. Refinery support could improve selected asset economics, while logistics investment could create additional transportation earnings and access to higher-value markets. Western Gateway also illustrates the offsetting effect: better supply access can benefit pipeline owners and supplying refineries while compressing scarcity premiums in destination markets. The consolidated result depends on the balance between those exposures rather than on the direction of gasoline prices alone. 

HF Sinclair reported consolidated crude capacity of 678,000 barrels per stream day. Its geographic exposure makes local crude advantages, product differentials and transportation constraints particularly important. A targeted project could be meaningful relative to its smaller refining base, but industry expansion or improved pipeline access could also narrow regional margins that support existing earnings. Participation in Western Gateway creates an infrastructure-related offset, while the company’s lubricants, marketing and other businesses diversify the overall result. Its reported utilization should not be compared mechanically with EIA’s national weekly measure because the definitions and measurement periods differ. 

Delek’s 302,000-barrel-per-day nameplate refining base makes modest absolute additions more significant proportionately. An illustrative 10,000-barrel-per-day expansion would equal approximately 3.3 percent of that capacity. However, the company reported its full system operating following completion of the Big Spring turnaround in the first quarter, so it should not be treated as holding a large idle refinery that could simply be switched on. Targeted reliability, yield and bottleneck improvements would need to be distinguished from new crude capacity. Delek’s second-quarter results also included an RVO adjustment; changes in renewable-fuel compliance accounting are separate from sustainable physical production gains. 

Across the group, smaller refiners could experience a larger proportional benefit from an individual award, while larger operators could have more eligible projects and broader execution resources. Neither observation establishes a net equity outcome. The important variables are the subsidy retained, the genuinely incremental output, the competitive response and the sensitivity of existing earnings to lower realized margins. A refinery expansion can have a positive project-level net present value while reducing the value of the owner’s broader refining franchise through lower market margins.

SCENARIOS AND INVESTMENT MONITORING

Under an announcement-only scenario, the immediate effect would primarily concern expectations. Without funded projects, physical output assumptions would remain largely unchanged. A credible commitment to future expansion could affect deferred crack spreads, but the near-term supply balance would continue to depend on operating availability, crude access, inventories and trade flows. The distinction between a policy headline and an executed project would therefore remain important for interpreting equity and commodity-market reactions.

Under a targeted implementation scenario, support would accelerate prepared modifications, improve reliability or enable specific product-quality and logistics investments. The effect could be material at individual assets or in constrained regional markets without producing a dramatic change in national crude-processing capacity. Diesel prices would respond most directly where the supported investment demonstrably increases delivered diesel availability. A gasoline-oriented project, a jet-yield project and a crude-throughput project would require separate supply-balance treatment.

Under a broader multiyear expansion scenario, persistent growth in net effective capacity would place greater pressure on normalized crack spreads. The eventual impact would depend on the global market at commissioning. Capacity arriving after disrupted foreign facilities recover could contribute to a looser market, whereas capacity arriving amid continued outages or offsetting closures could largely replace missing supply. Gross project announcements alone would not establish the direction or magnitude of the net industry capacity change.

The critical evidence would be appropriated and obligated funding, named facilities, binding award terms, engineering scope, construction milestones and startup dates. Operating disclosures would need to identify incremental crude runs separately from incremental gasoline, diesel and jet production. Market confirmation would come through sustained output, inventory rebuilding, regional price differentials and realized margins rather than headline utilization alone. Projects already included in corporate capital plans would require a clear explanation of what government support changed.

CONCLUSION

The DPA could increase U.S. refining capability by paying for or de-risking specific investments, accelerating eligible procurement and supporting infrastructure needed to produce and deliver additional fuel. The near-term physical response would be concentrated in work already prepared or underway. Larger additions would remain subject to engineering, equipment, construction and commissioning lead times. The relevant capacity measure is sustained incremental finished-fuel production after accounting for displaced products, closures, outages and logistics constraints.

Successful additions would reduce product scarcity and exert downward pressure on wholesale fuel prices relative to the no-addition scenario. They would not guarantee lower observed pump prices if crude costs continued rising, and their effects would differ across diesel, gasoline, jet fuel and regional markets. For MPC, VLO, PSX, DINO and DK, the investment question is not simply whether government support becomes available. It is whether the capital and operating benefits retained by each company exceed the potential erosion of refining margins across its existing production base.

text:
If nothing else, RFK Jr brings a unique perspective.  He delivers a gripping speech here at the RNC.

Transcript for those who prefer to scan:
1/
RFK Jr. at the Republican Midterm Convention in Dallas. Full remarks, cleaned from the transcript:

2/
Thank you very much. I’m 72 years old, and for 70 years of my life I would have bet any amount of money that I would not be addressing a Republican convention.The irony of my presence here is inescapable.

3/
I attended my first Democratic convention in 1960, when I was six years old. I attended most of the Democratic conventions after that, and I spoke as a keynote speaker at many of them.I grew up in a Democratic Party of Franklin Roosevelt, of my uncle John Kennedy, of my father Robert Kennedy.

4/
Ours was a party of strong principles, clear policies, and an inspiring, idealistic vision for America. My uncle ran on a platform of tax cuts, strong defense, and fighting communism.Does that sound familiar?

5/
The Democrats of that era stood with labor, working people, and the American middle class. Nearly every cop and firefighter was a Democrat.Our party was a champion of the Bill of Rights — particularly unbridled free speech. It was wary of centralized government power, corporate privilege, and secret intelligence agencies.

6/
My uncle and father understood the connection between free markets and functional democracy. They stood firmly against crony capitalism on the right and socialism on the left.They were for competition, meritocracy, and excellence.

7/
My family helped build NIH and CDC into centers of gold-standard science. They promoted physical fitness and protected women’s sports. My uncle Ted Kennedy wrote Title IX so that women — real women — would have a safe and guaranteed place in college sports.

8/
They stood with Israel as a bulwark of democracy and a beacon of press and religious freedom — a haven from oppression for gays, women, and ethnic and religious minorities, amidst a regional sea of intolerance, misogyny, child marriage, slavery, and genocide.They saw Israel as America’s most critical frontline ally against the toxic ideology of Islamism.

9/
During COVID, I watched the Democratic Party turn against every one of its essential values.Democrats turned away from gold-standard research and blindly defended industry-sponsored, agenda-driven science written by corrupt and captive regulatory agencies.

10/
The party that once championed the Constitution systematically obliterated the Bill of Rights — beginning with the First Amendment — under the guise of combating “misinformation.”They censored hundreds of scientists and physicians who questioned the government’s COVID orthodoxies.

11/
Thirty-seven hours after President Biden took the oath of office, he ordered Facebook and Instagram to remove my accounts in order to prevent public debate.I’m not complaining about what happened to me. It was a bad thing for our country.

12/
They closed every church in America for a year — and kept liquor stores and big-box stores open as “essential businesses.”They gave liability shields to pharmaceutical companies. No matter how negligent, reckless, or toxic the product, you could not sue them.

13/
In a single year, my party obliterated 250 years of constitutional guarantees.The only amendment they left unscathed was the Second — and probably only because there is a Second Amendment.

14/
The party of “my body, my choice” forced citizens to wear masks and submit to medical interventions against their will.The party of “believe women” silenced tens of thousands of mothers who believed their children had suffered vaccine injuries.They declared war on women’s sports and effectively destroyed Title IX.

15/
The Democratic Party became the party of elites, labeling working Americans “deplorables.”They abandoned their traditional values and offered Americans only one policy: the unbridled, sociopathic, and blind hatred of a single man — Donald J. Trump.

16/
I mourn the fact that neither my father nor my uncle would recognize the Democratic Party of today.I t struck me: this was no longer about left and right.
It was about sane and insane.
It was about common sense and communism.

17/
In April 2023 I ran for president hoping to summon my party back to its bedrock values.Instead, they sued candidates, cancelled primaries, excluded me from debates, and — for the first time in history — cancelled their own convention. No voter ever cast a primary ballot for Kamala Harris. No elected delegate was consulted. The party of “no kings” simply anointed a queen.

18/
The day President Trump was shot in Butler, Pennsylvania, within three hours he called me and asked for a meeting.During those talks I realized that everything I had heard about him from the mainstream media was a lie. Everything.

19/
I found a man of intelligence, empathy, and near-reckless courage to challenge vested interests.We talked about lowering drug prices, supporting farmers, restoring law and order, ending corporate capture of the agencies, restoring gold-standard science — and ending the chronic disease epidemic in our children.

20/
I realized that many of the foundational values of the old Democratic Party had found a new home. It was called the Republican Party.

21/
Out of fairness, after talking with President Trump, I tried to have the same conversation with Kamala Harris.Did she even pick up the telephone?
No.On August 23, 2024, I suspended my campaign and endorsed President Trump.

22/
Later that day, on stage at the Turning Point rally in Arizona, I met President Trump.That moment would never have happened without my friend Charlie Kirk.Charlie spent nearly a year trying to bring us together.

23/
Today, on the first anniversary of his assassination, I can’t stand here without thinking about him.Charlie believed people from different political traditions could find common ground in their love of country.He helped build the bridge that President Trump and I walked across that day.

24/
That afternoon we shook hands and made a promise to the American people:Together, we would Make America Healthy Again.Some of my Democratic friends said I was a fool for trusting President Trump.I want the record clear: President Trump has kept every single promise that he made to me — without exception.

25/
Two years in:Americans are eating more real food. Real food sales were up 8% in 2025.
Obesity is down 7% after 40 years of increase.
Preliminary CDC data indicates we have reversed a 30-year decline in longevity.

26/
We are making America healthy again. It’s up to you now.We need to elect a Republican Congress to keep this momentum going.God bless you. God bless America.

text:
✈️ Hagos, Afework✈️- Afework Hagos, a computer programmer, was on his way to work but stuck in a traffic jam near the Pentagon when the plane flew over. "There was a huge screaming noise and I got out of the car as the plane came over. Everybody was running away in different directions. It was tilting its wings up and down like it was trying to balance. It hit some lampposts on the way in."
✈️ Hagos, Asework✈️- Asework Hagos, 26, of Arlington, was driving on Columbia Pike on his way to work as a consultant for Nextel. He saw a plane flying very low and close to nearby buildings. "I thought something was coming down on me. I know this plane is going to crash. I've never seen a plane like this so low." He said he looked at it and saw American Airline insignia and when it made impact with the Pentagon initially he saw smoke, then flames.
✈️ Harrington, Joe✈️- Harrington was working on the installation of new furniture in Wedge One, when he was called out to the parking lot to talk about security with his customer moments before the crash. "About two minutes later one of my guys pointed to an American Airlines airplane 20 feet high over Washington Blvd.," Harrington said. "It seemed like it made impact just before the wedge. It was like a Hollywood movie or something.
✈️ Haubold, Art✈️- At about 9:20 a.m., Lt. Col. Art Haubold, a public affairs officer with air force, was in his office on the opposite side of the complex when the plane struck. "We were sitting there watching the reports on the World Trade Center. All of a sudden, the windows blew in," he said. "We could see a fireball out our window."
✈️ Hemphill, Albert✈️- From the view of the Navy Annex : After a few moments, Lt Gen Ron Kadish, Director of the Ballistic Missile Defense Organization entered the Secure Conference Room to pursue the day's activities and do real work. This office, with two nice windows and a great view of the monuments, the Capitol and the Pentagon was "good digs" by any Pentagon standard. I walked in the office and stood peering out of the window looking at the Pentagon. As I stood there, I instinctively ducked at the extremely loud roar and whine of a jet engine spooling up. Immediately, the large silver cylinder of an aircraft appeared in my window, coming over my right shoulder as I faced the Westside of the Pentagon directly towards the heliport. The aircraft, looking to be either a 757 or Airbus, seemed to come directly over the annex, as if it had been following Columbia Pike - an Arlington road leading to Pentagon. The aircraft was moving fast, at what I could only be estimate as between 250 to 300 knots. All in all, I probably only had the aircraft in my field of view for approximately 3 seconds. The aircraft was at a sharp downward angle of attack, on a direct course for the Pentagon. It was "clean", in as much as, there were no flaps applied and no apparent landing gear deployed. He was slightly left wing down as he appeared in my line of sight, as if he'd just "jinked" to avoid something. As he crossed Route 110 he appeared to level his wings, making a slight right wing slow adjustment as he impacted low on the Westside of the building to the right of the helo, tower and fire vehicle around corridor 5. What instantly followed was a large yellow fireball accompanied by an extremely bass sounding, deep thunderous boom. The yellow fireball rose quickly as black smoke engulfed the entire Westside of the Pentagon, obscuring the whole of the heliport. I could feel the concussion and felt the shockwave of the blast impact the window of the Annex, knocking me against the desk.
✈️ Henson, Jerry✈️- Pinned in his chair and wrapped in a shroud of thick smoke and darkness, Jerry Henson had almost given up hope. He could feel all his limbs, but they wouldn't move. It was as if he were frozen at his desk by forces he couldn't battle. Through the smoke, he mustered some pleas for help. His mind still raced to figure out what happened and whether this was real. It was 9:40 a.m., Sept. 11. (...) airliner (...) slammed into the Pentagon. "The impact was quite clear," Henson said. "But it wasn't what you would think. It was just a loud kathump. Just a loud noise." Then all his senses failed him. The plane had sliced through the emergency lighting generators leaving everything in blackness. Books and computer monitors tumbled from the shelves behind him. Then his head throbbed. Pain shot through his legs. He couldn't move. All he could taste was smoke and dust. "I knew I was wounded some place because you can tell the difference between water and blood," he said. "Blood is sticky and tacky and warm. But I couldn't tell where the blood was coming from." For 15 minutes he and two of his staff who also were trapped in the office yelled for help. They yelled for Punches, Henson's deputy. They yelled for other survivors. They yelled for anyone at all.https://t.co/nicKossRwE
✈️ Henson, Jerry✈️- Inside the hell that was once his office, Jerry Henson freed his hands enough to move rubble off of his shoulders. He dislodged his head. But he couldn't move the heavy desktop from his lap. It had been 15, maybe 20 minutes since everything turned dark and painful. Still no answer from Capt. Punches. Now fires were burning closer as deposits of jet fuel ignited. "You could hear them lighting off," Henson said. "They would go 'poof,' kind of like when you light a furnace. You could hear these getting closer." The two other men in the office couldn't get to Henson, but they found a hole in the wall to crawl through. And they found help. Minutes passed slowly as Henson remained trapped in the dark and more conscious of every breath. He heard rubble crumbling and splashes like footsteps in puddles. Then he saw a slice of light. "I'm a doctor, I'm here to help you," said a voice. Navy Lt. Cmdr. David Tarantino, the doctor, and Capt. David M. Thomas Jr. had dodged slithering electrical wires and dripping solder to reach Henson. Tarantino, realizing Henson was pinned, got on his back and lifted the table top with his feet enough for Henson to slide out. Thomas and Tarantino pulled him back out through the maze. With a blur of light and a rush of fresh air, Henson knew he was safe. Jerry Henson, now 65, spent four days at nearby Arlington Hospital Center. Doctors sewed up the gash in the back of his head and on his chin. His neck was sprained, his back was sore, and he still needed treatment for smoke inhalation. "I was eager to get out," he said. "I thought the sooner I was able to get walking and breathing, the better I'd avoid pneumonia and things like that."
✈️ Holland, Nicholas✈️- Nicholas Holland, an engineer with AMEC Construction Management of Bethesda, Md., had spent the last two years working to reinforce the walls. Two summers ago, a blast wall of reinforced steel and concrete was installed right where the plane hit. It stood for 25 minutes after it was hit before collapsing, long enough for people to escape, Holland said.
✈️ Hovis, Tom✈️- Being a former transport type (60's era) I cannot understand how that plane hit where it did giving the direction the aircraft was taking at the time. As most know, the Pentagon lies at the bottom of two hills from the west with the east side being next to the river at 14th street bridge. One hill is at the Navy Annex and the other is Arlington Cemetery. The plane came up I-395 also known as Shirley Hwy. (most likely used as a reference point.) The plane had been seen making a lazy pattern in the no fly zone over the White House and US Cap. Why the plane did not hit incoming traffic coming down the river from the north to Reagan Nat'l. is beyond me . Strangely, no one at the Reagan Tower noticed the aircraft. Andrews AFB radar should have also picked up the aircraft I would think. Nevertheless, the aircarft went southwest near Springfield and then veered left over Arlington and then put the nose down coming over Ft Myer picking off trees and light poles near the helicopter pad next to building. It was as if he leveled out at the last minute and put it square into the building. The wings came off as if it went through an arch way leaving a hole in the side of the building it seems a little larger than the wide body of the aircraft. The entry point was so clean that the roof (shown in news photo) fell in on the wreckage. They are just now getting to the passengers today. The nosewheel I understand is in the grass near the second ring. Right now it is estimated that it will take two years to repair the damage. Ironcally, the area had just been remodeled with most of the area was still blocked off and some offices were empty. I know a young Army Major who went to a planned staff meeting at 8:30 am sharp. He left his office and attended the meeting, there was something he needed. He called his friend also a major near his office on his cell phone. As they were talking his friend said, My God a plane has just came through near your office "(which was not part of the new area, but near it ). Fire rolled down the hallway, somehow his friend on the phone ducked down another hallway. Four of the Major's friends did not make it. Incidently, the fireball also went along the outside of the building as shown by the blackend side of the building to left of the impact point. The reason the fire took so long to put out was because the attic was filled with "horse hair" for insulation put there in 1942 when the building was built.
✈️ Hunt, Bob✈️- office when the explosion at the Pentagon occurred. "About a third of the sky was blacked with smoke", He said. Hunt was in contact with this office via e-mail on September 11 until he left work and decided to walk, rather than catch a crowded subway. "I talked to a number of average people in route who said they saw the plane hovering over the Washington Mall Area at an altitude lower that the height of the Washington Monument" Hunt stated. He said they reported to him they could clearly see the markings of an American Airlines airliner and some even said they could make out faces of passengers in the aircraft windows. Again, this is what Bob Hunt heard from witnesses on the street in Washington D.C. on September 11, 2001.
✈️ Jarvis, Will✈️- From time spent on military aircraft as part of his job at the Pentagon, Will Jarvis (who graduated with a bachelor of applied science in 1987 while attending New College) knows what aviation fuel smells like. That smell was his only clue that a plane had crashed into the Pentagon, where he works as an operations research analyst for the Office of the Secretary of Defense. Jarvis, who was around the corner from the disaster, tried but failed to see the plane when he left the building. "There was just nothing left. It was incinerated. We couldn't see a tail or a wing or anything," he says. "Just a big black hole in the building with smoke pouring out of it." For someone sitting only 300 metres away from the carnage of American Airlines Flight 77, Jarvis and his officemates were surprisingly well insulated from it. "We thought the plane was a dump truck backing into the building, because there was a lot of construction going on," he says. The group noticed that the sky was darker than normal, but still didn't think much of it. "Then I saw little bits of silver falling from the sky," says Jarvis.
✈️ Joyce, Tom✈️- Tom Joyce, a Navy captain, was reading at his desk on the fifth floor in the building's fifth wing, when the plane hit.The impact knocked him out of his chair. "The whole building shook," Captain Joyce said. "Smoke started coming into the building."
✈️ Kean, Terrance✈️- Terrance Kean, 35, who lives in a 14-story building nearby, heard the loud jet engines and glanced out his window. "I saw this very, very large passenger jet," said the architect, who had been packing for a move. "It just plowed right into the side of the Pentagon. The nose penetrated into the portico. And then it sort of disappeared, and there was fire and smoke everywhere. . . . It was very sort of surreal."
✈️ Khavkin, D. S.✈️- from an 8th floor high-rise: "At first, we thought it was the jets that sometimes fly overhead. However, it appeared to be a small commercial aircraft..."
✈️ Kirk, Mark Steven✈️- Rep. Mark Steven Kirk (R-Ill.), a Naval Reserve intelligence officer. ''Apparently, the fire killed everybody in there,'' said Kirk, shortly after he learned that two friends perished in the center. Kirk also went to the site. ''The first thing you smell is the burning. And then you can smell the aviation fuel. And then you can smell this sickly, rotten-meat smell,'' he said.
✈️ Kizildrgli, Aydan✈️- Kizildrgli, while driving by the Pentagon, "saw the jetliner bank slightly"
✈️ Krohn, Charles H.✈️- One of the aircraft's engines somehow ricocheted out of the building and arched into the Pentagon's mall parking area between the main building and the new loading dock facility, said Charles H. Krohn, the Army's deputy chief of public affairs. Those fleeing the building heard a loud secondary explosion about 10 min. after the initial impact.
✈️ Lagasse, William✈️- Sgt. William Lagasse, a pentagon police dog handler, the son of an aviation instructor, was filling up his patrol car at a gas station near the Pentagon when he noticed a jet fly in low. He watched as the plane plowed into the Pentagon. Initially, he thought the plane was about to drop on top of him -- it was that close. Lagasse knew something was wrong. The 757's flaps were not deployed and the landing gear was retracted.
✈️ Lagasse, William✈️- I saw the aircraft above my head about 80 feet above the ground, 400 miles an hour. The reason, I have some experience as a pilot and I looked at the plane. Didn't see any landing gear. Didn't see any flaps down. I realized it wasn't going to land. . . . It was close enough that I could see the windows and the blinds had been pulled down. I read American Airlines on it. . . .I got on the radio and broadcast. I said a plane is, is heading toward the heliport side of the building.
✈️ Liebner, Lincoln✈️- "I saw this large American Airlines passenger jet coming in fast and low," said Army Captain Lincoln Liebner. "My first thought was I've never seen one that high. Before it hit I realised what was happening."
✈️ Liebner, Lincoln✈️- After the second plane hit the World Trade Center, Major Lincoln Leibner jumped in his pickup truck and raced to the Pentagon. As he ran to an entrance, he heard jet engines and turned in time to see the American Airlines plane diving toward the building. "I was close enough that I could see through the windows of the airplane, and watch as it as it hit," he said. "There was no doubt in my mind what I was watching. Not for a second. It was accelerating," he said. "It was wheels up, flaps up, engines full throttle. "
✈️ Liebner, Lincoln✈️- Maj. Leibner drove in and made it as far as the south parking lot, where he got out on foot. "I heard the plane first," he said. "I thought it was a flyover Arlington cemetery." From his vantage point, Maj. Leibner looked up and saw the plane come in. "I was about 100 yards away," he said. "You could see through the windows of the aircraft. I saw it hit." The plane came in hard and level and was flown full throttle into the building, dead center mass, Maj. Leibner said. "The plane completely entered the building," he said. "I got a little repercussion, from the sound, the blast. I've heard artillery, and that was louder than the loudest has to offer. I started running toward the site. I jumped over a fence. I was probably the first person on the scene." A tree and the backend of a crash truck at the heliport near the crash site were on fire and the ground was scorched, Maj. Leibner recounted. "The plane went into the building like a toy into a birthday cake," he said. "The aircraft went in between the second and third floors." At that point, no one was outside. Spotting a Pentagon door that had been blown off its hinges, Maj. Leibner went in and out several times, helping rescue several people. "The very first person was right there," he said. "She could walk. I walked her out onto the grass." Maj. Leibner said a police officer pulled up onto the grass and began to help. "Everybody was hurt," Maj. Leibner said. "They were all civilian females. Everybody was burned on their hands and faces.
✈️ Leibner, Lincoln✈️- Captain Lincoln Leibner says the aircraft struck a helicopter on the helipad, setting fire to a fire truck. We got one guy out of the cab," he said, adding he could hear people crying inside the wreckage. Captain Liebner, who had cuts on his hands from the debris, says he has been parking his car in the car park when the crash occurred."

text:
The sitting president of the United States treated Ground Zero like a nightclub with a velvet rope and a no-open-mic policy. On the 25th anniversary of the day that tore a hole in Lower Manhattan, Donald Trump—the only living president who grew up looking at those towers—chose the Pentagon, where the microphone was waiting like a loyal retriever. New York got Vice President JD Vance, four former presidents, and the long, unforgiving recitation of names. Trump got a courtyard, a wreath, and an audience that would let him talk. 

The Ground Zero ceremony is a funeral that learned, after years of politicians turning grief into a campaign stop, to keep the eulogists off the stage. Since 2012, no speeches. Just families, bells, silence, and the names of the dead rolling out like a tide that never quite recedes. Trump’s people scouted the site. They floated the idea that he would come. Then the organizers reminded everyone of the house rule: this is not a rally. So the president, a man who treats a silent room the way a vampire treats sunlight, pivoted south. Asked why he wasn’t going to New York, he offered the political equivalent of a shrug in a $5,000 suit: “Because I’m going to the Pentagon.” Later he branded the speech-ban reporting “corrupt news,” which is his usual way of saying the facts inconvenienced the brand. 

Picture the plaza: Clinton, Bush, Obama, Biden—men who have spent decades circling this wound—standing in the place where the skyline used to be. Bush was in the chair when the planes hit. The Clintons were New York’s political furniture. Obama and Biden had done the pilgrimage on earlier round-number years, when the ritual still felt like a national handshake instead of a family argument. Trump, the Queens kid who built his myth on Manhattan steel and glass, was two hundred miles away, speaking where speaking is allowed. On other milestone anniversaries, presidents have hopscotched all three attack sites in a single day, as if proximity itself were a form of penance. This time the current occupant decided one microphone was enough. 

The Pentagon is not a consolation prize. One hundred eighty-four people died there. Their names deserve air. A wreath is not nothing. But let’s not pretend the choice was a coin flip between two equally sacred rooms. Ground Zero is the blast crater in the American mind. It is where the largest number of people were turned into dust and absence. Skipping it while every other living president showed up is like hosting a wedding and sending a cousin to stand at the altar because the priest wouldn’t let you give a toast.The self-insert that wouldn’t sit stillTrump has spent a quarter-century wallpapering himself onto that morning. He watched from Trump Tower. He gave interviews while the towers were still bleeding smoke. By September 13 he was downtown in a suit, telling cameras about construction workers he said he’d sent into the wreckage. Fair enough; the record puts him near the site two days later. What the record does not put him in is the version he keeps polishing like a family heirloom: that he was there “the following day,” that a neighboring building groaned like a dying animal, that two firefighters scooped him up and carried him out. First responders who actually worked the pile have not rushed forward to confirm the presidential extraction. The earliest pictures are not of a man being hauled from danger. They are of a developer giving television. He has also kept alive the old fable about “thousands and thousands” of New Jersey Muslims cheering the collapse—a story that has been fact-checked into mulch and still gets wheeled out when the anniversary lights come on. 

A man who cannot resist starring in the flashback decided he could not attend the scene of the crime unless he got a speaking part. That is not solemnity. That is casting.Grief as a stage with better lightingAt the Pentagon he did what he came to do. He talked about never forgetting. He talked about first responders. He also steered the anniversary toward the war with Iran, a conflict that has about as much to do with Mohamed Atta’s cockpit as a midterm convention has to do with a mass grave. The day that was supposed to be about 2001 became, for a few sentences, about 2026 policy. Grief, in this telling, is a hallway that always leads back to the current argument. 

Logistics played a part, too: Ireland the next day, fewer traffic headaches if Air Force One leaves from Andrews instead of fighting New York’s airspace. Fine. Presidents have calendars. They also have choices. The calendar did not require him to treat the silent ceremony like a venue that failed to book him.Absence is not treason. Attendance is not sainthood. Families do not need a president to make the names real. The reading would have happened if the White House had sent a cardboard cutout. But symbols are stubborn. A New York president who has spent years claiming he was in the story, then declining to stand in the place where the story actually happened—because no one would hand him the mic—looks less like a steward of memory and more like a guest who only shows up if he can emcee.The former presidents stood where the towers were. The current one stood where he could speak. 

One of those choices looks like remembrance. The other looks like a man who will honor the dead, provided the dead don’t mind sharing the stage.

text:
On September 5, President Anura Kumara Dissanayake addressing the nation and told Sri Lankans to stop going to hospitals so often. His exact advice to a country grappling with a severe medicine shortage, a dengue crisis, and cancer patients unable to access chemotherapy drugs was this: "If it is something that can be managed by drinking some koththamalli and taking some rest, then go home and rest." This is the president of a country where hospitals are running out of life-saving medicines telling his people to drink coriander water instead of seeking medical treatment.

Sri Lanka has a population of roughly 22 million people. The president cited 80 million annual outpatient visits across state hospitals as evidence of a system being misused. What he conveniently failed to acknowledge, however, is why those 80 million visits happen.

They happen because Sri Lanka’s free public healthcare system is the only option for millions of poor and working-class families who cannot afford private care. They happen because people are genuinely sick. Dengue cases have exceeded 100,000. Shortages of cancer medications are so severe that Filgrastim injections, needed by chemotherapy patients to prevent life-threatening infections, are unavailable in government hospitals. Meanwhile, experts warn that the country is on the brink of a crippling supply crisis that threatens to paralyze both public and private healthcare sectors.

Instead of addressing any of this (fixing drug procurement, investing in hospital infrastructure, or ensuring cancer patients can access treatment without begging), the president's solution is to tell people to stay home, drink koththamalli, and stop bothering hospitals.

He went further, announcing that under a new system, Sri Lankans will no longer be able to choose which hospital or specialist to visit. Instead, they will first have to consult a "family doctor" at one of 1,000 planned "Arogya" centers, who will decide whether they warrant a referral to a secondary or tertiary facility. He even scolded patients for not finishing their medication, calling it "a waste" and "a crime." Yet citizens struggling to secure essential drugs in empty pharmacies are hardly the ones committing crimes.

The same government that cannot ensure a steady supply of cancer therapies, control a dengue outbreak, or keep basic supplies on shelves now wants to introduce a gatekeeping model that adds another bureaucratic hurdle between sick people and critical care. The 1,000 Arogya centers do not exist yet. The family doctors have not been hired. The infrastructure has not been built. Yet the message is already loud and clear: stop coming to hospitals.

This is what happens when a political party that spent decades criticizing the healthcare system from the outside suddenly has to govern. The JVP has no plan for healthcare delivery. It has no plan for drug procurement. It has no strategy to address the structural drivers behind 80 million outpatient visits in a nation of 22 million. It offers only the audacity to blame the sick.

When cancer patients cannot get Filgrastim, that is not patient abuse of resources; that is government failure. When dengue surges and wards overflow, that is not unnecessary demand; that is survival. When a mother takes her sick child to a state facility because she has no alternative, she is doing what any parent must do in a system that has abandoned her. Telling Sri Lankans to drink koththamalli instead of seeking hospital care is not healthcare reform. It is an insult to every patient, doctor, nurse, and family depending on a public health system this administration has neither the competence nor the political will to fix.

The room falls quiet. Nobody pushes back.

Then he puts the person on the "yes train." Every small yes builds on the last one. Until saying no at the end is harder than saying yes.

By the time the paperwork comes out, they've already agreed five times without noticing.

Only 21 minutes. In them you pick up the two moves people now pay $1 million a day for: how to read anyone's state… and how to change it.

Most people spend years guessing their way through sales. He mapped it out on a flipchart in his living room in under half an hour.

The tape is free right now. And the answer is in this video.

text:
I bless thee Paulin the Name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit! Amen!
Heavenly Father, I lift this beloved man into Your loving hands, asking that Your healing touch restore his body completely. Remove all heart problems, strokes, leukemia, cancer, disease, infirmary, injury, sickness, fatigue, or pain, and renew his strength, energy, and vitality. Grant wisdom and skill to the medical team, patience to this beloved one, and peace to his heart. Surround him with Your divine protection, and let Your presence comfort and reassure him. May Your grace and mercy flow through every part of Paul’s being. In Jesus’ name I beg and pray, Amen.

Prayer to the Holy Spirit:
Come, Holy Spirit, Divine Comforter and Breath of Life. Enter all places of strokes, pain, injury, disease, infection, suffering, weakness and fear. Remove every and all infirmary, and surround Paul with Your gentle light, while completely healing Paulwhile filling his heart with the strength and peace that comes from above, trusting to the power of God’s eternal love. Amen.

Pray to the Blessed Holy Mother Mary:

Dear Mother Mary, With hearts heavy and bodies burdened, we approach your divine presence, seeking your miraculous touch. Your healing power knows no equal, and in our times of need, we implore you to mend not only our physical wounds but the scars that mar our souls. Pour forth your divine grace upon us, dear Mother, and restore us to a state of wholeness, that we may bear witness to the miracle of your love. Amen.

Prayer to St. Jude:

Oh glorious apostle St. Jude, faithful servant and friend of Jesus, the name of the traitor who delivered thy beloved Master into the hands of His enemies has caused thee to be forgotten by many, but the Church honors and invokes thee universally as the patron of hopeless cases--of things despaired of. Pray for me who am so miserable; make use, I implore thee, of that particular privilege accorded thee of bringing visible and speedy help where help is almost despaired of. Come to my assistance in this great need, that I may receive the consolations and succor of heaven in all my necessities, tribulations and sufferings, particularly—completely heal Paul from all strokes and disease, and protect Paul—and that I may bless God with thee and all the elect throughout eternity. I promise thee, O blessed St. Jude, to be ever mindful of this great favor, and I will never cease to honor thee as my special and powerful patron, and to do all in my power to encourage devotion to thee. Amen

Prayer to St. Michael (Long Version)

O Glorious Prince of the heavenly host, Saint Michael the Archangel, defend us in the battle and fearful warfare that we are waging against the principalities and powers, against the rulers of this world of darkness, against the evil spirits. Come thou to the assistance of men, whom Almighty God created immortal, making them in His own image and likeness and redeeming them at a great price from the tyranny of Satan. Fight this day the battle of the Lord with thy legions of holy Angels, even as of old thou didst fight against Lucifer, the leader of the proud spirits and all his rebel angels, who were powerless to stand against thee, neither was their place found any more in heaven. And that great dragon was cast forth, the ancient serpent, who is called the devil and satan, who seduces the whole world; and he was cast forth upon Earth, and his angels were sent with him.

But behold! the ancient enemy of mankind and a murderer from the beginning has been fiercely aroused. Changing himself into an angel of light, he goes about with the whole multitude of the wicked spirits to invade the earth and blot out the Name of God and of His Christ, to plunder, to slay, and to consign to eternal damnation the souls that have been destined for a crown of everlasting life. This wicked serpent, like an unclean torrent, pours into men of depraved minds and corrupt hearts the poison of his malice, the spirit of lying, impiety and blasphemy, and the deadly breath of impurity and every form of vice and iniquity.

Be favorable to Thy Church, the Bride of the Lamb without spot, whose enemies have filled to overflowing with gall and inebriated with wormwood. They have laid profane hands upon Her most sacred treasures. Where the See of the most blessed Peter and the Chair of Truth has been constituted as a light to the nations, there they have placed a throne of their abomination and impiety; so that with the Pastor struck, they may prevail to disperse the flock.

Therefore, most invincible Leader, be with the people of God against this spiritual wickedness and bring about victory. Thou art venerated by Holy Church as Her guard and patron; Thou art glorified as our defender against the impious powers of earth and of hell. Unto thee the Lord hath handed over the souls of the redeemed to be placed in happiness above.

Entreat the God of peace, to obliterate satan beneath our feet, lest he prevail further to hold men captive, and to injure the Church. Offer our prayers in the sight of the Most High, so that the mercy of the Lord may swiftly overtake us, and apprehend the dragon, the ancient serpent, who is the devil and satan, and send him bound into the abyss, so that he may seduce the nations no more.

Henceforth having been confided to thy escort and protection, we sacred ministers by the authority of the Holy Mother Church [if recited by a cleric of the order of exorcist or above, say instead: by our authority], do undertake to repel the infestations of diabolical deceit in the Name of Jesus Christ, Our God and Lord.

Behold the Cross of the Lord; be scattered hostile powers.
The Lion of the tribe of Juda has conquered, the root of David.
Let Thy mercies be upon us, O Lord.
As we have hoped in Thee.

✈️ Patterson, Steve✈️- Steve Patterson, who lives in Pentagon City, said it appeared to him that a commuter jet swooped over Arlington National Cemetery and headed for the Pentagon "at a frightening rate ... just slicing into that building." Steve Patterson, 43, said he was watching television reports of the World Trade Center being hit when he saw a silver commuter jet fly past the window of his 14th-floor apartment in Pentagon City. The plane was about 150 yards away, approaching from the west about 20 feet off the ground, Patterson said. He said the plane, which sounded like the high-pitched squeal of a fighter jet, flew over Arlington cemetary so low that he thought it was going to land on I-395. He said it was flying so fast that he couldn't read any writing on the side. The plane, whichappeared to hold about eight to 12 people, headed straight for the Pentagon but was flying as if coming in for a landing on a nonexistent runway, Patterson said. "At first I thought 'Oh my God, there's a plane truly misrouted from National,'" Patterson said. "Then this thing just became part of the Pentagon ... I was watching the World Trade Center go and then this. It was like Oh my God, what's next?" He said the plane, which approached the Pentagon below treetop level, seemed to be flying normally for a plane coming in for a landing other than going very fast for being so low. Then, he said, he saw the Pentagon "envelope" the plane and bright orange flames shoot out the back of the building. "It looked like a normal landing, as if someone knew exactly what they were doing," said Patterson, a graphics artist who works at home. "This looked intentional.".
✈️ Perkal, Don✈️- The airliner crashed between two and three hundred feet from my office in the Pentagon, just around a corner from where I work. I'm the deputy General Counsel, Washington Headquarters Services, Office of the Secretary of Defense. (...) My colleagues felt the impact, which reminded them of an earthquake. People shouted in the corridor outside that a bomb had gone off upstairs on the main concourse in the building. No alarms sounded. I walked to my office, shut down my computer, and headed out. Even before stepping outside I could smell the cordite. ThenI knew explosives had been set off somewhere. I looked to my right and saw a raging fire and smoke careening off the facade to the sky. (...) Two explosions, a few minutes apart, prompted me to start walking.
✈️ Peterson, Christine✈️- October 18, 2001 - Christine Peterson, '73 found herself in the thick of last month's terrorist tragedy, and submitted this report. It offers a personal perspective on the events in Washington, D.C., which have perhaps been overshadowed in the media by the scope of the horrors in New York. It was 9:30 a.m. on Tuesday, September 11th, and traffic was terrible. For all of my twenty-eight years living in the Washington, D.C. area, terrible traffic was a constant. I'd been in Boston the day before and gotten home late. That morning I repacked my suitcase because I was heading out to San Francisco on the 3:20 p.m. flight. I just needed a few hours in the office first, and now I was officially late for work. I was at a complete stop on the road in front of the helipad at the Pentagon; what I had thought would be a shortcut was as slow as the other routes I had taken that morning. I looked idly out my window to the left -- and saw a plane flying so low I said, "holy cow, that plane is going to hit my car" (not my actual words). The car shook as the plane flew over. It was so close that I could read the numbers under the wing. And then the plane crashed. My mind could not comprehend what had happened. Where did the plane go? For some reason I expected it to bounce off the Pentagon wall in pieces. But there was no plane visible, only huge billows of smoke and torrents of fire. (...) A few minutes later a second, much smaller explosion got the attention of the police arriving on the scene.
✈️ Pfeilstucker, Daniel C. Jr✈️- Daniel C. Pfeilstucker Jr., caught in the flying debris, didn't know if he was going to make it out alive. The Pentagon was on fire. "It was horrifying," Mr. Pfeilstucker says (...) Danny Pfeilstucker is a commissioning agent for John J. Kirlin Inc., a Maryland-based mechanical contracting company that worked on the Pentagon renovation project that was nearing completion September 11. (...) Kirlin Inc., among many companies involved in renovating the Pentagon since the early 1990s, was in charge of updating plumbing and heating units. Around 9:30 a.m., Mr. Pfeilstucker and a co-worker got orders to check a hot-water leak in a third-floor office on the western side. After doing so, he stepped off an elevator on the second floor in Corridor 4, ladder in hand. Suddenly the walls and the ceiling began to collapse around him. The lights went out. "It went from light to dark to orange to complete black," Mr. Pfeilstucker says. "It was so dark I couldn't even see my hand in front of my face."Within seconds, his left leg buckled. Unable to grab on to anything, he was thrust 70 feet down the corridor and into a tiny telephone closet halfway down the hallway connecting E Ring and A Ring. All I know is that the blast must have pushed open the steel door to the closet," says Mr. Pfeilstucker, who had been 40 feet away from the plane's point of impact.He remembers shutting the door and trying to stand up, not understanding what had just happened. "I thought it was some sort of a construction blast," Mr. Pfeilstucker says. "Or maybe there was a helicopter accident." His hard hat and work goggles were blown away. His ladder also had disappeared. (...) The fire sprinklers came on as the temperature shot up.Then he smelled jet fuel and smoke. The putrid odor was seeping into the closet."It was this odor that I can't describe, but one that I'll never forget, that's for sure," Mr. Pfeilstucker says. "It was so hard to breathe. I didn't think I was going to make it out."
✈️ Plaisted✈️- Plaisted, an artist, was sitting at her desk at home less than one mile from the Pentagon ... I jumped up from my chair as the screeching and whining of the engine got even louder and I looked out the window to the West just in time to see the belly of that aircraft and the tail section fly directly over my house at treetop height. It was utterly sickening to see, knowing that this plane was going to crash. The sound was so incredibly piercing and shrill- the engines were straining to keep the plane aloft. It is a sound I will never stop hearing- and I now imagine the screams of the innocent passengers were commingled with the sounds of the engines and I am haunted. I was unaware at this time that the World Trade center had been attacked so I thought this was just" a troubled plane en route to the airport. I started to run toward my front door but the plane was going so fast at this point that it only took 4 or 5 seconds before I heard a tremendously loud crash and books on my shelves started tumbling to the floor.
✈️ Probst, Frank✈️- Frank Probst : a Pentagon renovation worker and retired Army officer, he was inspecting newly installed telecommunications wiring inside the five-story, 6.5-million-square-foot building. The tall, soft-spoken Probst had a 10 a.m. meeting. About 9:25 a.m., he stopped by the renovation workers' trailer just south of the Pentagon heliport. Someone had a television turned on in the trailer's break room that showed smoke pouring out of the twin towers in New York. "The Pentagon would make a pretty good target," someone in the break room commented. The thought stuck with Probst as he picked up his notebook and walked to the North Parking Lot to attend his meeting. Probst took a sidewalk alongside Route 27, which runs near the Pentagon's western face. Traffic was at a standstill because of a road accident. Then, at about 9:35 a.m., he saw the airliner in the cloudless September sky. American Airlines Flight 77 approached from the west, coming in low over the nearby five-story Navy Annex on a hill overlooking the Pentagon. He has lights off, wheels up, nose down," Probst recalled. The plane seemed to be accelerating directly toward him. He froze. "I knew I was dead," he said later. "The only thing I thought was, 'Damn, my wife has to go to another funeral, and I'm not going to see my two boys again.'" He dove to his right. He recalls the engine passing on one side of him, about six feet away. The plane's right wing went through a generator trailer "like butter," Probst said. The starboard engine hit a low cement wall and blew apart. He still can't remember the sound of the explosion. Sometimes the memory starts to come back when he hears a particularly low-flying airliner heading into nearby Reagan National Airport, or when military jets fly over a burial at Arlington National Cemetery. Most of the time, though, his memory is silent. "It was pretty horrible," he said of the noiseless images he carries inside him, ofthe jet vanishing in a cloud of smoke and dust, and bits of metal and concrete drifting down like confetti. On either side of him, three streetlights had been sheared in half by the airliner's wings at 12 to 15 feet above the ground. An engine had clipped the antenna off a Jeep Grand Cherokee stalled in traffic not far away.
✈️ Probst, Frank✈️- "I was standing on the sidewalk (parallel to the site of impact)...and I saw this plane coming right at me at what seemed like 300 miles an hour. I dove towards the ground and watched this great big engine from this beautiful airplane just vaporize," said Frank Probst, a member of the Pentagon renovations crew commented. "It looked like a huge fireball, pieces were flying out everywhere."

He and his co-workers were watching television reports of the disaster in New York when "we gazed out our own windows and, to our horror and disbelief, saw huge billows of black smoke rising from the northeast, in the direction of D.C. and the river . . . and the Pentagon." Ragland described billowing black smoke and "what looked like white confetti raining down everywhere." He said it soon became apparent "that the 'confetti' was little bits of airplane, falling down after being flung high into the bright, blue sky."

But that morning, like many others, the traffic slowed to a crawl just in front of the Pentagon. With the Pentagon to the left of my van at about 10 o'clock on the dial of a clock, I glanced at my watch to see if I was going to be late for my appointment. At that moment I heard a very loud, quick whooshing sound that began behind me and stopped suddenly in front of me and to my left. In fractions of a second I heard the impact and an explosion. The next thing I saw was the fireball. I was convinced it was a missile. It came in so fast it sounded nothing like an airplane. Friends and colleagues have asked me if I felt a shock wave and I honestly do not know. I felt something, but I don't know if it was a shock wave or the fact that I jumped so hard I strained against the seat belt and shoulder harness and was thrown back into my seat. text:
September 11, 1697. A thirty three year old general caught an entire Ottoman army halfway across a river and destroyed it in about three hours.

Four days ago I posted the Battle of Turin and Prince Eugene of Savoy's march across northern Italy. This is Eugene nine years earlier, and it is the day that made him.

He had been appointed commander in chief in Hungary on 5 July 1697 and inherited an army with an empty war chest. He borrowed money personally to pay his own troops and fund his field hospitals.

Sultan Mustafa II had left Edirne in April with around 100,000 men to retake Hungary. He reached Belgrade in August and turned north.

Then a Serbian militia commander named Jovan Popović Tekelija brought Eugene the single piece of information that decided the campaign. The Ottoman army was crossing the Tisza at Zenta, on a pontoon bridge.

An army crossing a river is two armies, and neither half can help the other.

Eugene marched ten hours to get there and arrived with roughly two hours of daylight left. Every instinct in the manual says do not do this. You do not throw an exhausted army straight off a forced march, at dusk, at a numerically superior enemy.

He attacked immediately.

Cavalry went in on both flanks with the infantry in the centre, folding the Ottoman bridgehead into a crescent and pinning it against the water. The sultan and his cavalry were already across on the far bank and could do nothing but watch it happen.

The troops still on the near side broke for the bridge. Too many men, too fast, and it collapsed under them.

What followed was not a battle. Between 7,000 and 30,000 Ottoman soldiers were killed, wounded or drowned, depending which estimate you take.

Habsburg losses were 429 killed and 1,598 wounded.

The Grand Vizier did not die fighting the Austrians. He was murdered on the field by his own mutinying Janissaries.

And in the collapse the sultan abandoned his baggage, which included a treasury of three million piastres and the Seal of the Empire.

That last one had never happened before in Ottoman history. The imperial seal is the physical instrument of sovereignty, and it had never been taken. It is in the Museum of Military History in Vienna today.

Two years later the Ottomans signed the Treaty of Karlowitz and surrendered Hungary, Transylvania, Croatia and Slavonia.

That is the hinge of the whole era. From 1453 to 1683 the question in central Europe was how far the Ottomans would advance. After Karlowitz the only question was how much they would lose and how quickly. It never turned back the other way.

Eugene went on to Blenheim, Turin, Oudenarde and Malplaquet, and Napoleon later named him one of the seven greatest commanders in history.

He was thirty three and personally in debt when he made this call.

text: I was on Fort Devens on September 11, 2001. I was the Executive Officer of the 2nd Bde, 78th division, and the representative of the region 2 FEMA team. We were combining the regions into one, and we were just starting our meeting when the towers were attacked. We all left immediately to join our teams for the anticipated support mission. Later that afternoon, as my Commander, Col Kevin Conners and SGM Richardson moved with a small team into Manhattan and assumed duties as the DCO, or Defense Coordinating Officer. As his Deputy, I went first to the rear staging area at Fort Dix, NJ, and later to the HQ 78th division at Camp Kilmer NJ. At about 1 am on the morning of the 12th, I went to the Morristown airport with 2 vans to pick up the First Army Commander, his CSM, and the First Army team. After briefing them, we moved to Fort Dix and coordinated the staging and preparation for our move into Manhattan. I always remember from our training that that one of the first calls for support, besides helicopters, would be for “body bags”. I was surprised by the first request, which was for “pouches”. I asked for clarification, and I was told that they weren’t recovering many bodies, just parts. I knew then that the effort wasn’t going to be so much of a rescue anymore, but a recovery.  After the second day, I moved the remaining team members into the city, and we took up quarters and began working at the FEMA operations center on pier 92. Our job included the command and control of all US military resources in the city or in support. Remarkably, the use of Federal troops was very limited, with only specialized units, individuals, and items of equipment being allowed into the area.  Despite numerous requests and offers from various commands, relatively few military assets were inserted. This included nurses to support the burn victims in hospitals, demolition experts to assist in penatrating the rubble for rescue workers, and aviation for transport. Whenever possible, civilian assets were used to provide services and support.  For the next three weeks, I worked with FEMA on recovery efforts.

Love in the Gospels is not “all paths are the same.” Love is telling the truth and still treating the person in front of you as a soul, not a suspect.
If He were standing among us today, I picture less of a speech and more of that look he gave people: I see you. You are not those men. Come. Follow me.
That’s the part that fits both his kindness and his backbone. He never needed a mob, and he never needed to pretend differences don’t exist.

He loved the ones his own crowd wanted kept outside the fence. Samaritans. Romans. Tax collectors. The woman at the well. The thief next to him. He loved people who were wrong about him, people who would kill him, and people who had never heard his name yet.
That love was not soft in the modern sense. He did not pat everyone on the head and say every story about God is the same. He loved them enough to tell them the truth and then walk toward the cross for them anyway.
