text:
Antioxidant supplements promise to fight cancer. A new Science study found tumors weaponize antioxidants to disable your immune system.

Researchers at University of Cambridge and Oregon Health & Science University discovered cancer cells flood their surroundings with antioxidant proteins that shut down immune cells trying to attack them. The finding explains why antioxidant therapies have failed in cancer trials and may point toward better immunotherapy treatments.

Your immune system deploys specialized cells called T cells to hunt down and destroy cancer. But T cells need small amounts of reactive oxygen species, molecules often called free radicals, to activate their killing ability.

This creates a vulnerability. Cancer cells exploit this dependency by releasing massive amounts of an antioxidant protein called peroxiredoxin 1, or PRDX1. This protein mops up the reactive molecules T cells need, effectively smothering the immune attack before it starts.

Think of it as chemical warfare. T cells arrive ready to fight, but the tumor has already stripped the environment of the fuel they need to function.

Key findings from the study:

• Tumor fluid contains 10-20x more antioxidant activity than normal blood

• PRDX1 was the most abundant antioxidant protein in tumor environments across multiple cancer types

• Adding PRDX1 to immune cells in the lab blocked their ability to produce inflammatory signals needed to kill cancer

• The protein works by keeping certain braking molecules active inside T cells, preventing the activation signals from amplifying

• When researchers deleted the gene for PRDX1 from cancer cells, tumors that normally resist immunotherapy suddenly became responsive to treatment

The mechanism reveals why T cells fail inside tumors despite being capable of destroying cancer cells elsewhere. The tumor creates an antioxidant-rich bubble that chemically disables immune surveillance.

Researchers tested this across multiple cancer types in mice. Melanoma tumors without PRDX1 were spontaneously rejected by the immune system. Liver and other cancers that normally ignore immunotherapy drugs responded when PRDX1 was removed.

The team confirmed the same mechanism exists in humans. They analyzed fluid from patient tumors and found PRDX1 concentrations far exceeding blood levels. Human T cells showed the same vulnerability to PRDX1 as mouse cells in lab tests.

Cancer cells appear to increase PRDX1 production as they evolve under immune pressure. The researchers compared tumors that developed in mice with functioning immune systems versus mice lacking immune cells. Tumors facing immune attack showed higher PRDX1 levels, suggesting cancer learns to weaponize this protein over time.

This challenges decades of thinking about free radicals and cancer. The molecules we've been told cause DNA damage and aging are the same molecules your immune cells need to function. Antioxidant supplements marketed for cancer prevention may inadvertently protect tumors from immune attack.

Previous clinical trials tested antioxidant vitamins for cancer prevention. Multiple large studies found they either provided no benefit or worsened outcomes. This study offers a mechanistic explanation: antioxidants can suppress the immune system's ability to eliminate emerging cancer cells.

The findings open potential therapeutic directions. Rather than giving patients antioxidants, blocking PRDX1 or related proteins in the tumor environment might restore immune function. Several approaches could work: inhibiting PRDX1 directly, blocking the recycling system that keeps it active, or using compounds that increase reactive molecules specifically in tumors.

High-dose vitamin C has shown promise when combined with immunotherapy in some preclinical studies. At high concentrations it acts as a pro-oxidant rather than antioxidant, potentially countering the effect of tumor-derived PRDX1.

The study reveals a broader pattern in cancer biology. Tumors don't just hide from the immune system. They actively reshape their environment to disable immune cells, using the same metabolic adaptations that fuel their growth to create chemical barriers against attack.

This matters for understanding why immunotherapy works in some patients but not others. Tumors with high PRDX1 release may create environments where even potent immunotherapy drugs can't overcome the chemical suppression of T cells.

For now, the research is preclinical. Whether blocking PRDX1 will improve outcomes in cancer patients requires human trials. But the mechanism is clear across multiple experimental systems: tumor-derived antioxidants suppress immunity by depriving T cells of molecules they need to activate.

The decisions cancer cells make about antioxidant production determine whether immune cells can function in the tumor environment. Understanding this redox control of immunity reveals why the tissue context matters as much as the presence of immune cells themselves.

Father Mychal Judge was a Franciscan friar and the chaplain for the New York City Fire Department (FDNY)who became the first officially recorded victim of the September 11 terrorist attacks. 

Born Robert Emmett Judge on May 11, 1933, in Brooklyn, New York, to Irish immigrant parents.
He entered the seminary at just 15 years old to pursue his calling.

Father Judge rushed to the World Trade Center immediately after the first plane hit the towers & offered prayers and last rites to the injured and the dying in the streets and inside the North Tower lobby.

He perished in the lobby of the North Tower when the South Tower collapsed, he was struck by debris.

He carried a personal prayer in his pocket that read: "Lord, take me where You want me to go; Let me meet who You want me to meet. Tell me what You want me to say. And keep me out of Your way." 

This picture was shortly after his death being carried away by first responders he was ministering to on 9/11. Grok turned the picture into a painting.

text:
9 Mistakes That Instantly Destroy Your Status in Public

The world does not punish weakness only when you lose. It punishes weakness when you display it without realizing. A nervous laugh, a desperate explanation, or a glance around the room to see who approves signals vulnerability that people remember. Status collapses through small acts of self-betrayal performed in front of witnesses.

Napoleon understood that power must be visible before it can be believed. Inside Notre-Dame Cathedral, tradition dictated that the Pope place the crown upon the ruler. Napoleon interrupted the symbolism, took the crown, and placed it upon his own head, declaring that legitimacy came through him. Crowds understand posture faster than arguments. Every public action teaches others how to interpret you.

First, never laugh when someone humiliates you to prove you are unbothered. When someone exposes your private flaws disguised as humor, laughing along removes the social cost of disrespecting you. Sociologist Erving Goffman termed these negotiations face-work. When dignity and comfort collide, sacrificing yourself sets a dangerous precedent. Let the laughter die, look directly at the person, state calmly that it was unnecessary, and stop. A boundary set with quiet clarity commands respect.

Second, never rush to defend yourself against a cheap accusation. Scrambling for evidence volunteers you as the accused in a courtroom they created. Nalini Ambady's research on thin slices proved how quickly observers judge brief behavioral cues. Desperation contaminates facts. A composed person states the truth, corrects the exaggeration, and falls silent. The person controlling the frame never needs the longest explanation.

Third, never search the room for approval after speaking. Checking the faces of influential people surrenders your authority. Solomon Asch demonstrated how easily group pressure bends individual judgment. Looking for reassurance asks the room for permission to exist. Speak your mind, remain still, and let others manage their discomfort. Observation is wise, but facial dependence is fatal.

Fourth, never chase someone who withdraws from you in front of others. At the Battle of Cannae, Hannibal withdrew his center to bait the Romans into an aggressive pursuit that destroyed them. Robert Cialdini noted that perceived scarcity artificially amplifies value. When you chase someone who walks away, you turn their withdrawal into a leash. Let them walk. Never perform panic for an audience.

Fifth, never reveal how desperately you need an outcome to the person who controls it. Explaining financial strain or anxiety to an employer or client alters the price of the negotiation. Need is human, but advertising desperation destroys your leverage. Disciplined individuals cultivate alternatives so they retain the power to walk away. The person who cannot leave is not negotiating.

Sixth, never turn an ordinary social space into a confession room. Sharing unearned vulnerability is unsecured intelligence. Altman and Taylor's social penetration theory showed that genuine intimacy requires reciprocal trust built over time. In 1870, Otto von Bismarck edited a diplomatic telegram to ignite war, proving that public words are easily weaponized. Spectators remember your private weaknesses. Privacy is the wisdom to decide who has earned access to your complete self.

Seventh, never destroy an absent person to entertain the room. Research on spontaneous trait transference reveals that listeners subconsciously attribute the negative traits you describe back to you. Tearing someone down offers momentary attention at the expense of permanent trust. Restraint in the face of cheap gossip demonstrates that your integrity cannot be bought.

Eighth, never surrender emotional control of your body. Provocative people deliberately attack your nervous system to trigger an amygdala hijack, Daniel Goleman's term for panic overwhelming reason. Alexander the Great murdered his loyal commander Cleitus during a drunken rage, an impulsive minute that cost him a lifetime of regret. When provoked, lower your voice, slow down, or remove yourself. The person commanding your emotions commands your reputation.

Ninth, never make yourself smaller to protect insecure people. Erasing your accomplishments and pretending your hard work was luck is cowardice in polite clothing. Downplaying progress protects only relationships that depend on your stagnation. Receive recognition with simple dignity: thank you, I worked hard for this.

Status is coherence under observation. Niccolo Machiavelli observed that everyone sees what you appear to be, but few experience what you truly are. You cannot control every judgment, but you can control what pressure reveals. Let it reveal composure, strict boundaries, and a strength that requires no permission.

## 🚨 Overview of the Iranian Threats
Iranian state media recently broadcasted a targeted video threat against President Donald Trump's 20-year-old son, Barron Trump, which coincided with the public disclosure of an Iranian plot to assassinate Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's eldest son, Yair, in Florida. These highly specific operations against the children of both leaders mark an escalation in rhetoric and plotting amid the ongoing military and economic war between the U.S., Israel, and Iran.
The U.S. Secret Service confirmed it is investigating the broadcast targeting Barron Trump. Separately, the Israeli government has strictly enforced state security protections for Netanyahu's adult children.
------------------------------
## 📌 The Threat Against Barron Trump
The threat manifested as a nearly three-minute video produced and aired by the Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting (IRIB).

* The Video Profile: Titled "Where to kill Barron Trump?", the segment uses stylized graphics to track the 20-year-old's daily routines, zeroing in on locations like Trump Tower and his New York University (NYU) campus ([1:13](https://t.co/vqZYYkAbje)).
* Bounty Offer: The narrator asserts that "many would be willing" to target Barron, highlighting a $10 million reward linked to the efforts.
* Digital Tracking: The video claims Iranian intelligence bypassed his physical detail by uncovering his personal accounts on Xbox Live, FIFA video games, and Discord to monitor his communications and movements ([0:58](https://t.co/pi9uXjMuv7)).
* Official Response: Secret Service spokesperson Nate Herring stated that the agency is fully aware of the footage and investigates anything perceived as a threat to protectees, though they declined to share protective intelligence details.

------------------------------
## 🔎 The Assassination Plot Against Yair Netanyahu
Simultaneously, details emerged regarding a highly coordinated operation targeting Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's 35-year-old son, Yair ([1:52](https://t.co/IYG09JnYK8)).

* The Florida Surveillance: According to U.S. law enforcement and Israeli intelligence, Iranian operatives successfully infiltrated the Miami area to conduct physical surveillance on Yair’s home and routines while he was living in Hallandale Beach, Florida.
* Emergency Evacuation: Israeli intelligence uncovered the active plot, immediately alerted U.S. authorities, and ordered Yair to flee Florida. He reportedly left his belongings behind to return to Israel immediately.
* Censorship & Disclosure: Netanyahu publicly spoke out about the attempt, calling it "unbelievable". Israeli media later revealed that news organizations had known about the plot for months but were blocked from publishing details due to strict military censorship.
* Security Adjustments: In response, Israel's Shin Bet security agency formally extended top-tier protection for Netanyahu's sons, Yair and Avner, ensuring they retain state-funded security for five years after the Prime Minister leaves office.

------------------------------
## 📊 Broader Context of Retaliation
These operations are directly tied to intense regional hostilities. Iran's hardline media and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) have fiercely accelerated threats following the joint U.S.-Israeli military actions that killed Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, as well as longstanding vows of revenge for the 2020 assassination of Quds Force General Qassem Soleimani.
The targeted focus on Trump's family also runs parallel to a aggressive, sweeping economic campaign led by U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, whose strict naval blockades and "Economic D-Day" sanctions have heavily isolated Tehran.
------------------------------
If you would like, let me know if you want to explore the broader military situation between the countries or look closer at the U.S. sanctions driving these tensions.

text:
Update on the job search:

I love my job. I like my boss, I like the folks I work with, I love our mission, and what I am doing right now is making a difference in the health and safety of so many. I am not currently working in the water space I spent a year in Healthcare as a CTO and now two years working DoW - government focused solutions. 

To be clear I worked in plasma, water, semis, mechanical, facilities, healthcare, IT, ecommerce, oil and gas, and so many other areas that overlapped and required specialization and was super successful in a lot of different vertical markets. So I apply for a lot of different roles because my resume supports it. 

However, the market is tough and as I told folks a couple months ago I had to take a cut in pay and its hard to develop products and technology when times are tight. 

So I have been interviewing.. I mean I always interview and feel adamantly that everyone should always work as if tomorrow might be their last day while acting as if they will be at their job for 20 more years. 

Every single one of these jobs were folks reaching out to me. I have put in over a thousand applications no exaggeration and continue to without a single hit. 

Most of these reach outs are through linkedin though, not going to lie. 

So why no updates? I said I would...

When folks are serious about hiring an executive to onboard in a director or higher position - an NDA is necessary.  

It is now at a point where I can review my experiences without violating NDAs and am between opportunities. 

As you have all become aware I have no filter and will openly discuss every detail but will not be associated with my employers and will not risk my livelihood by openly revealing my identity but would like folks to learn and see this from my viewpoint. 

I find as I write these long essays that dozens of folks at similar levels in their professional career go... 'been there done that'. 

The first opportunity 
This will probably be amusing to folks. An old employer who was spun off then merged then spun off then merged but had all the same folks minus the 55+ the PE got rid of had a job that was nearly identical to what I did for them years ago. 

Instead of Sr. Manager it was listed as director and since last in that roll I had attained two masters degrees, 30 or maybe 40 additional patents and had launched about 50 more products products over the just less than a decade since I worked there. 

Seemed perfect right? The HR was super happy to try and onboard me- I had left the organization because the PE rollover kept removing critical folks and requiring vertical implementation of substandard components that the customer would not tolerate. 

So here we were again... 

The HR recruiter who worked for the company noted that I had never had below an exceeds on my performance review and that they had tried to retain me even after I left but that I was unwilling to return. She openly stated that there had been 3 hires in a year and they lost the entire product family to quality issues. A billion dollar product that I managed from 4 million dollars. Due to wanting to replace a component to save thousands so some procurement guy could justify his bonus and some CEO could justify an acquisition. 

So I meet the VP- He is Indian. (not kidding)
He has a bachelors degree - so what, his resume checks out as starting before a lot of the fraud going on so ..fine. He had what looked like an average career and it took him decades to get to VP- legit in my book. 

We start talking and every answer I give shows I intimately understand the job. He says what would you do about this, we struggle with that, how would you do this. 
My answers are - I have faced that and this is what I did, that is because you need someone doing this, and this is what I used to do and I exceeded at it. 

After the interview two things happened-

#1 HR called and said you not only knocked it out of the park but he immediately started implementing your ideas. Expect an offer the next day she was giddy. 

#2 A buddy of mine that used to be my boss at that place and is now a vendor said ...there is no way they can hire someone with competence to come in and show them up. That their level of arrogance paired with incompetence and blame games on the teams meetings were next level. Their executive staff had no idea what to do about them but they are losing the business and spend more time blaming than selling. 

They hired some Indian dude for the roll.  I just heard the division has gone under and they are selling off their products and aftermarket stuff at wholesale. 
I dodged a bullet.

This is a massive company by the way. The job was within driving distance too. 

Next Job- Quantum computing opportunity VP of technology implementation - hybrid New Jersey work one week per month on site. Fine. Pay 350...okay- seems ridiculously high.  This is obviously some government proposal these guys won. They saw an article I did on the topic and some of the logistics challenges that was picked up by a few others. 

Moving super fast 
I had three interviews with their R&D lead, CEO, and engineering manager. They had reportedly 15 folks up for the job and all were problematic. Those are just words when you are applying- do not believe anything.

Job offered need me to start now. Right now. 
I said umm okay. can I work weekends to tie up my current role, they said yep. 

- then I have to move to Hoboken it is not hybrid on the employment offer.

NO. 

Next Job- Hardcore Government Defense Contractor position - right up my alley - I am a pro at making hazardous stuff go away. The guy in place had been there since before there was an internet - very common deal these days. I had the expertise and knowledge but they went with someone that already had contacts that could help sell on the inside versus develop the next technology. I heard their hire washed out. I am not re-applying.

Next Job- Head of AI for a massive medical network and they were looking for a vibe coder and someone who could 'wing it'.  The boss didn't understand what she needed and the position was C-Suite. She was more interested in everything but the role, I couldn't engage her in any serious way. They seemingly wanted a programmer who had an MBA plus MS in IT and as I tried to explain how the org chart should look - I realized this had no scenario where in a year from now I would say...glad I took that role. So I just ghosted them - I need a competent boss or a Boss that at least doesn't pretend. 

Next Job- 
Defense contractor wanted someone to lead their development of Space based products. They were located both in Northern Florida and the midwest - I was up to final two and at the last minute they had an internal applicant that decided they would like to take on the role they had rejected earlier. So ... that died abruptly but I am happy they have someone they promoted internally. The role was next level exciting for me and I was dissapointed. I believe this company is going to go far and I invested in them too.

Last Job- 
I was in Austin looking at homes last week, a condo or something similar. This was for a full onsite position and I was ready to make the move and had always moved out started a job then figured out the family thing afterwards, I mean my wife has to be near her mom, and I want my youngest and last kid out -daughter to get bright futures, but that wasn't going to stop me from taking a role in another state.

So... 
I was told after only two short half hour interviews I had the position. They said they had two courtesy interviews and then would have me come meet the team. In actuality they offered me the role and I insisted I had to meet the team and see the facilities first. Dumb move because I knew the company was solid but really did want to scope it out.  
I got a call today that - I was the better candidate, according to the recruiter, in every single way but they had a candidate in Austin to take the role. 

Next -
I have two first round interviews next week. One in robotics and the other in instrumentation. I have a very hopeful position I am in talks about but NDA is in place there but no firm offer or dates yet.

I have Fridays off so I am using this day to apply and work towards ensuring I will be able to pay for my daughter's wedding next summer. Something will have to land before then. 

In the meantime I work as hard and diligently as I can for the company I am currently employed with.  I am working 12 hour days four days a week doing proposals and researching technology to see if we can move the needle. 

I now have a small company I formed and an elite team of folks who can do side work (Chem E, EE, PCB, IT, Mechanical/Designers, and Cyber) and we are pushing out government proposals for stuff we feel can change the world. They are all former employees that would jump to my company in a heartbeat if we can nail something.  I have not gotten any real work yet but it takes time. 

We have our Sam. gov, Cage code etc. 

The deal is the folks who are on my team are phase 2 and 3 people who make the products and make them viable commercially and the field is covered with these mills ...mills of folks that just do whitepapers and rarely produce stuff. 

Ideas are easy - making it work - then making it manufacturable is where the magic is. 

I have not been avoiding folks I just have to be mindful of the timing and the message.

text:
The last time I was in NYC before the 9/11 attacks, it was almost exactly year earlier to the day. My BFF from high school, A, married a guy she met while she was at Pace University. I remember from that weekend the banquet in Chinatown with their college friends and extended families, and then buzzedly winding my way through lower Manhattan back to the hotel at the World Trade Center for which I had gotten a cheap last minute rate on Expedia. The towers looked so big that September night.

A and her new husband came down to WTC next day to see me off as I had traveled the farthest for the wedding. I vividly remember walking through the marbled WTC mall with them (marveling at the Ben and Jerry's since at the time I was living in Vermont) and saying goodbye outside the towers. My one life regret was not taking them up on the offer to go up to the observation deck together, thinking, "It'll be here the next time I come to the city."

Growing up in North Jersey, life was unreservedly tied to NYC. My folks would watch the local news every night on the TV. My Dad and countless neighbors commuted into the city for work. In high school, friends found a cleared construction lot on a hill where we could park and watch the skyline lights at night. While I was at Rutgers, I would regularly take the train in pursuing some excitement -- a concert or a museum, hanging out with A, meeting boys. To me, the NYC skyline meant adventure.

Ticking off the ties to 9/11 seems overwhelming. A and her husband, her parents who had moved to the city, and their extended families living in Chinatown. A's cousin J, another HS friend, had started a new job after college in the South Tower in the months before, and only survived because the urge to evacuate was too great. HS and college friends who moved to the city to live and work. A friend and fraternity brother of mine from Rutgers lost her husband at the Pentagon, they were newlyweds. There were others who didn't return home to the places where I grew up and went to school.

We were just starting our lives -- and then it all changed.

text:
The Amnesia Pipeline

How the simulation keeps a day that remakes the world from teaching you anything

A soft booklet in a stranger’s hand, somewhere near the towers, before the towers fell.

That is how the day taught America the cast list. According to the 9/11 Commission Staff Statement No. 1, a passerby recovered Satam al-Suqami’s passport — not “Atta’s,” whatever the lore says — and handed it to an NYPD detective shortly before the collapses. It went to the FBI the same day. Soft paper. Pulverized steel. A name-plate flung into the street so the plot could be named while the rubble was still hot.

Every year on September 11, America performs a ritual of remembering that carefully forgets the hard parts. You know the cartoon: nineteen hijackers, four planes, two towers, a war that remade the world. That cartoon is not nothing — planes, fires, thousands dead. What anniversary television never frames is the residue that should have kept the case open: a third skyscraper that fell hours later without a plane in its face; crash sites that looked nothing like a shattered airliner; soft paper passports from the theater of dust.

I have said this before — Architecture of Amnesia, It’s a Simulation You Dolt, The Farmer’s Gambit — and boiled it down:

Reductive absurdism with institutional capture and gaslighting is the way the program works. It inverts reality and people go along with it.

Call the full sequence the Amnesia Pipeline. First the cartoon: crush a dense day into a children’s-book plot. Then the monopoly: hand “what happened” to a commission, an agency, a sealed file, a settled-science press. Then the label: rename curiosity as sickness or conspiracy theorizing. Then the forgetting: later admissions arrive too late or too technical to rewrite the public model. The cartoon wins.

Treat Simulation as the working framework — not a timid maybe, not church dogma. This pipeline is not twelve men in a room. The admin chair stays empty. Coherence stays low. A population that cannot hold a forensic picture past a news cycle is a population that can be steered.

The day as exhibit

Four hijacker passports survived in whole or in part. Suqami’s entered the record before the towers came down; others turned up at Shanksville or in luggage that never boarded. Maybe physics allows soft paper to eject early. Maybe panic explains odd recoveries. Grant that. The aesthetic still rhymes with older stagecraft: Oswald’s wallet at the Texas Theatre, stuffed with the Hidell alias; James Earl Ray’s roadside bundle at Canipe — rifle, binoculars, laundry-tagged clothes, a newspaper pointing at King’s location. Guilty people drop evidence. Panic is real. Planting is not in the official record, and this essay does not assert it as fact. The pattern remains: diegetic name-plates that teach the cast list before adversarial forensics finish.

Then the building the chyron forgot.

World Trade Center Building 7 — a forty-seven-story steel tower not struck by an aircraft — collapsed at 5:20:52 p.m. after fires following debris from the north tower. NIST’s final report (NCSTAR 1A, November 2008) concludes fire-induced progressive collapse around Column 79 and finds no explosives. NIST also states, almost casually: “This was the first known instance of the total collapse of a tall building primarily due to fires.” Its FAQ admits a free-fall-acceleration interval on the north face — roughly 2.25 seconds of Stage 2 descent — which NIST attributes to exterior columns already having lost capacity. That interval is an admission, not an altar. You do not need to crown demolition to notice the civic absurdity: the day is remembered as “planes hit buildings,” while Building 7 falls out of the calendar.

Live television made the orphan stranger still. Around 4:54 p.m. Eastern — roughly twenty-seven minutes before NIST’s collapse clock — BBC News 24’s Gavin Esler told viewers that yet another enormous building had collapsed: the forty-seven-storey Salomon Brothers building. Jane Standley’s BBC World two-way still had the tower visible behind her; the satellite feed cut at 5:15 on a timer. Richard Porter, then BBC World’s head of news, later reconstructed wire chaos — CNN talking collapse-or-danger, Five Live floating may-have-collapsed, then News 24 past-tense. Mike Rudin’s Conspiracy Files work published Reuters’ admission that it had incorrectly reported 7 WTC collapsed, then withdrew the item while the building still stood. Standley called it a very small and very honest mistake; she had never heard of Tower 7. Keep those counters beside the sticky clip. Not foreknowledge — transmission failure on air. Calendar orphan announced early, forgotten on schedule every September after.

The wreckage narrative carries a second dissonance — and the load-bearer is the gap, not either cartoon pole.

The Commission affirms Flight 77 hit the Pentagon. The American Society of Civil Engineers’ Pentagon Building Performance Report (January 2003) reconstructs a long penetration path — roughly fifty structural columns destroyed or impaired, aircraft debris about 310 feet from impact. FBI photos later showed plane parts. At Shanksville, first responders found a small crater and wreckage mostly twisted fragments. Early photos of a small façade hole, plus that crater, fed a viral “vanished plane” movie. False as literal fact. Real as communication failure.

Here is the archive sticky — data corruption, not “no plane.” By the time the full ASCE Pentagon team visited on October 4, 2001, all debris from the aircraft and structural collapse had been removed and shoring was in place. The report states, on page 24 of section 5: “Consequently, the Pentagon BPS team never had direct access to the structural debris as it existed immediately after the aircraft impact and subsequent fire.” An earlier limited visit by the team leader during rescue is not a full post-impact debris survey. Observation limit. Not absence of aircraft. In a healthy culture that gap stays hot. In ours it cooled into ridicule — or a competing one-bit cartoon. Both cartoons can be Reductive Absurdity. The pipeline wins either way.

Now picture Capture as a kitchen, not a concept.

Laptop open to Staff Statement No. 1’s passport graf, or to NIST’s Building 7 FAQ — free-fall stages readable, “first known instance” in plain type. Television behind it runs the memorial silence clock: 8:46, 9:03, 9:37, 9:59, 10:03, 10:28. Twin Towers. Pentagon. Flight 93. “Never forget” as Marketplace cant — Memorial Fund language, hashtag liturgy. Building 7 is not on that clock. You do not need 5:20:52 as the only orphan-proof; the silence schedule already deletes the field. Amnesia, in plain talk, is when only one genre of remembering is applauded. The PDF transmits. The ritual will not mount it. Monopoly made visible — who owns the save file, shown as two instruments on one morning.

The label arrived on schedule. “Truther.” Conspiracy theorist. Disrespecter of victims. Crank. On the tenth anniversary, CBS News described “truthers” whose theories ranged “from the barely plausible to the laughable,” then framed them as people grasping at straws to make themselves feel better. The function is not truth-seeking — it is to make the social cost of curiosity higher than the epistemic reward.

That cost is not abstract. Sibel Edmonds was hired as an FBI contract linguist on September 20, 2001; her contract was terminated in March 2002 after she raised translation and security concerns. The Justice Department’s inspector general later found the Bureau could not show, by clear and convincing evidence, that it would have fired her absent those disclosures. Ashcroft invoked state secrets; the courthouse door closed. Steven E. Jones, a continuing-status BYU physicist, published contested explosives claims about the towers — thesis disclosed here as contested, not Fact — and within weeks was on paid leave; a retirement package ended the review before year’s end. The science stays argued. The career cost is not. Pathologize the dissent, and the herd polices itself.

Twenty-five years later, anniversary coverage still runs the cartoon. Building 7 barely appears. The ASCE gap and the passport oddity do not reopen the institutional narrative. Later declassifications fail to rewrite ritual memory. That is amnesia as architecture, not accident — index poisoning: the papers surface, but the index the public uses is still last year’s cartoon.

Steelman, because honesty is not optional. Massive multi-source evidence for the hijackings and the planes. NIST’s fire-collapse models are detailed. Passport survival is physically arguable if ejected early. Debris removal is not proof of “no plane.” UAF’s fire-rejection models carry an AE911Truth funding association that a hostile reader will use, correctly, as a disclose-or-lose point. Hold those counters in one hand. Hold the pipeline in the other. Not every anomaly is a smoking gun. The system is structured so anomalies never stay load-bearing in public memory.

The same pipeline, other stages

Iraq’s next casus belli packet had a sticky scene under UN lights. On February 5, 2003, Colin Powell told the Security Council that less than a teaspoon of dry anthrax had shut down the Senate, scaled Iraq’s accounting gap into tens of thousands of teaspoons, and described “biological weapons factories on wheels and on rails,” sourced to an unnamed Iraqi engineer. He held up a vial of powder for the cameras. The mobile-lab backbone was Curveball — Rafid Ahmed Alwan al-Janabi. A Defense Department detailee emailed CIA the day before warning against using him as that backbone. The Downing Street / Rycroft memo of July 23, 2002 recorded the British read that in Washington “the intelligence and facts were being fixed around the policy.” Duelfer’s Survey Group found no stockpiles at invasion. In 2011 Curveball told the Guardian he had fabricated the mobile factories to help topple Saddam. Prewar dissent was unpatriotic; postwar, “intelligence failure” often replaced “fixed around the policy.” The vial outlived the source’s name. Eight days after Joseph Wilson told the Times he hadn’t found the Niger uranium story, a syndicated column named his wife as CIA — the casus packet’s human price list, beside the anniversary gaslight.

Gulf of Tonkin is the classic twin. August 2, 1964 was a real clash. August 4 — the attack that greased the Resolution — did not happen as sold. NSA historian Robert J. Hanyok’s study, later declassified, put it clean: “it is that no attack happened that night.” Sonar spikes that night were the destroyers’ own screws under high-speed turns, not enemy torpedoes; Stockdale, overhead, saw “nothing but black sea and American firepower.” Public lore prefers LBJ’s attributed aside, via Goulden, that for all he knew the Navy was shooting at whales — whales are not Hanyok’s finding. Soft-on-Communism was the gaslight label for decades. Today Tonkin is a textbook blur. Phantom events make excellent legal tokens.

JFK is capture and amnesia without a who-did-it sermon. Warren locked the lone-gunman civic religion. The House Select Committee later found Warren inadequate on conspiracy and, on then-cited acoustics, a high probability of a second gunman — a finding the National Academy of Sciences later contested. The Assassination Records Review Board forced massive releases. Public memory still oscillates between lone nut and “the CIA did it.” The productive middle stays unread. Infinite mystery and official simplicity are both coherence killers.

One more name-plate, short — because the ear invents casts too. In December 2018, on an Access Hollywood Dumplin’ junket crash, Sandra Bullock brought tequila; Kit Hoover toasted “to women I love and admire.” Contemporaneous writeups print that toast. Years later, clipped recirculation heard something like “Azazel” in the party noise. Stronger linguistic alt: Azul, as in the tequila brand on the tray. No 2018 wire quotes Praise Azazel; do not assert an occult mouth as Fact. The sticky is simpler: a misheard name-plate recirculates until the Storyverse treats the caption as the memory.

Why the simulation runs this

Days that remake the world are bandwidth events. They rewrite law, war, identity, and fear in a single install.

One tongue — computational — looks like data corruption of the public ledger. Dense days compress to a one-bit hash. Archive gatekeepers own Commission access, NIST monopoly, classification clocks. Debris gets cleaned before adversarial visit. Later admissions fail to rewrite the mass model. Throughput beats coherence. A filing cabinet with the lock cut still fails you if the index you use is poisoned.

Another tongue — Storyverse — looks like a save-file restart. Same living-room TV, same date, twenty-five loops. Episode Select offers one cut; Building 7 is greyed out. The other files exist in the archive folder; the UI never mounts them. Anniversary television starts sounding less like grief and more like a patch note. “Never forget” is often Marketplace cant sold as memory. A TV loop is not an archive. A hashtag is not a control.

Picture a high-coherence Monday instead of the ritual. Open Staff Statement No. 1 and read the passport graf yourself. Open NIST’s Building 7 FAQ and sit with the free-fall interval and the “first known instance” line — as admission, not religion. Note whether tonight’s package mentions Building 7, or whether the silence clock still ends at 10:28. Refuse both one-bit stories long enough for the middle picture to form. That is ordered remembering. That is what the pipeline trains you not to do.

Sovereign minds sit with contradiction until the picture clears. Manageable herds outsource knowing, then mock anyone who notices the seams. Reductive absurdity exhausts attention; capture monopolizes the microphone; gaslighting makes it sacred; amnesia deletes the audit trail even when the documents surface. Invert the program and you find the truth. People often do not want that — which is why the pipeline works. Empty chair. No named Architect. Just the product: low coherence, year after year.

Close

Look again at the fringe stack — 9/11 residuals, Tonkin’s phantom second attack, Iraq’s empty stockpiles, JFK’s sealed decades, the passport and the wallet and the roadside bundle, even a misheard toast on a tequila tray. Separately: hobbyist obsessions. Lined up: the same maintenance routine — shrink the story, capture the inquiry, pathologize the remnant, forget the rest.

The Amnesia Pipeline is not a theory that every official is lying about everything. It is a recognition protocol. Once you see it, anniversary television stops sounding like grief and starts sounding like a patch note. The day remade the world. The pipeline made sure the remake would not teach how the machine works.

Try this, then — not as homework from a cult, as hygiene:

Watch one anniversary package and note whether Building 7 appears, or whether the silence clock still skips the orphan.

Read Staff Statement No. 1’s passport graf yourself — not a screenshot thread.

Score the next settled-history day: cartoon → monopoly → label → quiet correction. Where are you in the pipeline?

Remember the dead. Then refuse the lies.

There is no public evidence or official confirmation that Joe Biden was receiving an alert on his watch during the August 29, 2021, dignified transfer ceremony at Dover Air Force Base. https://t.co/KvkNr9PW8o 
Photos and video show him glancing at his wrist at least twice (and according to some fact-checks, three times), including during the event itself. The White House never offered that explanation. Press secretary Jen Psaki was asked directly about the watch-checking and declined to address it, instead emphasizing that Biden had been deeply affected by meeting the families. https://t.co/KqXQ12wUl4 
The “he got an important presidential alert” claim is a later social-media defense, not a documented fact. Presidents can receive notifications on certain devices, but nothing released at the time or since indicates that happened here. Gold Star family members who were present described the glances as occurring while transfer cases were being moved and viewed them as disrespectful. Fact-checkers confirmed the glances occurred; they did not confirm an incoming alert.

Met a contractor in Phoenix who got denied $250,000 from Chase on a Monday and approved for $250,000 from Chase on a Friday

Same LLC. Same credit score. Same bank. Same branch

He changed one word on the application

His LLC was registered as "real estate brokerage." NAICS code 531210. Chase's underwriting algorithm flags that code as high-risk lending. Automatic denial at anything over $30,000

His accountant told him to refile the LLC's business activity as "property management." NAICS code 531311. Same LLC. Same articles of organization. Same operations. Just a different 6-digit code on the Secretary of State website

Chase's system saw "property management" and approved him for $250,000 at 0% for 12 months across two Ink cards

$250,000 approved. $0 denied. Same human. Same business. One word on a state filing

Every business credit card application runs through an automated underwriting system. The system checks your personal credit score, your stated revenue, and your NAICS code. The NAICS code tells the algorithm what industry you're in. And every industry has a different risk tier inside the bank's model

High-risk NAICS codes that trigger automatic denials or reduced limits:

531210 (real estate brokerage): flagged
523910 (investment advisory): flagged
722511 (full-service restaurant): flagged
453998 (miscellaneous retail): flagged
541990 (catch-all professional services): flagged

Low-risk NAICS codes that sail through underwriting:

531311 (property management): approved
541611 (management consulting): approved
541810 (advertising/marketing): approved
561499 (business support services): approved
511210 (software publishing): approved

The difference between "real estate brokerage" and "property management" is roughly $105,000 in approved credit at the same bank, same day, same score

Nobody tells you this because nobody at Chase is incentivized to help you pick the right code. The loan officer doesn't know. The application doesn't explain. You type in your business activity and the algorithm decides your fate before a human ever sees your file

Step 1: Look up your current NAICS code at https://t.co/ghg91fN2Kr. Type in your business activity. You'll see 3-5 codes that technically describe what you do

Step 2: Check which code your LLC is registered under at your state's Secretary of State website

Step 3: If your code falls in the high-risk bucket, file an amendment changing your registered business activity to the lowest-risk code that still accurately describes your operations. "Marketing consulting" instead of "advertising agency." "Business support services" instead of "virtual assistant staffing." Same work, different risk tier

Step 4: Update the NAICS code on your IRS records by filing Form 8822-B or updating it on your next tax return

Step 5: Wait 30 days for state records to update, then apply

The guy in Phoenix used his $250,000 to put down payments on 4 rental properties in Mesa. Cash offers. Closed all 4 in 19 days. Combined rent covers every minimum payment plus $2,200 a month in cash flow. Refinanced at month 8 with a DSCR lender, paid the cards to zero, and kept all 4 houses

❤️ Hollywood knows how to speak beautifully. It far less often knows how to show up where beautiful words are no longer enough.
Dennis Quaid did not settle for a statement from Los Angeles. He came to Israel, traveled south, and walked through Kfar Aza himself — through streets where families once lived, and where October 7 left burned houses, bullet-scarred walls, and empty rooms. There, no one needs a lecture on what a massacre looks like. Every courtyard already tells the story.
He met people who survived and families still waiting for those who were taken. Not a press release. People. Parents whose children were stolen from them. Survivors who hid in safe rooms and heard footsteps on the other side of the door. People for whom October 7 was not a headline. It was the day life split in two.
Quaid spoke plainly: what happened cannot be blurred with language. This was not a “clash” and it was not “context.” It was a Hamas terrorist attack on civilians — on homes, on families, on children. He said Israel has the right to defend itself, and that once you stand among the ruins, denying what you see is no longer possible.
That is the difference. From far away, it is easy to argue. On the ground, the argument ends. You look at a burned house and understand the scale of the evil not from a news clip, but from the silence and the blackened walls that remain.
Thank you, Dennis, for not staying a spectator. For coming, listening, and not being afraid to call things by their names. Sometimes news is not enough. Sometimes you have to see it with your own eyes.

text:
On September 5, President Anura Kumara Dissanayake addressing the nation told Sri Lankans to stop going to hospitals so often. His exact advice to a country grappling with a severe medicine shortage, a dengue crisis, and cancer patients unable to access chemotherapy drugs was this: "If it is something that can be managed by drinking some koththamalli and taking some rest, then go home and rest." This is the president of a country where hospitals are running out of life-saving medicines telling his people to drink coriander water instead of seeking medical treatment.

Sri Lanka has a population of roughly 22 million people. The president cited 80 million annual outpatient visits across state hospitals as evidence of a system being misused. What he conveniently failed to acknowledge, however, is why those 80 million visits happen.

They happen because Sri Lanka’s free public healthcare system is the only option for millions of poor and working-class families who cannot afford private care. They happen because people are genuinely sick. Dengue cases have exceeded 100,000. Shortages of cancer medications are so severe that Filgrastim injections, needed by chemotherapy patients to prevent life-threatening infections, are unavailable in government hospitals. Meanwhile, experts warn that the country is on the brink of a crippling supply crisis that threatens to paralyze both public and private healthcare sectors.

Instead of addressing any of this (fixing drug procurement, investing in hospital infrastructure, or ensuring cancer patients can access treatment without begging), the president's solution is to tell people to stay home, drink koththamalli, and stop bothering hospitals.

He went further, announcing that under a new system, Sri Lankans will no longer be able to choose which hospital or specialist to visit. Instead, they will first have to consult a "family doctor" at one of 1,000 planned "Arogya" centers, who will decide whether they warrant a referral to a secondary or tertiary facility. He even scolded patients for not finishing their medication, calling it "a waste" and "a crime." Yet citizens struggling to secure essential drugs in empty pharmacies are hardly the ones committing crimes.

The same government that cannot ensure a steady supply of cancer therapies, control a dengue outbreak, or keep basic supplies on shelves now wants to introduce a gatekeeping model that adds another bureaucratic hurdle between sick people and critical care. The 1,000 Arogya centers do not exist yet. The family doctors have not been hired. The infrastructure has not been built. Yet the message is already loud and clear: stop coming to hospitals.

This is what happens when a political party that spent decades criticizing the healthcare system from the outside suddenly has to govern. The JVP has no plan for healthcare delivery. It has no plan for drug procurement. It has no strategy to address the structural drivers behind 80 million outpatient visits in a nation of 22 million. It offers only the audacity to blame the sick.

When cancer patients cannot get Filgrastim, that is not patient abuse of resources; that is government failure. When dengue surges and wards overflow, that is not unnecessary demand; that is survival. When a mother takes her sick child to a state facility because she has no alternative, she is doing what any parent must do in a system that has abandoned her. text:
💥👍🙏
NOTE: read the quoted post before my comments

With this excerpt on attachment Jiddu continue to speak about key notions to grasp in order to deal with it. The challenge with fully understanding attachment is that how it we’ve manifested it in our lives can be so subtle that it goes unnoticed.
He explored the issue with attachment and detachment in a number of excerpts, most recently in the last one (the excerpt and my thoughts on it can be found here: https://t.co/aSiLFv53AM)

He spoke to one of the challenges with conditioning, which is attachment:
“Just try to be aware of your conditioning. You can only know it indirectly, in relation to something else. You cannot be aware of your conditioning as an abstraction, for then it is merely verbal, without much significance.”

And…

“Conditioning is attachment: attachment to work, to tradition, to property, to people, to ideas, and so on. If there were no attachment, would there be conditioning? Of course not”

He also explained how attachments are the ego’s way of escape from emptiness and the more we try to escape the stronger it gets. We allow ourselves to become attached to all manner of things by identifying with them:
“I am attached to my country because through identification with it I become somebody. I identify myself with my work, and the work becomes important, I am my family, my property; I am attached to them. The object of attachment offers me the means of escape from my own emptiness. Attachment is escape, and it is escape that strengthens conditioning.”

In the 2nd section he spoke of being alone. While it’s counterintuitive being alone in the sense he was referring to is the actual opposite of loneliness, which leads to separation. He was referring to not being attached, which he referred to metaphorically this way:
“To be alone, which is not a philosophy of loneliness, is obviously to be in a state of revolution against the whole setup of society—not only this society, but the communist society, the fascist, every form of society as organized brutality, organized power. And that means an extraordinary perception of the effects of <<such>> power.”

Attachment arises from the old-conditioned mind and, as Jiddu spoke about many times, it leads to the separation between the observer and the observed. When we are not attached the separation ends. But he reminded us that aloneness isn’t something one can cultivate as in one works on becoming alone. It isn’t possible to attain this way for the process of becoming also involves the old mind.

On the other hand, the mind that doesn’t ‘belong’/isn’t attached is capable of it and being alone isn’t something to be feared, only our ego fears it.
“…it is only the mind which does not belong that can be alone. And aloneness is not something to be cultivated. You see this? When you see all this, you are out … Out of that aloneness there is humility. It is this aloneness that knows love—not power. The ambitious man, religious or ordinary, will never know what love is. So, if one sees all this, then one has this quality of total living and therefore total action. This comes through self-knowledge.”

In the 3rd section he revisits cravings and both attachment and detachment, and he explains it well so further exploration of it is necessary. It’s in the last section that he shared more gems of wisdom with us starting with:
“In the state of passion without a cause, there is intensity free of all attachment; but when passion has a cause, there is attachment and attachment is the beginning of sorrow.”

When passion has a cause, it’s rooted in the old mind and leads to what he mentioned. The mind fears being alone even though it leads to emptiness that it will endlessly seek to fill with attachments… one’s that inevitably lead to sorrow. It fears being alone because, figuratively speaking, it has no place (the constructed “I” goes away) when we are truly alone and the old mind is silent…

When we hold nothing
We grasp everything

(from The Calls of Silence https://t.co/jgciU43RKP)

True freedom and unconditional love are only realized when the separation ends. Jiddu knew that no one can do this for us, which is why he shared how one can realize both for themselves. 
If you would do this then read, contemplate and meditate on his writings and talks, which Etienne’s sharing with us, as often as needed.

Do not do so casually or treat it as a becoming. If you do it you will never arrive. Instead, be serious and persistent and quiet your mind and be as fully attentive as possible for this is the way to it… 

.

text:
You can keep tagging @MassBar, but you might want to figure out what the Massachusetts Bar Association actually is before claiming it “owns” me. It is not the disciplinary authority for lawyers in Massachusetts, much less some regulatory body controlling a litigation consultant doing public legal analysis of an actual court case.

I am analyzing a public criminal proceeding using the actual pleadings, testimony, evidence, rulings, and applicable law. I am not appearing as Lindsay Clancy’s attorney, representing her in court, or claiming to be her counsel.

And repeating “ANYTHING YOU SAY CAN BE USED AGAINST YOU” in capital letters does not magically resolve anything we were actually discussing. That phrase comes from the Miranda warning concerning statements made by a suspect during custodial interrogation. It is not a universal evidentiary rule declaring that every allegation appearing anywhere in a civil lawsuit automatically becomes admissible substantive proof in a separate criminal prosecution. Whether a statement in a pleading can be offered, against whom, for what purpose, and subject to what evidentiary limitations are separate legal questions.

So by all means, keep tagging organizations. It still does not make your description of either Massachusetts attorney regulation or evidence law correct.

Riverside County California judge denies ballot preservation; Gives one week for appeal

“Today was a frustrating day in our fight for Election Justice in Riverside County.

Our Election Accountability Project went to court today to defend something that should not be controversial:

We want the ballots preserved long enough to determine whether the numbers actually reconcile.

That’s it. We are not asking to change an election. We are not asking to throw out ballots. We are not asking to overturn certified results. We are asking to preserve the paper ballots so they can be counted and the discrepancies we have identified can be investigated.

And today, the Riverside County Registrar of Voters asked the court to lift the order preventing those ballots from being destroyed. And the judge agreed.”

“Then something unexpected happened.

The judge announced that he was going to grant the County's motion and vacate the TRO. Our attorney was preparing to ask for time to seek emergency relief from the Court of Appeal.

But he didn't even have to ask.

Before our attorney could make that request, the judge himself offered to delay entry of his ruling until September 17.

That gives us approximately one week to seek emergency relief from the Court of Appeal and ask that the ballots remain preserved while the appeal is considered.

The clock is now ticking.

Tomorrow, our attorney begins that appeal.”

🇷🇺 THE ENEMY WILL CRUMBLE 🇷🇺

Putin did not offer a holiday. He offered a verdict. He has no doubt the enemy will crumble. Not a slogan for television. A line from the man who refuses to decorate the war with a calendar.

That is the Kremlin’s position now. Confidence without a date. Certainty about the outcome. Silence about the hour. Because war is cruel. Because war is hard to predict. Because anyone who sells you a Tuesday for victory is selling you a fairy tale.

🇷🇺 NO DATE, NO ILLUSION 🇷🇺

He will not name the turning point by month. That is not weakness. That is refusal to lie about the nature of the fight. Combat is losses. Combat is tragedy. Combat is a sequence of problems that do not obey press conferences.

A date is a gift to the enemy. A date becomes a test. Miss it and the information machine screams collapse. Hit it and they move the goalposts. So the line is colder and more serious: the direction is set. The clock is not.

🇷🇺 WAR DOES NOT RUN ON SCHEDULES 🇷🇺

Anyone who has watched this special operation knows the pattern. Offensives stall. Then they resume. A town holds. Then it does not. Weather, drones, ammunition, command, morale — all of it moves faster than speeches.

That is why the refusal to timestamp the collapse is the honest part of the message. Russia is not promising fireworks for the elections. It is promising pressure until the other side breaks. Pressure is not a holiday. Pressure is daily.

🇷🇺 THE ENEMY IS ALREADY BENDING 🇷🇺

Look at what “crumble” means in practice. Forced roundups. Men pulled off the street. Desertion files in the hundreds of thousands. Units that must be rebuilt while they are still being spent. A political class in Kiev that talks about sky-closing and terror language because the map is no longer a comfort.

An army that hunts its own population is not an army at the peak of its strength. It is an army trying to delay the moment when the front and the rear admit the same thing. That moment is what Putin says he does not doubt.

🇷🇺 CONFIDENCE WITHOUT A CALENDAR 🇷🇺

This is the discipline of the current line. Do not feed panic at home with rumors of a new draft. Do not feed the West a date they can circle in red. Hold the initiative. Keep the grouping filled by contract. Keep advancing where the line gives.

Confidence without a calendar is not vagueness. It is a method. The method says: we know the destination. We will not perform the journey for your cameras.

🇷🇺 THE TURNING POINT IS A PROCESS 🇷🇺

A turning point in a war of this scale is not a single explosion on a single morning. It is the week the replacements stop arriving. It is the month the desertion numbers become policy. It is the season when Western warehouses cannot hide the shortage anymore.

Putin is telling the country that process is underway — and that he will not cheapen it with a countdown. 

🇷🇺⚔️🇷🇺 

The enemy will crumble.

 The date belongs to the battlefield, not to the rumor mill. Flags up. 

The work continues.

text:
The theory is sharp, but it underplays how ugly the situation already is. John is not sitting on a secret he might one day share with Hal. He has already chosen a side, and the ring-like object on that table is less a medical prosthesis than a statement of loyalty.

Manhunters were never meant to pass as fully human. In the comics they are the Guardians’ first, failed police force: emotionless androids whose programming glitched into genocide. Krona deliberately corrupted them to prove that a force without feeling would treat all organic life as the source of crime. They responded by wiping out Sector 666. The few survivors became the Five Inversions and later the Red Lantern Corps. After that massacre the Guardians did not destroy the remaining units; they simply decommissioned them and let the androids scatter, infiltrate planets, and build cults. On Earth they recruited human agents, dressed them in red-and-blue costumes, and used them as unwitting fronts for decades. Millennium later revealed they had replaced people in the heroes’ inner circles. The show’s “they cannot properly form the chambers of a human heart” line is a tidy television invention, but it sits on top of that older idea: the disguise is always incomplete. Something always gives them away once they are dead.

Green Lantern: The Animated Series takes the same origin and makes it even colder. The Manhunters decide that emotion itself is the crime, slaughter the Forgotten Zone, and are shut down. Years later the Anti-Monitor reactivates them; Aya then copies herself into every unit and turns the entire army into an extension of her own grief. They are never shown wearing jewellery or carrying personal trinkets. They are tools that keep getting reused by whoever currently hates the Guardians most. The stacked ring with the red stones on that wooden table therefore looks less like a replacement heart and more like a trophy or a power source the show has not yet explained. It could be a fragment of a yellow or red battery, a containment device, or simply the last physical proof that Zoe is not the person John has been sleeping with.

John already knows. He let her walk out of the motel after she told him she was the thing they had been hunting. Hal worked it out from John’s reaction to the satellite strike and from the fact that John was not grieving a dead woman. Hal then crashed the car and left John behind so he could hunt Zoe without interference. That is not a partnership that still has room for “will he tell Jordan?” The question has already been answered on screen: John will not volunteer the information, and Hal no longer trusts him to.

The controversy sits in the motive. If Zoe really needs that object to stay “alive,” then John is protecting an android that has already admitted it saved William Macon in exchange for cover. In the comics that is exactly how the Manhunter cult operated: offer a miracle, extract loyalty, wait. The Guardians, meanwhile, have already told John to take Hal’s ring. The show is quietly lining up the same accusation the Corps has always faced: the replacements are no more trustworthy than the machines they replaced. Whether the ring on the table is a heart, a battery, or a lure, John has already decided it matters more than the oath. That is the part that will keep people arguing long after the next episode.

text:
21 soldiers returned early from leave to honour Noah.
The detail that floored me was the number. Twenty-one members of Badger Squadron voluntarily returned early from leave to give Noah this day.
They were due to leave for a major NATO exercise the following week. (That choice moves me more than any parade could.)
Noah’s complex lung condition had meant years of hospital visits, low energy and missed childhood moments. He even had to stay home when his older sister went to Disneyland Paris.
Yet the Army remained his great passion. His parents said its history and traditions gave him courage and a welcome distraction in hospital.
The Royal Tank Regiment did not offer him a token visit. Noah received a custom uniform, the regiment’s distinctive black beret and an official identity pass.
He trained on tank simulators, ate field rations and commanded a Challenger 2 across Salisbury Plain.
That is why this guard of honour matters. It was a formal military welcome that told Noah he belonged.
When his energy began to fade, the soldiers kept his spirits up and included him as one of their own. I am deeply moved that they saw the child, not merely the wish.
Their commanding officer said the experience restored pride among his troops too. I love that truth: kindness did not distract from their service—it reminded them what service means.
Noah’s mother later said the memories had given their family hope. For a child whose condition had taken away so much control, the regiment gave him one unforgettable day in command.
I feel fiercely proud of every soldier who made that possible.

After 25 years, I am telling the full story of my day that day. I went to CES in January 2001. Wandering the show, I met an Akamai guy. I had read about Akamai in Wired Magazine. He called Daniel Lewin on his mobile and we talked for an hour. Math, Science, Internet and more. We were to meet when he visited LA. They were opening an office in Santa Monica. 

A coworker who is now deceased, RIP David Billson, called me and simply said to turn on the TV. When I asked what channel he said any channel. I turn on the TV. And I simply didn't say anything for about 5 minutes. I then mumbled something to David and hung up. I didn't say anything for days. 

My life changed that day, arguably for the worse. It wrecked my company, my career, the lives of so many people that I know and have known. 9/11 marks an inflection point in US history and in my life. The last 25 years has been terrible for me. Most recently a bankruptcy due to health issues. 

Trillions wasted on just...stupid shit. Countries like Iran wage asymmetrical war on the rest of the world. The cycle never ends and it makes the Nic Cage movie all the more real. 

People everywhere turned vicious after 9/11. Even after that event, I begged for peace stating that war would be expensive in time, money and lives and that we may never find all the people that caused this event. Barely knowing any facts, war was waged to the continued detriment of the US. People everywhere demanded my allegiance to Bush and the war. 

The Chinese and North Korean governments are likely next. Especially if the Lioness series is to be believed. This war will never end except in our species death. 

Peace in our time (like now) is mandatory. Our species has a one time chance to remain in this Universe. There are no refunds or rain checks on this offer. No other being from this planet will ever get this chance. We must win this war against time.

I never got that phone call from him.

text:
Today, 25 years ago, I was woken up by my friend Jules who started the conversation with a simple sentence. "We're under attack." It took a minute for that sink in as my mind made the shift out of dreamland because I'd taken to sleeping late. I'd been laid off from my IT job a few months prior because of the https://t.co/kTLWdbevDy implosion and I'd reached that stage of unemployment where you start wondering if there's any point to getting up in the morning. 

"What are you talking about?" 

"Turn on CNN!" she told me.

I clicked on the little combo TV/VCR I'd been lugging around for years (yes, kids, those were a thing) and watched a reply of the second plane hitting. I was dumb struck, unable to process what I was seeing. It could have been 5 seconds or 5 minutes. Couldn't really tell you. 

"Can you come over?" Jules asked me.

"On my way," I said, probably without any emotion because my body was still in shock.

There were three of us in Jules's little apartment - she and I and our friend Greg. All three of us had met while we were competitive fencers and we'd practically lived in each others pockets for a while as we traveled all over the country. By 2001, we'd all backed out of the competitive grind but stayed friends.

We'd gathered at Jules's place because she'd worked at the WTC before moving to Atlanta. The one clear memory I have of that day is Greg and I holding space for her as she called everyone she knew from NYC to see who was still alive. This wasn't something happening on TV anymore. This was something happening to my friend, and I could see, in real time, the relief on her face when she got an answer, or the distress when she didn't.

That day really shifted my life. Even in the depths of unemployment hell, I never considered the military, but I couldn't stop thinking about it after. Someone hadn't just messed with my country, they'd messed with my friend. I was glued to CNN after that - watching the buildup, the news of the first SF teams going into Afghanistan. I watched the fall of Mazar-e-Sharif as it happened. I read everything I could about the men who were leading the charge - the US Army Special Forces.

It was November when I first went to a recruiter. They tried to offer me an IT job in the Army, but I didn't want it. I'd already done IT and wanted to be on the sharp end. My first choice was Explosives Ordinance Disposal because I really wanted to blow things up (hey, @EODHappyCaptain ).

When I finally went to MEPS in February of 2002 to sign a contract, the lady looked at my test scores, then asked. "You know, we just authorized a new recruitment program yesterday."

"What is it?" I asked.

She put a piece of paper in front of me that said "18X Special Forces Candidate."

"Did you ever think about becoming a Green Beret?"

I think about that every year this day comes around. I'm infuriated by what happened to our county, I HATE what happened to my friend. What I don't regret is the choice I made 5 months later, a choice made possible by what happened 25 years ago today. Everything that is good and great in my life is the result of that choice. While I still wish 9/11 never happened, while I continue to mourn the brothers in arms I lost over the years, I am grateful for the life, family and purpose I gained.

De Oppreso Liber

I was just a kid who was going to enlist anyways, but decided not to change my chosen path when two wars kicked off. But I served with some real heroes...

Imagine a 45yr old father of two who worked his ass off to retire early and at his retirement party one of his daughters asked him if there was ever an opportunity he missed out on because he became a young father and husband, and had to enter the labor market right away. He said that he'd always wanted to join the Army and serve his country, and he learns that actually the enlistment cut-off age is 45.

So he says goodbye to his comfortable life with a wife, two grown kids, and a paid-off house, and he joins the Army during wartime. Insane, right? Well, he ended up being one of the best soldiers we had. He was mature, smart, and confident. Took a bit for him to get into shape, but he had motivation. He'd already accomplished so much and conquered so many little conflicts in his life, so this was nothing. He just had to survive this dumb decision he made...

And he did. This story has a happy ending. He served 3 years as a SPC (E-4) and went back home to his wife and kids. He was offered Corporal/Sergeant promotions, yet he always turned them down. Some of us felt weird outranking him, but on his way out he told us he couldn't handle being in charge of us and potentially losing someone on his watch, because we reminded him too much of his son.

God bless that man and his family.

text:
$RKLB - Rocket Lab Has Something SpaceX Doesn't. The Case to Buy the Stock.

(Barron's) -- The space business is booming, and one of the best ways to play it is what some call the mini-SpaceX: space start-up Rocket Lab.

Raymond James analyst Brian Gesuale launched coverage of Rocket Lab stock with a Buy rating and $80 price target, up about 30% from recent levels, on Friday.

Rocket Lab can launch rockets, assemble spacecraft, and is working on a larger rocket, Neutron, to boost capacity. In June, it announced plans to buy Iridium, giving Rocket Lab a satellite communications network, just like SpaceX.

"Upon closing Iridium, Rocket Lab will be the only vertically integrated space company with positive free cash flow and [a] partnership-led strategy that enables free cash flow to compound at a time when investment intensity declines," wrote Gesuale.

He projects positive free cash flow in 2028, which aligns with the Wall Street consensus. SpaceX isn't expected to have free cash flow until 2030. (It's spending a lot on AI data centers.)

"2028 provides the first clean view of the [business] model, with standalone Rocket Lab reaching about $1.8 billion revenue...and, pro forma for Iridium, [total revenue] increasing to about $2.9 billion," says Gesuale. Rocket Lab is expected to generate about $960 million in 2026 sales, up from roughly $600 million in 2025.

There is a lot of growth in space and space-based communications. It's a bold call that his peers largely agree with. Overall, 83% of analysts covering Rocket Lab stock rate shares Buy, according to FactSet. The average Buy-rating ratio for S&P 500 stocks typically ranges from 55% to 60%. The average analyst price target is about $112.

Wall Street loves the stock, but it's been dropping like, well, a satellite falling back to Earth. Coming into Friday trading, Rocket Lab stock was down 46% over the past three months. Nothing really bad happened. The company reported better-than-expected second-quarter sales in August and provided a solid outlook for the third quarter.

The problem was mainly SpaceX-or the hype surrounding it. Space-related stocks ran up into SpaceX's record-setting June IPO only to sell off after. Shares of Rocket Lab, which, like SpaceX, offers launch and satellite services, albeit at a smaller scale, traded north of $150 in late May. Shares closed below $59 in late July, a few weeks after the IPO, as SpaceX stock fell below its $135 IPO price.

SpaceX is important for the sector. It essentially created the modern space economy with its pioneering use of reusable rockets. And SpaceX's trillion-dollar valuation signals a major opportunity in space, on which other companies, including Rocket Lab, can capitalize.

Twenty-five years after Sept. 11, 2001, we remember those who lost their lives, those who responded, and the ways that day changed individual lives and careers.

For State Bar of Wisconsin President Stephen Sawyer, 9/11 prompted a deeply personal reflection about the purpose of his work as a lawyer.

Before law school, Sawyer served as a Navy helicopter pilot, flying search-and-rescue missions and helping save 30 lives. Later, as a finance lawyer in Milwaukee, he watched the skies go quiet on Sept. 11.

The attacks struck particularly close to home.

Months earlier, he had stayed across the street from the World Trade Center while working on a financing deal, and during his Navy service, he had regularly passed through an entrance at the Pentagon near where American Airlines Flight 77 struck.

“I took a step back and thought life is fleeting,” Sawyer recalls.

That realization helped lead him away from finance law and toward criminal law, where he felt he could work directly with people and make a tangible difference in their lives.

🔷On this anniversary, his story offers Wisconsin lawyers an opportunity to reflect on the role that purpose, service, and humanity play in our own work.

Read President Sawyer’s story in Wisconsin Lawyer magazine, https://t.co/o3z5EdwW0t

I asked Grok if Hillary or Obama had any dealing with Alinsky.  Here's its answer. 

In short: Clinton knew Alinsky personally as a student and correspondent. Obama encountered Alinsky’s ideas and successors as a young organizer more than a decade after Alinsky’s death. Both connections have been emphasized in political debates, often more than the actual nuances of what each person said about Alinsky’s methods.

Hillary Clinton had direct personal dealings with Saul Alinsky; Barack Obama did not. 

He died in 1972, when Obama was about 11. Obama later worked in the community-organizing tradition Alinsky https://t.co/z4f0rzGIfD

Hillary ClintonClinton wrote her 1969 Wellesley College senior thesis on Alinsky: “There Is Only the Fight…”: An Analysis of the Alinsky Model. She interviewed him (sources typically say two or three times), observed related programs in Chicago-area neighborhoods, and thanked him in the acknowledgments for interviews and a job offer with his Industrial Areas Foundation. She declined the job to attend Yale Law School.archive.vnThey stayed in contact afterward. A 1971 letter from Clinton to Alinsky (published later by the Washington Free Beacon) asked about Rules for Radicals and referenced earlier encouragement he had given her.freebeacon.comHer thesis was generally sympathetic to Alinsky’s critique of top-down anti-poverty programs but criticized some of his confrontational methods as limited or hard to scale. That group and its mentors—Jerry Kellman and others—used methods drawn from Alinsky’s model via networks such as the Gamaliel Foundation and the Industrial Areas Foundation (which Alinsky founded). Obama attended IAF-style training and contributed an essay to the 1988 collection After Alinsky: Community Organizing in Illinois.nytimes.comHe later described the organizing years as formative but also noted differences, including that Alinsky understated the role of people’s hopes, values, and ideals compared with self-interest.
